chapters.title: Before I Formed You
chapters.html:
Jeremiah 1

1The words of Jeremiah son of Hilkiah, one of the priests who were in Anathoth in the land of Benjamin,

2to whom the word of the LORD came in the days of Josiah son of Amon, king of Judah, in the thirteenth year of his reign.

3It came also in the days of Jehoiakim son of Josiah, king of Judah, until the end of the eleventh year of Zedekiah son of Josiah, king of Judah, until the exile of Jerusalem in the fifth month.

The Call

4The word of the LORD came to me, saying,

5"Before I formed you in the belly I knew you,
and before you came out of the womb I consecrated you;
I appointed you a prophet to the nations."

6Then I said, "Ah, Lord GOD! I do not know how to speak, for I am a youth."

7But the LORD said to me, "Do not say, 'I am a youth'; for to all to whom I send you, you shall go, and all that I command you, you shall speak.

8Do not be afraid of them, for I am with you to deliver you, declares the LORD."

9Then the LORD put out His hand and touched my mouth, and the LORD said to me, "I have put My words in your mouth.

10See, I have appointed you this day over the nations and over the kingdoms, to uproot and to pull down, to destroy and to overthrow, to build and to plant."

The Almond Branch and the Boiling Pot

11The word of the LORD came to me, saying, "What do you see, Jeremiah?" I said, "I see a branch of an almond tree."

12The LORD said to me, "You have seen well, for I am watching over My word to do it."

13The word of the LORD came to me a second time, saying, "What do you see?" I said, "I see a boiling pot, tilting from the north."

14Then the LORD said to me, "Out of the north disaster will break loose on all who live in the land.

15For I am about to call all the clans of the kingdoms of the north, declares the LORD; and they will come, and each will set his throne at the entrance of the gates of Jerusalem, against all its walls all around, and against all the cities of Judah.

16I will speak My judgments against them for all their wickedness, because they have forsaken Me, burned incense to other gods, and bowed down to the works of their own hands.

17But you, gird up your loins; arise, and speak to them all that I command you. Do not be dismayed before them, or I will dismay you before them.

18I Myself have made you today a fortified city, an iron pillar and bronze walls against the whole land: against the kings of Judah, its princes, its priests and the people of the land.

19They will fight against you, but they will not overcome you, for I am with you, declares the LORD, to deliver you."

Notes

  • v1 "one of the priests who were in Anathoth" — Anathoth was one of the towns given to the sons of Aaron the priest (Joshua 21:13, 18), and the place Solomon sent Abiathar the priest: Go to Anathoth, to your fields (1 Kings 2:26). The Greek begins The word of God which came to Jeremiah.

  • v3 "until the exile of Jerusalem in the fifth month" — the month the city fell: In the fifth month, on the seventh day of the month… Nebuzaradan… came to Jerusalem (2 Kings 25:8). The book's first verses already name its end.

  • v5 "Before I formed you in the belly I knew you" — yatsar, "formed," the potter's verb, used of the man shaped from dust (Genesis 2:7) and of the servant, who formed me from the womb (Isaiah 49:5). "Consecrated" is hiqdashtikha, "made you holy": set apart before birth. Paul says the same of himself: He who set me apart from my mother's womb and called me by His grace (Galatians 1:15).

  • vv6–8 "I do not know how to speak… I am with you" — the objection Moses made, I am not a man of words (Exodus 4:10), and the same answer: I Myself will be with your mouth (Exodus 4:12); here I am with you to deliver you, said again at the end of the chapter (v19).

  • vv7, 9 "all that I command you, you shall speak… I have put My words in your mouth" — the two halves of the promise of a prophet like Moses: I will put My words in his mouth, and he shall speak to them all that I command him (Deuteronomy 18:18). Isaiah's lips were touched with a coal (Isaiah 6:7); Jeremiah's mouth is touched by the LORD's own hand.

  • v10 "to uproot and to pull down, to destroy and to overthrow, to build and to plant" — four verbs of tearing down and two of building. They come back through the book (18:7, 9; 31:28), and the tearing down comes first.

  • vv11–12 "a branch of an almond tree… I am watching over My word" — shaqed, "almond," and shoqed, "watching," the same three letters. In 31:28 the almond's verb and the verbs of v10 meet: As I watched over them to uproot and to pull down… so I will watch over them to build and to plant.

  • v15 "each will set his throne at the entrance of the gates of Jerusalem" — at the fall, all the princes of the king of Babylon came and sat in the Middle Gate (39:3).

  • vv17–19 "Do not be dismayed before them, or I will dismay you… a fortified city… bronze walls" — al techat… pen achittekha, the same verb twice: the prophet who fears the people is given something worse to fear. The promise is made again in 15:20, I will make you to this people a fortified wall of bronze; they will fight against you, but they will not overcome you.

chapters.title: The Fountain of Living Waters
chapters.html:
Jeremiah 2

1The word of the LORD came to me, saying,

2Go and proclaim in the ears of Jerusalem: This is what the LORD says:
I remember the loyal love of your youth,
your love as a bride,
how you followed Me in the wilderness,
in a land not sown.

3Israel was holy to the LORD,
the firstfruits of His harvest;
all who ate of it were held guilty;
disaster came on them,
declares the LORD.

4Hear the word of the LORD, house of Jacob,
and all the clans of the house of Israel.

5This is what the LORD says:
What wrong did your fathers find in Me,
that they went far from Me,
and went after emptiness and became empty?

6They did not say, "Where is the LORD,
who brought us up from the land of Egypt,
who led us through the wilderness,
through a land of deserts and pits,
through a land of drought and the shadow of death,
through a land that no one passes through,
where no man lives?"

7I brought you into a fruitful land
to eat its fruit and its good things;
but you came in and defiled My land,
and made My inheritance a detestable thing.

8The priests did not say, "Where is the LORD?"
Those who handle the law did not know Me;
the shepherds rebelled against Me;
the prophets prophesied by Baal,
and went after things that do not profit.

9Therefore I will still contend with you, declares the LORD,
and with your sons' sons I will contend.

10Cross over to the coastlands of Kittim and see;
send to Kedar and consider carefully;
see whether there has ever been such a thing.

11Has a nation exchanged its gods,
though they are not gods?
But My people have exchanged their Glory
for what does not profit.

12Be appalled, heavens, at this;
shudder, be utterly desolate,
declares the LORD.

13For My people have committed two evils:
they have forsaken Me,
the fountain of living waters,
to hew out cisterns for themselves,
broken cisterns
that cannot hold water.

14Is Israel a slave?
Is he a servant born in the house?
Why then has he become plunder?

15Young lions have roared against him;
they have raised their voice;
they have made his land a desolation;
his cities are burned,
without inhabitant.

16The men of Memphis and Tahpanhes
have also broken the crown of your head.

17Have you not brought this on yourself
by forsaking the LORD your God
when He led you in the way?

18So now, what are you doing on the road to Egypt,
to drink the waters of the Shihor?
Or what are you doing on the road to Assyria,
to drink the waters of the River?

19Your own evil will discipline you,
and your faithlessness will rebuke you.
Know and see that it is evil and bitter
to forsake the LORD your God;
the fear of Me is not in you,
declares the Lord GOD of hosts.

20For long ago I broke your yoke
and tore off your bonds,
and you said, "I will not transgress";
yet on every high hill
and under every green tree
you lay down as a prostitute.

21Yet I had planted you a choice vine,
wholly of true seed;
how then have you turned against Me
into the wild shoots of a foreign vine?

22Though you wash yourself with lye
and use much soap,
the stain of your iniquity is before Me,
declares the Lord GOD.

23How can you say, "I am not defiled;
I have not gone after the Baals"?
See your way in the valley;
know what you have done:
a swift young camel
running here and there,

24a wild donkey used to the wilderness,
sniffing the wind in her desire.
In her heat who can turn her back?
None who seek her need weary themselves;
in her month they will find her.

25Keep your feet from going bare,
and your throat from thirst.
But you said, "It is hopeless!
No, for I have loved strangers,
and after them I will go."

26As a thief is put to shame when he is caught,
so the house of Israel is put to shame:
they, their kings, their princes,
their priests and their prophets,

27who say to wood, "You are my father,"
and to stone, "You gave birth to us."
For they have turned their backs to Me,
and not their faces;
but in the time of their trouble they say,
"Arise and save us!"

28But where are your gods
that you made for yourself?
Let them arise, if they can save you
in the time of your trouble;
for as many as your cities
are your gods, Judah.

29Why do you contend with Me?
You have all rebelled against Me,
declares the LORD.

30In vain I have struck your sons;
they took no correction;
your own sword has devoured your prophets
like a ravening lion.

31You of this generation, see the word of the LORD!
Have I been a wilderness to Israel,
or a land of thick darkness?
Why do My people say, "We roam free;
we will come to You no more"?

32Can a virgin forget her ornaments,
or a bride her sash?
Yet My people have forgotten Me
days without number.

33How well you direct your way
to seek love!
So you have taught your ways
even to wicked women.

34On your skirts too is found
the lifeblood of the innocent poor;
you did not find them breaking in.
Yet in spite of all these things

35you say, "I am innocent;
surely His anger has turned from me."
I am about to enter into judgment with you
for saying, "I have not sinned."

36Why do you go about so lightly,
changing your way?
You will be put to shame by Egypt
as you were put to shame by Assyria.

37From there too you will come away
with your hands on your head;
for the LORD has rejected those you trust,
and you will not prosper by them.

Notes

  • v2 "the loyal love of your youth… how you followed Me in the wilderness" — chesed, the word for the LORD's own loyal love, here said of Israel's love for Him. The wilderness years, which Numbers tells as years of complaint (The people became complainers, Numbers 11:1), are remembered here as a bride following her husband. The Greek has I remembered the mercy of your youth.

  • v3 "Israel was holy to the LORD, the firstfruits of His harvest; all who ate of it were held guilty" — ye'shamu, "became guilty," the law of holy things: No outsider shall eat a holy thing (Leviticus 22:10), and one who eats it by mistake must make it good (22:14). Israel is the LORD's portion, and the nations that devoured her answered for it.

  • v5 "went after emptiness and became empty" — hevel, the word Ecclesiastes uses for vanity and the name of Abel (Genesis 4:2). 2 Kings 17:15 says it of the northern kingdom in the same words, They went after emptiness and became empty.

  • v11 "My people have exchanged their Glory for what does not profit" — the verb and noun of Psalm 106:20, said of the golden calf: They exchanged their Glory for the image of an ox that eats grass. Paul: they exchanged the glory of the immortal God for the likeness of an image (Romans 1:23). "What does not profit" — be-lo yo'il, the things that do not profit of v8.

  • v13 "the fountain of living waters… broken cisterns" — mayim chayyim, "living water," is the law's word for fresh running water (Leviticus 14:5): water that flows by itself, set against water stored by hand in a cistern that cracks. The LORD calls Himself the fountain again in 17:13. Jesus offers the Samaritan woman living water (John 4:10).

  • v18 "the waters of the Shihor… the waters of the River" — Shichor stands beside the Nile in Isaiah 23:3, the grain of Shihor, the harvest of the Nile; the River is the Euphrates. The Greek has Gihon, the name of the river of Eden winding through all the land of Cush (Genesis 2:13).

  • v20 "Long ago I broke your yoke… 'I will not transgress'" — the Hebrew as read: shavarti, "I broke," the LORD's work at the Exodus, I broke the bars of your yoke (Leviticus 26:13), and the read form e'evor, "I will not transgress," Israel's promise. The written form is e'evod, "I will not serve," and the Greek has you broke your yoke… and said, I will not serve You. In Jeremiah a written -ti is often read "you" (limmadti, v33; qarati, 3:4; dibbarti, 3:5; shama'ti, 4:19), so shavarti can be "you broke"; and 5:5 says it of the people in the same words, they have broken the yoke, they have burst the bonds.

  • v21 "a choice vine" — soreq, the vine of Isaiah's song of the vineyard, planted it with choice vines (Isaiah 5:2), which also yielded what it should not.

  • v34 "you did not find them breaking in" — va-machteret, the word of the law: If the thief is found breaking in and is struck so that he dies, there is no bloodguilt for him (Exodus 22:2). The poor whose blood is on Judah's skirts were no thieves caught in the act. The Greek has not in breakings-in did I find them, but on every oak.

  • v37 "with your hands on your head" — the sign of grief and disgrace: Tamar put her hand on her head and went away, crying out (2 Samuel 13:19).

chapters.title: Return, Faithless Sons
chapters.html:
Jeremiah 3

1If a man sends away his wife,
and she goes from him
and becomes another man's wife,
will he return to her again?
Would not that land be greatly polluted?
But you have prostituted yourself with many lovers;
and would you return to Me?
declares the LORD.

2Lift up your eyes to the bare heights and see:
where have you not been lain with?
By the roads you sat waiting for them
like an Arab in the wilderness.
You have polluted the land
with your prostitution and your wickedness.

3Therefore the showers have been withheld,
and the late rain has not come;
yet you have a prostitute's forehead;
you refuse to be ashamed.

4Have you not just now called to Me,
"My Father, You are the companion of my youth!

5Will He keep His anger forever?
Will He hold on to it to the end?"
This is how you have spoken,
yet you have done all the evil you could.

Faithless Israel and Treacherous Judah

6The LORD said to me in the days of King Josiah, "Have you seen what faithless Israel did? She went up on every high mountain and under every green tree, and prostituted herself there.

7I said, 'After she has done all this, she will return to Me'; but she did not return. Her treacherous sister Judah saw it.

8I saw that, though I had sent faithless Israel away and given her a certificate of divorce for all her adulteries, her treacherous sister Judah did not fear; she too went and prostituted herself.

9Because her prostitution was so light a thing to her, she polluted the land, committing adultery with stone and wood.

10Yet for all this her treacherous sister Judah did not return to Me with her whole heart, but in falsehood, declares the LORD."

11The LORD said to me, "Faithless Israel has shown herself more righteous than treacherous Judah.

12Go and proclaim these words toward the north, and say:
Return, faithless Israel, declares the LORD;
I will not look on you in anger,
for I am loyal, declares the LORD;
I will not keep My anger forever.

13Only acknowledge your iniquity,
that you have rebelled against the LORD your God
and scattered your ways to strangers
under every green tree,
and have not obeyed My voice,
declares the LORD.

14Return, faithless sons, declares the LORD, for I am your husband; I will take you, one from a city and two from a clan, and bring you to Zion.

15I will give you shepherds after My own heart, who will feed you with knowledge and understanding.

16And it shall come to pass, when you have multiplied and been fruitful in the land, in those days, declares the LORD, that they will no longer say, 'The ark of the covenant of the LORD.' It will not come to mind; they will not remember it or miss it, and it will not be made again.

17At that time they will call Jerusalem the throne of the LORD, and all the nations will gather to it, to the name of the LORD at Jerusalem; and they will no longer walk after the stubbornness of their evil heart.

18In those days the house of Judah will walk with the house of Israel, and together they will come from the land of the north to the land I gave your fathers as an inheritance.

19I said, 'How I would set you among the sons, and give you a pleasant land, the most beautiful inheritance of the nations!' And I said, 'You will call Me My Father, and will not turn back from following Me.'

20Surely, as a woman betrays her companion, so you have betrayed Me, house of Israel, declares the LORD."

21A voice is heard on the bare heights,
the weeping and pleading of the sons of Israel,
because they have perverted their way;
they have forgotten the LORD their God.

22Return, faithless sons;
I will heal your faithlessness.
"Here we are; we come to You,
for You are the LORD our God.

23Surely the hills are a lie,
the uproar on the mountains;
surely in the LORD our God
is the deliverance of Israel.

24But the Shame has devoured
all that our fathers labored for from our youth:
their flocks and their herds,
their sons and their daughters.

25Let us lie down in our shame,
and let our disgrace cover us;
for we have sinned against the LORD our God,
we and our fathers,
from our youth to this day,
and we have not obeyed the voice of the LORD our God."

Notes

  • v1 "will he return to her again?… and would you return to Me?" — the law of Deuteronomy 24:1–4: a man who has sent his wife away with a certificate of divorce may not take her again to be his wife after she has been made unclean, for that is detestable before the LORD. You shall not bring sin on the land. The verse asks the law's question. Ve-shov elai has no mark of a question, and can also be read as a call, yet return to Me, the call the chapter makes three times (vv12, 14, 22). The Greek has the question.

  • v3 "the late rain has not come" — malqosh, the rain the LORD promised, the early rain and the late rain (Deuteronomy 11:14), and said He would withhold if the people served other gods: He will shut up the heavens so that there is no rain (11:16–17).

  • v4 "the companion of my youth" — alluf ne'urai, the words of Proverbs 2:17, the woman who forsakes the companion of her youth. Here the faithless wife still calls the LORD by that name.

  • vv6, 12, 14, 22 "faithless… Return" — meshuvah, "turning away," and shuvah, "return," are one root, shuv: Return, turned-away Israel. The play runs through the chapter, Return, faithless sons (vv14, 22), I will heal your faithlessness (v22), and began at 2:19. Treacherous (bogedah) is from bagad, "betray," the verb of v20.

  • v8 "a certificate of divorce" — sefer keritut, the words of Deuteronomy 24:1. Isaiah asked, Where is your mother's certificate of divorce, with which I sent her away? (Isaiah 50:1). Here it was given, to Israel, the northern kingdom; Judah saw it and did not fear.

  • v10 "did not return to Me with her whole heart" — said in the days of Josiah (v6), the king of whom it is written that there was no king like him, who turned to the LORD with all his heart (2 Kings 23:25), the same verb and the same phrase, with all his heart. The king turned; the people turned in falsehood.

  • v14 "for I am your husband" — ba'alti, from ba'al, "master, husband," the name of the god of 2:8 and 2:23. Hosea has the same play: you will call Me "My husband," and no longer call Me "My Baal" (Hosea 2:16). The Greek has I will be lord over you.

  • vv16–17 "The ark of the covenant of the LORD… will not be made again… the throne of the LORD" — the only place Jeremiah names the ark. It was the seat of the LORD of hosts, who is enthroned on the cherubim (1 Samuel 4:4); here the throne is Jerusalem itself.

  • v19 "How I would set you among the sons" — ashitekh, "set you," feminine: the daughter is given a son's place and inheritance, as the daughters of Zelophehad were given a holding as an inheritance among their father's brothers (Numbers 27:7).

  • v24 "the Shame" — ha-boshet, Jeremiah's name for Baal: altars to the Shame, altars to burn incense to Baal (11:13). It is the god that devoured the flocks, the herds and the children.

speech.text: Jeremiah 3

If a man sends away his wife, and she goes from him and becomes another man's wife, will he return to her again? Would not that land be greatly polluted? But you have prostituted yourself with many lovers; and would you return to Me? declares the LORD.

Lift up your eyes to the bare heights and see: where have you not been lain with? By the roads you sat waiting for them like an Arab in the wilderness. You have polluted the land with your prostitution and your wickedness.
Therefore the showers have been withheld, and the late rain has not come; yet you have a prostitute's forehead; you refuse to be ashamed.
Have you not just now called to Me, "My Father, You are the companion of my youth!
Will He keep His anger forever? Will He hold on to it to the end?" This is how you have spoken, yet you have done all the evil you could.
Faithless Israel and Treacherous Judah
The LORD said to me in the days of King Josiah, "Have you seen what faithless Israel did? She went up on every high mountain and under every green tree, and prostituted herself there.
I said, 'After she has done all this, she will return to Me'; but she did not return. Her treacherous sister Judah saw it.
I saw that, though I had sent faithless Israel away and given her a certificate of divorce for all her adulteries, her treacherous sister Judah did not fear; she too went and prostituted herself.
Because her prostitution was so light a thing to her, she polluted the land, committing adultery with stone and wood.
Yet for all this her treacherous sister Judah did not return to Me with her whole heart, but in falsehood, declares the LORD."
The LORD said to me, "Faithless Israel has shown herself more righteous than treacherous Judah.

Go and proclaim these words toward the north, and say: Return, faithless Israel, declares the LORD; I will not look on you in anger, for I am loyal, declares the LORD; I will not keep My anger forever.
Only acknowledge your iniquity, that you have rebelled against the LORD your God and scattered your ways to strangers under every green tree, and have not obeyed My voice, declares the LORD.
Return, faithless sons, declares the LORD, for I am your husband; I will take you, one from a city and two from a clan, and bring you to Zion.
I will give you shepherds after My own heart, who will feed you with knowledge and understanding.

And it shall come to pass, when you have multiplied and been fruitful in the land, in those days, declares the LORD, that they will no longer say, 'The ark of the covenant of the LORD.' It will not come to mind; they will not remember it or miss it, and it will not be made again.

At that time they will call Jerusalem the throne of the LORD, and all the nations will gather to it, to the name of the LORD at Jerusalem; and they will no longer walk after the stubbornness of their evil heart.
In those days the house of Judah will walk with the house of Israel, and together they will come from the land of the north to the land I gave your fathers as an inheritance.

I said, 'How I would set you among the sons, and give you a pleasant land, the most beautiful inheritance of the nations!' And I said, 'You will call Me My Father, and will not turn back from following Me.'
Surely, as a woman betrays her companion, so you have betrayed Me, house of Israel, declares the LORD."
A voice is heard on the bare heights, the weeping and pleading of the sons of Israel, because they have perverted their way; they have forgotten the LORD their God.
Return, faithless sons; I will heal your faithlessness. "Here we are; we come to You, for You are the LORD our God.
Surely the hills are a lie, the uproar on the mountains; surely in the LORD our God is the deliverance of Israel.
But the Shame has devoured all that our fathers labored for from our youth: their flocks and their herds, their sons and their daughters.

Let us lie down in our shame, and let our disgrace cover us; for we have sinned against the LORD our God, we and our fathers, from our youth to this day, and we have not obeyed the voice of the LORD our God."

chapters.title: Wild and Waste
chapters.html:
Jeremiah 4

1If you return, Israel, declares the LORD,
return to Me;
if you put your loathsome things out of My sight,
and do not waver,

2and swear, "As the LORD lives,"
in truth, in justice and in righteousness,
then nations will bless themselves in Him,
and in Him they will glory.

3For this is what the LORD says to the men of Judah and to Jerusalem:
Break up your fallow ground,
and do not sow among thorns.

4Circumcise yourselves to the LORD;
remove the foreskins of your hearts,
men of Judah and inhabitants of Jerusalem;
or My wrath will go out like fire
and burn with no one to quench it,
because of the evil of your deeds.

Disaster from the North

5Declare in Judah, proclaim in Jerusalem, and say:
Blow the ram's horn in the land!
Cry aloud and say:
"Gather together, and let us go
into the fortified cities!"

6Raise a signal toward Zion;
flee for safety; do not stand still;
for I am bringing disaster from the north,
and great destruction.

7A lion has gone up from his thicket;
a destroyer of nations has set out;
he has gone out from his place
to make your land a desolation;
your cities will be ruins,
without inhabitant.

8For this, put on sackcloth;
lament and wail;
for the fierce anger of the LORD
has not turned back from us.

9And it shall come to pass in that day, declares the LORD, that the courage of the king and the courage of the princes will fail; the priests will be appalled, and the prophets astounded.

10Then I said, "Ah, Lord GOD! Surely You have utterly deceived this people and Jerusalem, saying, 'You will have peace,' when the sword has reached the throat."

11At that time it will be said to this people and to Jerusalem:
A scorching wind from the bare heights in the wilderness
comes toward the daughter of My people,
not to winnow and not to cleanse;

12a wind too strong for that
comes at My command.
Now I Myself will speak judgments against them.

13He comes up like clouds,
his chariots like the whirlwind;
his horses are swifter than eagles.
Woe to us, for we are ruined!

14Wash your heart from evil, Jerusalem,
so that you may be saved.
How long will your wicked thoughts
lodge within you?

15For a voice declares from Dan,
and proclaims disaster from Mount Ephraim.

16Warn the nations;
proclaim against Jerusalem:
Besiegers are coming from a distant land;
they raise their voice against the cities of Judah.

17Like keepers of a field they surround her,
because she has rebelled against Me,
declares the LORD.

18Your way and your deeds
have brought this on you.
This is your disaster; how bitter it is!
How it reaches your very heart!

19My insides, my insides! I writhe in pain!
The walls of my heart!
My heart is pounding within me;
I cannot keep silent;
for you have heard, my soul,
the sound of the ram's horn,
the alarm of war.

20Disaster on disaster is proclaimed,
for the whole land is devastated;
suddenly my tents are devastated,
my curtains in a moment.

21How long must I see the signal
and hear the sound of the ram's horn?

22For My people are foolish;
they do not know Me;
they are senseless sons;
they have no understanding.
They are wise in doing evil,
but how to do good they do not know.

23I looked at the earth, and it was wild and waste;
and at the heavens, and their light was gone.

24I looked at the mountains, and they were quaking,
and all the hills were swaying.

25I looked, and there was no man,
and all the birds of the heavens had fled.

26I looked, and the fruitful land was a wilderness,
and all its cities were pulled down
before the LORD,
before His fierce anger.

27For this is what the LORD says:
The whole land will be a desolation;
yet I will not make a full end.

28For this the earth will mourn,
and the heavens above grow dark,
because I have spoken, I have purposed;
I have not relented, and I will not turn back from it.

29At the noise of horseman and archer
every city flees;
they go into the thickets
and climb among the rocks;
every city is forsaken,
and no man lives in them.

30As for you, devastated one, what will you do?
Though you dress in scarlet,
though you adorn yourself with ornaments of gold,
though you enlarge your eyes with paint,
in vain you make yourself beautiful.
Your lovers despise you;
they seek your life.

31For I heard a cry as of a woman in labor,
anguish as of one bearing her first child,
the cry of the daughter of Zion gasping for breath,
stretching out her hands:
"Woe is me! My soul faints
before murderers."

Notes

  • vv1–2 "then nations will bless themselves in Him" — ve-hitbarekhu, the form of the verb in the promise to Abraham, In your seed all the nations of the earth shall bless themselves (Genesis 22:18). Israel's return is the way the blessing reaches the nations.

  • vv3–4 "Break up your fallow ground… remove the foreskins of your hearts" — niru lakhem nir, the words of Hosea 10:12, Break up your fallow ground; it is time to seek the LORD; and the command of Deuteronomy 10:16, Circumcise, then, the foreskin of your heart. Paul: circumcision is of the heart, by the Spirit, not by the letter (Romans 2:29).

  • v10 "Surely You have utterly deceived this people… saying, 'You will have peace'" — hashe hishe'ta, the verb doubled. The peace is the message of the prophets who speak in the LORD's name, Peace, peace, when there is no peace (6:14), and Jeremiah lays it before the LORD as a charge. The Greek also has I said.

  • vv23–26 "I looked at the earth, and it was wild and waste" — tohu va-vohu, the words of Genesis 1:2, the earth was wild and waste, found together elsewhere only in Isaiah 34:11, the line of the wild and the stones of the waste. Then the creation of Genesis 1 runs backward: the light of the first day is gone, there is no man (the sixth day), the birds have fled (the fifth), and the fruitful land is a wilderness (the third). Four times the prophet says I looked.

  • v27 "yet I will not make a full end" — ve-khalah lo e'eseh. The same limit is set twice more in the next chapter, do not make a full end (5:10) and I will not make a full end of you (5:18).

  • v30 "though you enlarge your eyes with paint" — puk, the eye paint of Jezebel, who painted her eyes and adorned her head and looked down from the window (2 Kings 9:30) as her killer arrived. Jerusalem dresses for lovers who now want her life.

  • v31 "as of one bearing her first child" — at the end of Isaiah, Zion gave birth before she was in labor (Isaiah 66:7). Here the daughter of Zion is in labor, and what comes is the murderers.

chapters.title: Search the Streets of Jerusalem
chapters.html:
Jeremiah 5

1Roam through the streets of Jerusalem,
look and take note;
search her squares
to see if you can find a man,
one who does justice
and seeks faithfulness,
that I may pardon her.

2Though they say, "As the LORD lives,"
yet they swear falsely.

3LORD, are not Your eyes on faithfulness?
You struck them, but they felt no pain;
You consumed them,
but they refused to take correction.
They made their faces harder than rock;
they refused to return.

4Then I said, "These are only the poor;
they are foolish,
for they do not know the way of the LORD,
the justice of their God.

5I will go to the great
and speak to them,
for they know the way of the LORD,
the justice of their God."
But they had all alike broken the yoke
and burst the bonds.

6Therefore a lion from the forest will strike them;
a wolf of the desert will destroy them;
a leopard is watching over their cities;
everyone who goes out of them will be torn to pieces;
for their transgressions are many,
their faithlessness is great.

7How can I pardon you?
Your sons have forsaken Me
and sworn by those who are not gods.
When I fed them to the full,
they committed adultery
and trooped to the house of a prostitute.

8They were well-fed, lusty stallions,
each neighing for his neighbor's wife.

9Shall I not punish them for these things?
declares the LORD;
shall I not avenge Myself
on a nation such as this?

10Go up through her vine rows and destroy,
but do not make a full end;
strip away her branches,
for they are not the LORD's.

11For the house of Israel and the house of Judah
have utterly betrayed Me,
declares the LORD.

12They have denied the LORD
and said, "Not He!
No disaster will come on us;
we will not see sword or famine.

13The prophets will become wind;
the word is not in them.
So may it be done to them!"

14Therefore this is what the LORD, the God of hosts, says:
Because you have spoken this word,
I am about to make My words in your mouth a fire,
and this people wood,
and it will devour them.

15I am about to bring against you
a nation from far away, house of Israel,
declares the LORD.
It is an enduring nation;
it is an ancient nation,
a nation whose language you do not know,
nor can you understand what they say.

16Their quiver is like an open grave;
they are all mighty men.

17They will devour your harvest and your bread;
they will devour your sons and your daughters;
they will devour your flocks and your herds;
they will devour your vines and your fig trees;
your fortified cities in which you trust
they will beat down with the sword.

18Yet even in those days, declares the LORD, I will not make a full end of you.

19And it shall come to pass, when you say, "Why has the LORD our God done all these things to us?" that you shall say to them, "As you have forsaken Me and served foreign gods in your land, so you will serve strangers in a land that is not yours."

20Declare this in the house of Jacob,
and proclaim it in Judah:

21Hear this, foolish people without sense,
who have eyes but do not see,
who have ears but do not hear.

22Do you not fear Me? declares the LORD.
Do you not tremble before Me?
I placed the sand as the boundary for the sea,
a lasting decree that it cannot pass;
though its waves toss, they cannot prevail;
though they roar, they cannot pass over it.

23But this people has a stubborn and rebellious heart;
they have turned aside and gone away.

24They do not say in their hearts,
"Let us fear the LORD our God,
who gives the rain in its season,
the early rain and the late rain,
who keeps for us
the weeks appointed for the harvest."

25Your iniquities have turned these away,
and your sins have kept good from you.

26For wicked men are found among My people;
they lie in wait like fowlers crouching;
they set a trap;
they catch men.

27Like a cage full of birds,
their houses are full of deceit;
so they have become great and rich;

28they have grown fat and sleek.
They also overflow with deeds of evil;
they do not plead the cause,
the cause of the fatherless, to make it prosper;
and they do not defend the rights of the needy.

29Shall I not punish them for these things?
declares the LORD;
shall I not avenge Myself
on a nation such as this?

30An appalling and horrible thing
has happened in the land:

31the prophets prophesy falsely,
and the priests rule at their direction;
and My people love to have it so.
But what will you do when the end comes?

Notes

  • v1 "to see if you can find a man… that I may pardon her" — the bargain Abraham struck for Sodom, If I find in Sodom fifty righteous within the city, then I will lift the whole place for their sake (Genesis 18:26), which came down to ten. Here the LORD asks for one, and none is found.

  • v5 "they had all alike broken the yoke and burst the bonds" — shaveru ol nittequ moserot, the words of 2:20, where the Hebrew as read has the LORD breaking the yoke; here the people break it.

  • v6 "a leopard is watching over their cities" — shoqed, the word of the almond branch, I am watching over My word to do it (1:12). The LORD watches over His word, and the leopard over the cities.

  • v14 "I am about to make My words in your mouth a fire" — the words put into Jeremiah's mouth at his call (I have put My words in your mouth, 1:9) now burn. Later he says it again: Is not My word like fire, declares the LORD, and like a hammer that shatters rock? (23:29).

  • v15 "a nation from far away… a nation whose language you do not know" — the curse of Deuteronomy 28:49, The LORD will bring against you a nation from far away… a nation whose language you will not understand; vv16–17 go on in the curse's own picture, a nation that eats the land's produce (28:51).

  • v21 "who have eyes but do not see, who have ears but do not hear" — the words the psalm uses of idols: eyes, but do not see… ears but do not hear (Psalm 115:5–6). Jesus asks His disciples, Having eyes, do you not see, and having ears, do you not hear? (Mark 8:18).

  • v22 "I placed the sand as the boundary for the sea" — the sea obeys a line of sand; the people do not. The LORD says the same to Job of the sea, This far you may come, and no farther, and here your proud waves shall stop (Job 38:11).

  • v24 "the early rain and the late rain… the weeks appointed for the harvest" — the rain of Deuteronomy 11:14, the early rain and the late rain, and the seven weeks counted from the first sickle to the Festival of Weeks (Deuteronomy 16:9–10). The people take the harvest and forget who keeps its calendar.

chapters.title: Peace, Peace, When There Is No Peace
chapters.html:
Jeremiah 6

1Flee for safety, sons of Benjamin,
out of the middle of Jerusalem!
Blow the ram's horn in Tekoa,
and raise a fire signal on Beth-haccherem;
for disaster looks down from the north,
and great destruction.

2The lovely and delicate one,
the daughter of Zion, I will destroy.

3Shepherds with their flocks will come against her;
they will pitch their tents all around her;
each will graze his own part.

4Consecrate war against her!
"Arise, let us go up at noon!"
"Woe to us, for the day is turning,
for the shadows of evening lengthen!"

5"Arise, let us go up by night,
and destroy her palaces!"

6For this is what the LORD of hosts says:
Cut down her trees,
and cast up a siege ramp against Jerusalem.
This is the city to be punished;
there is nothing but oppression within her.

7As a well keeps its water fresh,
so she keeps her wickedness fresh;
violence and destruction are heard in her;
sickness and wounds are ever before Me.

8Be warned, Jerusalem,
or My soul will be torn from you,
or I will make you a desolation,
a land without inhabitant.

9This is what the LORD of hosts says:
They will strip the remnant of Israel bare
as one strips a vine;
pass your hand again over its branches,
like a grape gatherer.

10To whom shall I speak and give warning,
that they may hear?
Their ears are uncircumcised,
and they cannot listen;
the word of the LORD has become a reproach to them;
they take no pleasure in it.

11But I am full of the wrath of the LORD;
I am weary of holding it in.
Pour it out on the children in the street,
and on the gatherings of young men together;
for both husband and wife will be taken,
the old with the very aged.

12Their houses will be turned over to others,
their fields and their wives together;
for I will stretch out My hand
against the inhabitants of the land,
declares the LORD.

13For from the least of them to the greatest,
everyone is greedy for unjust gain;
from prophet to priest,
everyone deals falsely.

14They have healed the wound of My people lightly,
saying, "Peace, peace,"
when there is no peace.

15They acted shamefully, committing detestable things;
yet they were not at all ashamed;
they did not know how to blush.
Therefore they will fall among those who fall;
at the time I punish them they will stumble,
says the LORD.

16This is what the LORD says:
Stand by the roads and look,
and ask for the ancient paths,
where the good way is,
and walk in it,
and you will find rest for your souls.
But they said, "We will not walk in it."

17I set watchmen over you:
"Listen to the sound of the ram's horn!"
But they said, "We will not listen."

18Therefore hear, you nations,
and know, you congregation,
what is among them.

19Hear, earth:
I am about to bring disaster on this people,
the fruit of their own schemes,
because they have not listened to My words,
and My law, they have rejected it.

20What use to Me is frankincense that comes from Sheba,
or fragrant cane from a distant land?
Your burnt offerings are not acceptable,
and your sacrifices do not please Me.

21Therefore this is what the LORD says:
I am about to lay stumbling blocks before this people;
fathers and sons together will stumble on them;
neighbor and friend will perish.

22This is what the LORD says:
A people is coming from the land of the north;
a great nation is stirring
from the farthest parts of the earth.

23They lay hold of bow and javelin;
they are cruel and have no mercy;
their voice roars like the sea;
they ride on horses,
set in array as a man for battle,
against you, daughter of Zion.

24We have heard the report of it;
our hands fall limp;
anguish has seized us,
pain as of a woman in labor.

25Do not go out into the field,
or walk on the road;
for the enemy has a sword;
terror is on every side.

26Daughter of my people,
put on sackcloth
and roll in ashes;
make mourning as for an only son,
a most bitter lament;
for suddenly the destroyer
will come upon us.

27I have made you a tester among My people,
a fortress,
that you may know and test their way.

28They are all stubborn rebels,
going about with slander;
they are bronze and iron;
all of them act corruptly.

29The bellows blow fiercely;
the lead is consumed by the fire;
in vain the refiner refines,
for the wicked are not removed.

30They are called rejected silver,
for the LORD has rejected them.

Notes

  • v1 "Blow the ram's horn in Tekoa" — bi-Tqoa tiq'u, the town's name and the verb, taqa, "blow," share their letters. Tekoa was the home of the prophet Amos (among the shepherds of Tekoa, Amos 1:1). Sons of Benjamin are Jeremiah's own tribe (1:1).

  • v2 "The lovely and delicate one, the daughter of Zion, I will destroy" — ha-navah ve-ha-me'unnagah damiti. Me'unnagah is the delicate woman of the curse, most tender and delicate among you (Deuteronomy 28:56), and damiti is "I will cut off." The same letters can be read navah, "pasture," and damiti, "I have likened": To a lovely pasture I liken the daughter of Zion, which runs into the shepherds and flocks of v3. The Greek has your pride will be taken away, daughter of Zion.

  • v9 "They will strip the remnant of Israel bare as one strips a vine" — olel ye'olelu, the verb of the law, You shall not strip your vineyard bare… You shall leave them for the poor and for the guest (Leviticus 19:10). The enemy will leave nothing.

  • v10 "Their ears are uncircumcised" — as their hearts are (4:4). Stephen to the council: you stiff-necked people, uncircumcised in hearts and ears (Acts 7:51).

  • vv13–15 "saying, 'Peace, peace,' when there is no peace" — the peace of 4:10. These verses come again almost word for word in 8:10–12, where the Greek does not have them.

  • v16 "ask for the ancient paths… and find rest for your souls" — margo'a le-nafshekhem. Jesus says, Take My yoke upon you… and you will find rest for your souls (Matthew 11:29), in the words of the Hebrew; the Greek of Jeremiah has purification for your souls.

  • vv22–24 "A people is coming from the land of the north… against you, daughter of Zion" — the same words are turned on Babylon at the end of the book: against you, daughter of Babylon, and the king of Babylon has heard the report of them, and his hands fall limp; anguish has seized him, pain as of a woman in labor (50:41–43).

  • v25 "terror is on every side" — magor mi-saviv, Jeremiah's phrase. He gives it as a name to the priest Pashhur, who had him beaten and put in the stocks (20:3), and hears it whispered against himself (20:10), as the psalmist did: terror on every side, as they plot together against me (Psalm 31:13).

  • v26 "make mourning as for an only son" — evel yachid, the grief for a son who leaves no other; yachid is the word God used of Isaac, your son — your beloved one (Genesis 22:2).

  • vv27–30 "a tester… the refiner refines… rejected silver" — the prophet is set to test the people as silver is tested, and the metal does not come clean. Isaiah used the same picture: Your silver has become dross… I will smelt away your dross as with lye (Isaiah 1:22, 25).

speech.text: Jeremiah 6

Flee for safety, sons of Benjamin, out of the middle of Jerusalem! Blow the ram's horn in Tekoa, and raise a fire signal on Beth-haccherem; for disaster looks down from the north, and great destruction.
The lovely and delicate one, the daughter of Zion, I will destroy.
Shepherds with their flocks will come against her; they will pitch their tents all around her; each will graze his own part.
Consecrate war against her! "Arise, let us go up at noon!" "Woe to us, for the day is turning, for the shadows of evening lengthen!"
"Arise, let us go up by night, and destroy her palaces!"
For this is what the LORD of hosts says: Cut down her trees, and cast up a siege ramp against Jerusalem. This is the city to be punished; there is nothing but oppression within her.
As a well keeps its water fresh, so she keeps her wickedness fresh; violence and destruction are heard in her; sickness and wounds are ever before Me.
Be warned, Jerusalem, or My soul will be torn from you, or I will make you a desolation, a land without inhabitant.
This is what the LORD of hosts says: They will strip the remnant of Israel bare as one strips a vine; pass your hand again over its branches, like a grape gatherer.
To whom shall I speak and give warning, that they may hear? Their ears are uncircumcised, and they cannot listen; the word of the LORD has become a reproach to them; they take no pleasure in it.

But I am full of the wrath of the LORD; I am weary of holding it in. Pour it out on the children in the street, and on the gatherings of young men together; for both husband and wife will be taken, the old with the very aged.
Their houses will be turned over to others, their fields and their wives together; for I will stretch out My hand against the inhabitants of the land, declares the LORD.
For from the least of them to the greatest, everyone is greedy for unjust gain; from prophet to priest, everyone deals falsely.
They have healed the wound of My people lightly, saying, "Peace, peace," when there is no peace.

They acted shamefully, committing detestable things; yet they were not at all ashamed; they did not know how to blush. Therefore they will fall among those who fall; at the time I punish them they will stumble, says the LORD.

This is what the LORD says: Stand by the roads and look, and ask for the ancient paths, where the good way is, and walk in it, and you will find rest for your souls. But they said, "We will not walk in it."
I set watchmen over you: "Listen to the sound of the ram's horn!" But they said, "We will not listen."
Therefore hear, you nations, and know, you congregation, what is among them.
Hear, earth: I am about to bring disaster on this people, the fruit of their own schemes, because they have not listened to My words, and My law, they have rejected it.
What use to Me is frankincense that comes from Sheba, or fragrant cane from a distant land? Your burnt offerings are not acceptable, and your sacrifices do not please Me.
Therefore this is what the LORD says: I am about to lay stumbling blocks before this people; fathers and sons together will stumble on them; neighbor and friend will perish.
This is what the LORD says: A people is coming from the land of the north; a great nation is stirring from the farthest parts of the earth.
They lay hold of bow and javelin; they are cruel and have no mercy; their voice roars like the sea; they ride on horses, set in array as a man for battle, against you, daughter of Zion.
We have heard the report of it; our hands fall limp; anguish has seized us, pain as of a woman in labor.
Do not go out into the field, or walk on the road; for the enemy has a sword; terror is on every side.
Daughter of my people, put on sackcloth and roll in ashes; make mourning as for an only son, a most bitter lament; for suddenly the destroyer will come upon us.
I have made you a tester among My people, a fortress, that you may know and test their way.
They are all stubborn rebels, going about with slander; they are bronze and iron; all of them act corruptly.
The bellows blow fiercely; the lead is consumed by the fire; in vain the refiner refines, for the wicked are not removed.
They are called rejected silver, for the LORD has rejected them.

chapters.title: A Den of Robbers
chapters.html:
Jeremiah 7

1The word that came to Jeremiah from the LORD:

2Stand in the gate of the LORD's house and proclaim there this word, and say: Hear the word of the LORD, all you of Judah who enter these gates to worship the LORD.

3This is what the LORD of hosts, the God of Israel, says: Amend your ways and your deeds, and I will let you dwell in this place.

4Do not trust in these deceptive words: "The temple of the LORD, the temple of the LORD, the temple of the LORD is this!"

5For if you truly amend your ways and your deeds, if you truly do justice between a man and his neighbor,

6if you do not oppress the guest, the fatherless and the widow, and do not shed innocent blood in this place, and do not go after other gods to your own harm,

7then I will let you dwell in this place, in the land that I gave to your fathers from of old and forever.

8But you are trusting in deceptive words that cannot profit.

9Will you steal, murder, commit adultery, swear falsely, burn incense to Baal and go after other gods that you have not known,

10and then come and stand before Me in this house, which is called by My name, and say, "We are delivered!" — only to go on doing all these detestable things?

11Has this house, which is called by My name, become a den of robbers in your eyes? I Myself have seen it, declares the LORD.

12Go now to My place that was in Shiloh, where I made My name dwell at first, and see what I did to it because of the wickedness of My people Israel.

13So now, because you have done all these things, declares the LORD, and I spoke to you again and again, but you did not listen, and I called you, but you did not answer,

14I will do to the house that is called by My name, in which you trust, and to the place that I gave to you and to your fathers, as I did to Shiloh.

15I will cast you out of My sight, as I cast out all your brothers, all the offspring of Ephraim.

Do Not Pray for This People

16As for you, do not pray for this people, or lift up a cry or a prayer for them, or intercede with Me, for I will not hear you.

17Do you not see what they are doing in the cities of Judah and in the streets of Jerusalem?

18The children gather wood, the fathers kindle the fire, and the women knead dough to make cakes for the queen of heaven; and they pour out drink offerings to other gods, to provoke Me.

19Is it Me they provoke? declares the LORD. Is it not themselves, to their own shame?

20Therefore this is what the Lord GOD says: My anger and My wrath will be poured out on this place, on man and on beast, on the trees of the field and on the fruit of the ground; it will burn and not be quenched.

Obey My Voice

21This is what the LORD of hosts, the God of Israel, says: Add your burnt offerings to your sacrifices, and eat the meat.

22For I did not speak to your fathers or command them, in the day I brought them out of the land of Egypt, about burnt offerings and sacrifices.

23But this is what I commanded them: "Obey My voice, and I will be your God, and you will be My people; and walk in all the way that I command you, so that it may go well with you."

24But they did not listen or incline their ear; they walked in their own counsels, in the stubbornness of their evil heart, and went backward and not forward.

25From the day your fathers came out of the land of Egypt to this day, I have sent you all My servants the prophets, sending them again and again, day after day.

26Yet they did not listen to Me or incline their ear, but stiffened their neck; they did worse than their fathers.

27You shall speak all these words to them, but they will not listen to you; you shall call to them, but they will not answer you.

28You shall say to them: "This is the nation that did not obey the voice of the LORD its God and did not take correction; faithfulness has perished; it is cut off from their mouth."

The Valley of Slaughter

29Cut off your crown and throw it away; raise a lament on the bare heights; for the LORD has rejected and forsaken the generation of His wrath.

30For the sons of Judah have done what is evil in My eyes, declares the LORD; they have set their loathsome things in the house that is called by My name, to defile it.

31They have built the high places of Topheth, which is in the Valley of the Son of Hinnom, to burn their sons and their daughters in the fire, which I did not command, nor did it come into My mind.

32Therefore, days are coming, declares the LORD, when it will no longer be called Topheth or the Valley of the Son of Hinnom, but the Valley of Slaughter; for they will bury in Topheth because there is no room elsewhere.

33The corpses of this people will be food for the birds of the heavens and for the beasts of the earth, and there will be no one to frighten them away.

34I will silence from the cities of Judah and from the streets of Jerusalem the voice of mirth and the voice of gladness, the voice of the bridegroom and the voice of the bride; for the land will become a ruin.

Notes

  • v9 "Will you steal, murder, commit adultery, swear falsely… and go after other gods" — five of the Ten Words, given as bare verbs: You shall not murder… commit adultery… steal… answer against your neighbor as a false witness (Exodus 20:13–16), and You shall have no other gods before My face (20:3). Then the people come to the temple and say, We are delivered!

  • v11 "a den of robbers" — me'arat paritsim, a cave where robbers hide between raids. Jesus, clearing the temple, joins Isaiah to this verse: My house shall be called a house of prayer (Isaiah 56:7), but you are making it a den of robbers (Matthew 21:13).

  • vv12, 14 "My place that was in Shiloh" — where the tent of meeting stood when the land was first taken (Joshua 18:1), and from which the ark was carried into battle and taken (1 Samuel 4:11). The psalm says, He abandoned the dwelling at Shiloh (Psalm 78:60). The house in Jerusalem has no promise Shiloh did not have.

  • vv13, 25 "I spoke to you again and again… sending them again and again" — hashkem, "rising early": Jeremiah's word for the LORD's persistence (7:13, 25; 11:7; 25:4; 26:5), and the word of the Chronicler's last chapter, sent to them by His messengers, sending again and again, because He had compassion on His people (2 Chronicles 36:15).

  • v16 "do not… intercede with Me" — al tifga bi, the verb of the servant who intercedes for the transgressors (Isaiah 53:12). The prophet is forbidden to do what the prophet's office was for.

  • v18 "cakes for the queen of heaven" — the whole family serves her: children, fathers, women. Kavvanim, "cakes," is found only here and in 44:19, where the women answer Jeremiah that they made them with their husbands' knowledge. The Greek has the host of heaven.

  • vv21–23 "Add your burnt offerings to your sacrifices, and eat the meat… Obey My voice" — a burnt offering was wholly burned, the priest shall turn all of it into smoke on the altar (Leviticus 1:9); since they mean nothing, the people may as well eat them. What came first was the voice: if you will truly listen to My voice and keep My covenant (Exodus 19:5), and I will be your God, and you will be My people (Leviticus 26:12). Samuel said it to Saul: To listen is better than sacrifice (1 Samuel 15:22).

  • v29 "Cut off your crown and throw it away" — nezer, the Nazirite's hair, the crown of his God is on his head (Numbers 6:7). Jerusalem, the city set apart, is told to shave off what marked her as the LORD's.

  • vv31–32 "Topheth, which is in the Valley of the Son of Hinnom" — the place Josiah defiled… so that no one might make his son or his daughter pass through the fire to Molech (2 Kings 23:10). The valley's name, ge-Hinnom, becomes the Greek geenna, Gehenna: liable to the fire of Gehenna (Matthew 5:22).

  • v34 "the voice of the bridegroom and the voice of the bride" — silenced again in 16:9 and 25:10, and given back in 33:11, the voice of the bridegroom and the voice of the bride, the voice of those who say, Give thanks to the LORD of hosts, for the LORD is good.

chapters.title: Is There No Balm in Gilead?
chapters.html:
Jeremiah 8

1At that time, declares the LORD, they will bring out of their graves the bones of the kings of Judah, the bones of its princes, the bones of the priests, the bones of the prophets and the bones of the inhabitants of Jerusalem,

2and spread them before the sun and the moon and all the host of heaven, which they have loved and served, which they have gone after, which they have sought and worshipped. They will not be gathered or buried; they will be dung on the face of the ground.

3Death will be chosen rather than life by all the remnant that remains of this evil family, in all the places where I have driven them, declares the LORD of hosts.

Turning Away

4You shall say to them, This is what the LORD says:
When men fall, do they not get up?
If one turns away, does he not turn back?

5Why then has this people, Jerusalem,
turned away in lasting faithlessness?
They hold fast to deceit;
they refuse to return.

6I have listened and heard;
they do not speak what is right;
no one repents of his wickedness,
saying, "What have I done?"
Each one turns to his own course,
like a horse plunging headlong into battle.

7Even the stork in the heavens
knows her appointed times;
and the turtledove, the swift and the crane
keep the time of their coming;
but My people do not know
the ordinance of the LORD.

8How can you say, "We are wise,
and the law of the LORD is with us"?
But the lying pen of the scribes
has made it into a lie.

9The wise will be put to shame;
they will be dismayed and taken;
they have rejected the word of the LORD,
and what wisdom is in them?

10Therefore I will give their wives to others,
and their fields to new owners;
for from the least to the greatest
everyone is greedy for unjust gain;
from prophet to priest
everyone deals falsely.

11They have healed the wound of the daughter of My people lightly,
saying, "Peace, peace,"
when there is no peace.

12They acted shamefully, committing detestable things;
yet they were not at all ashamed;
they did not know how to blush.
Therefore they will fall among those who fall;
in the time of their punishment they will stumble,
says the LORD.

13I will gather them up and sweep them away,
declares the LORD;
there are no grapes on the vine,
no figs on the fig tree,
and the leaf has withered;
what I gave them will pass away from them.

14Why are we sitting still?
Gather together, and let us go into the fortified cities
and perish there;
for the LORD our God has doomed us to perish,
and given us poisoned water to drink,
because we have sinned against the LORD.

15We hoped for peace, but no good came;
for a time of healing, but there is terror.

16The snorting of his horses is heard from Dan;
at the sound of the neighing of his stallions
the whole land quakes.
They come and devour the land and all that fills it,
the city and those who live in it.

17For I am about to send among you serpents,
adders that cannot be charmed,
and they will bite you,
declares the LORD.

Is There No Balm in Gilead?

18There is no cheer for me in my grief;
my heart is sick within me.

19Hear the cry of the daughter of my people
from a land far away:
"Is the LORD not in Zion?
Is her King not in her?"
"Why have they provoked Me with their carved images,
with their foreign emptiness?"

20"The harvest is past, the summer is ended,
and we are not saved."

21For the wound of the daughter of my people I am wounded;
I mourn; horror has seized me.

22Is there no balm in Gilead?
Is there no physician there?
Why then has the daughter of my people
not been healed?

Notes

  • vv1–2 "they will bring out of their graves the bones… and spread them before the sun and the moon and all the host of heaven" — what Josiah did to the graves at Bethel, He sent and took the bones out of the graves and burned them on the altar (2 Kings 23:16), is done to Judah's own kings and priests. Josiah had put down the priests who burned incense to the sun and the moon… and to all the host of heaven (23:5); here five verbs of devotion are given to them, loved… served… gone after… sought… worshipped, and the bones are laid out before them.

  • v3 "Death will be chosen rather than life" — Moses set the choice before the people: I have set before you life and death… Choose life (Deuteronomy 30:19). The remnant will choose the other.

  • vv4–5 "If one turns away, does he not turn back?… they refuse to return" — shuv, "turn," five times in two verses, as through 3:6–22: yashuv… yashuv… shovevah… meshuvah… lashuv.

  • v7 "the stork… the turtledove, the swift and the crane keep the time of their coming" — the birds keep their seasons; the people do not keep the LORD's. Isaiah began the same way: The ox knows its owner… Israel does not know (Isaiah 1:3). Swift is the read form, sis; the written form is sus, "horse."

  • vv10–12 "from prophet to priest everyone deals falsely… 'Peace, peace'" — 6:12–15, nearly word for word. The Greek has only the first line of v10 and nothing of vv11–12.

  • v13 "I will gather them up and sweep them away… there are no grapes on the vine, no figs on the fig tree" — asof asifem, two verbs that sound alike: asaf, "gather," the word for bringing in a harvest, and suf, "come to an end." The same pair stands in Zephaniah 1:2, I will utterly sweep away everything from the face of the ground. Read with asaf alone, the line is a harvest that finds nothing: When I would gather them, there are no grapes on the vine. The Greek has they will gather their produce. Jesus came to a fig tree and found nothing on it but leaves (Matthew 21:19).

  • v14 "Gather together, and let us go into the fortified cities and perish there" — the cry of 4:5, Gather together, and let us go into the fortified cities, said again with its end added. Poisoned water, mei rosh, comes back in 9:15 and 23:15.

  • v17 "I am about to send among you serpents… and they will bite you" — the words of the wilderness, the LORD sent the fiery serpents among the people, and they bit the people (Numbers 21:6). There, Moses made a bronze serpent, and whoever looked at it lived (21:9); here the adders cannot be charmed.

  • vv18–22 "Is there no balm in Gilead?" — tsori, the balm the Ishmaelites were carrying from Gilead when Joseph was sold (Genesis 37:25). The lament goes on in one more verse, numbered 8:23 in the Hebrew and 9:1 in the English, and the English numbering is followed.

chapters.title: Let Him Who Boasts Boast in This
chapters.html:
Jeremiah 9

1Oh, that my head were waters,
and my eyes a fountain of tears,
so that I might weep day and night
for the slain of the daughter of my people!

2Oh, that I had in the wilderness
a travelers' lodging place,
that I might leave my people
and go away from them!
For they are all adulterers,
a company of traitors.

3They bend their tongue like their bow;
falsehood and not faithfulness
has grown strong in the land;
for they go from evil to evil,
and they do not know Me,
declares the LORD.

4Let everyone beware of his neighbor,
and put no trust in any brother;
for every brother is a supplanter,
and every neighbor goes about with slander.

5Each one deceives his neighbor,
and no one speaks the truth;
they have taught their tongue to speak falsehood;
they weary themselves doing wrong.

6You live in the middle of deceit;
through deceit they refuse to know Me,
declares the LORD.

7Therefore this is what the LORD of hosts says:
I am about to refine them and test them,
for what else can I do
because of the daughter of My people?

8Their tongue is a sharpened arrow;
it speaks deceit;
with his mouth each speaks peace to his neighbor,
but in his heart he plans an ambush.

9Shall I not punish them for these things?
declares the LORD;
shall I not avenge Myself
on a nation such as this?

10I will take up weeping and wailing for the mountains,
and a lament for the pastures of the wilderness,
because they are burned up so that no one passes through,
and the lowing of cattle is not heard;
both the birds of the heavens and the beasts
have fled and are gone.

11I will make Jerusalem a heap of ruins,
a lair of jackals;
and I will make the cities of Judah a desolation,
without inhabitant.

12Who is the man wise enough to understand this? To whom has the mouth of the LORD spoken, that he may declare it? Why is the land ruined and burned like a wilderness, so that no one passes through?

13The LORD said: Because they have forsaken My law that I set before them, and have not obeyed My voice or walked in it,

14but have walked after the stubbornness of their own heart and after the Baals, as their fathers taught them,

15therefore this is what the LORD of hosts, the God of Israel, says: I am about to feed this people with wormwood and give them poisoned water to drink.

16I will scatter them among nations that neither they nor their fathers have known, and I will send the sword after them until I have consumed them.

17This is what the LORD of hosts says:
Consider, and call for the mourning women to come;
send for the skilled women to come;

18let them hurry and raise a wailing over us,
so that our eyes may run down with tears,
and our eyelids flow with water.

19For a sound of wailing is heard from Zion:
"How we are ruined!
We are utterly put to shame,
for we have left the land,
for they have cast down our dwellings."

20Hear, you women, the word of the LORD,
and let your ear receive the word of His mouth;
teach your daughters a wailing,
and each her neighbor a lament.

21For death has come up through our windows;
it has entered our palaces,
to cut off the children from the street,
and the young men from the squares.

22Speak: This is what the LORD declares:
The corpses of men will fall
like dung on the open field,
like sheaves after the reaper,
with no one to gather them.

23This is what the LORD says:
Let not the wise man boast in his wisdom;
let not the mighty man boast in his might;
let not the rich man boast in his riches;

24but let him who boasts boast in this,
that he understands and knows Me,
that I am the LORD who practices loyal love,
justice and righteousness in the earth;
for in these things I delight,
declares the LORD.

25Days are coming, declares the LORD, when I will punish all who are circumcised in the flesh alone:

26Egypt, Judah, Edom, the sons of Ammon, Moab, and all who clip the hair at the sides of their head, who live in the wilderness; for all these nations are uncircumcised, and all the house of Israel is uncircumcised in heart.

Notes

  • v1 "Oh, that my head were waters" — in the Hebrew this verse is 8:23, the last line of the lament that began at 8:18, and the Hebrew numbers the rest of this chapter one lower (9:2 is Hebrew 9:1). The English numbering is followed.

  • vv3, 8 "They bend their tongue like their bow… Their tongue is a sharpened arrow" — the tongue is the weapon in both verses: bent like a bow in v3, loosed as an arrow in v8. Sharpened is the read form, shachut; the written form is shochet, "slaughtering."

  • v4 "every brother is a supplanter" — aqov ya'qov, "supplanting he supplants": the verb is Jacob's name. Esau said it first, Is it because his name is called Jacob that he has heeled me these two times? (Genesis 27:36). Every brother in Judah has become a Jacob.

  • v7 "I am about to refine them and test them" — the refiner of 6:27–30, where the silver did not come clean; here the LORD takes up the work Himself.

  • v15 "I am about to feed this people with wormwood and give them poisoned water to drink" — the words of Deuteronomy 29:18, Let there not be among you a root bearing poison and wormwood: what Moses warned would grow among them is now their food and drink.

  • v16 "I will scatter them among nations… and I will send the sword after them" — the curse of the covenant, I will scatter you among the nations, and I will draw the sword after you (Leviticus 26:33).

  • vv17–20 "call for the mourning women… teach your daughters a wailing" — the women whose trade was the lament; ha-chakhamot, "the skilled women," are the wise in their craft. The Chronicler says all the singing men and singing women have spoken of Josiah in their laments to this day, and that Jeremiah lamented for him (2 Chronicles 35:25). Here the mothers must teach the lament to their daughters.

  • vv23–24 "let him who boasts boast in this, that he understands and knows Me" — Paul gives the sense of the verse twice, Let the one who boasts, boast in the Lord (1 Corinthians 1:31; 2 Corinthians 10:17). What the LORD delights in is chesed, loyal love, with justice and righteousness.

  • vv25–26 "all who are circumcised in the flesh alone… uncircumcised in heart" — kol mul be-orlah, "all circumcised in foreskin": circumcised outwardly, with the heart untouched. It can also be read the circumcised together with the uncircumcised. Judah is listed among the nations. Who clip the hair at the sides of their head is the custom the law forbade, You shall not round off the hair at the sides of your head (Leviticus 19:27). The heart is what 4:4 asked to be circumcised.

chapters.title: The Living God and the Idols
chapters.html:
Jeremiah 10

1Hear the word that the LORD speaks to you, house of Israel.

2This is what the LORD says:
Do not learn the way of the nations,
and do not be dismayed at the signs of the heavens,
though the nations are dismayed at them;

3for the customs of the peoples are emptiness.
A tree is cut from the forest,
the work of a craftsman's hands with an axe.

4They adorn it with silver and gold;
they fasten it with nails and hammers
so that it will not totter.

5They are like a scarecrow in a cucumber field,
and they cannot speak;
they have to be carried,
for they cannot walk.
Do not be afraid of them,
for they can do no harm,
and neither is it in them to do good.

6There is none like You, LORD;
You are great,
and Your name is great in might.

7Who would not fear You, King of the nations?
For this is Your due;
for among all the wise of the nations
and in all their kingdoms
there is none like You.

8They are all senseless and foolish;
the teaching of emptiness is wood.

9Beaten silver is brought from Tarshish,
and gold from Uphaz,
the work of the craftsman and of the goldsmith's hands;
their clothing is blue and purple;
they are all the work of skilled men.

10But the LORD is the true God;
He is the living God and the everlasting King.
At His wrath the earth quakes,
and the nations cannot endure His indignation.

11This is what you shall say to them: The gods who did not make the heavens and the earth will perish from the earth and from under these heavens.

12It is He who made the earth by His power,
who established the world by His wisdom,
and by His understanding stretched out the heavens.

13When He utters His voice,
there is a roar of waters in the heavens;
He makes the clouds rise from the ends of the earth;
He makes lightning for the rain
and brings out the wind from His storehouses.

14Every man is senseless, without knowledge;
every goldsmith is put to shame by his idol;
for his images are falsehood,
and there is no breath in them.

15They are emptiness, a work of mockery;
in the time of their punishment they will perish.

16Not like these is the Portion of Jacob,
for He is the One who formed all things,
and Israel is the tribe of His inheritance;
the LORD of hosts is His name.

17Gather up your bundle from the ground,
you who live under siege!

18For this is what the LORD says:
I am about to sling out the inhabitants of the land
at this time,
and I will bring distress on them,
so that they may find it so.

19Woe is me because of my wound!
My wound is grievous.
But I said, "Surely this is a sickness,
and I must bear it."

20My tent is destroyed,
and all my cords are broken;
my sons have gone from me,
and they are no more;
there is no one to spread my tent again
and to set up my curtains.

21For the shepherds have become senseless
and have not sought the LORD;
therefore they have not prospered,
and all their flock is scattered.

22The sound of a report: it is coming,
a great commotion from the land of the north,
to make the cities of Judah a desolation,
a lair of jackals.

23I know, LORD, that a man's way is not his own;
it is not in a man who walks
to direct his steps.

24Correct me, LORD, but with justice;
not in Your anger,
or You will bring me to nothing.

25Pour out Your wrath on the nations that do not know You,
and on the clans that do not call on Your name;
for they have devoured Jacob;
they have devoured him and consumed him,
and have laid waste his pasture.

Notes

  • v4 "they fasten it with nails and hammers so that it will not totter" — Isaiah's picture of the idol-maker, who fastens it with nails so that it will not totter (Isaiah 41:7; also 40:20). A god that must be nailed down so as not to fall over.

  • v5 "like a scarecrow in a cucumber field" — ke-tomer miqshah. Miqshah is the cucumber field of Isaiah 1:8, like a hut in a cucumber field, and the Letter of Jeremiah has the same picture: like a scarecrow in a cucumber field that guards nothing, so are their gods of wood, overlaid with gold and silver (Letter of Jeremiah 1:69, Swete's Greek). Miqshah is also the word for hammered work, the hammered gold of the lampstand (Exodus 25:31), and tomer can be a post: like a post of hammered work. The Greek has it is chased silver.

  • vv6–8, 10 "There is none like You, LORD… He is the living God and the everlasting King" — the Greek does not have these verses; it goes from the idols of v5 to the silver of v9 and on to v11. The song John hears in heaven takes up v7: Who will not fear, Lord, and glorify Your name?… All the nations will come and worship before You (Revelation 15:4).

  • v9 "their clothing is blue and purple" — tekhelet ve-argaman, two of the colors of the dwelling's curtains, blue and purple and crimson (Exodus 26:1), and of the priests' garments (28:5). The idol is dressed as the LORD's house was.

  • v11 "This is what you shall say to them: The gods who did not make the heavens and the earth will perish" — this one verse is in Aramaic, the language Hezekiah's officials asked the Assyrian envoy to use (Please speak to your servants in Aramaic, 2 Kings 18:26): a sentence given to be said to the nations. It turns on a pair of sounds, avadu, "made," and ye'vadu, "will perish": the gods who did not make will be unmade.

  • vv12–16 "It is He who made the earth by His power" — these five verses are given again, nearly word for word, in the oracle against Babylon (51:15–19). v13's last lines are those of Psalm 135:7, He makes the clouds rise from the ends of the earth; He makes lightning for the rain and brings out the wind from His storehouses.

  • v16 "Not like these is the Portion of Jacob" — the Song of Moses says the LORD's portion is His people, Jacob the measured lot of His inheritance (Deuteronomy 32:9); here it is turned around, and the LORD is Jacob's portion, as He said to Aaron, I am your share and your inheritance (Numbers 18:20).

  • v20 "My tent is destroyed, and all my cords are broken… no one to spread my tent again" — the opposite of Isaiah's promise to Zion, Enlarge the place of your tent… lengthen your cords (Isaiah 54:2).

  • vv23–24 "a man's way is not his own… Correct me, LORD, but with justice; not in Your anger" — the wisdom of A man's steps are from the LORD (Proverbs 20:24), and the prayer of LORD, do not rebuke me in Your anger (Psalm 6:1). The Greek has Correct us.

  • v25 "Pour out Your wrath on the nations that do not know You" — Psalm 79:6–7 has the same prayer, and on the kingdoms that do not call on Your name, for they have devoured Jacob and laid waste his homeland; Jeremiah has clans for kingdoms, and doubles the devouring.
