chapters.title: The Words of This Covenant
chapters.html:
Jeremiah 11

1The word that came to Jeremiah from the LORD:

2Hear the words of this covenant, and speak to the men of Judah and to the inhabitants of Jerusalem.

3You shall say to them, This is what the LORD, the God of Israel, says: Cursed is the man who does not obey the words of this covenant,

4which I commanded your fathers in the day I brought them out of the land of Egypt, out of the iron furnace, saying, "Obey My voice, and do all that I command you; so you will be My people, and I will be your God,

5so that I may confirm the oath that I swore to your fathers, to give them a land flowing with milk and honey, as at this day." Then I answered, "Amen, LORD."

6The LORD said to me: Proclaim all these words in the cities of Judah and in the streets of Jerusalem: Hear the words of this covenant and do them.

7For I solemnly warned your fathers on the day I brought them up out of the land of Egypt, and to this day I have warned them again and again, saying, "Obey My voice."

8Yet they did not obey or incline their ear, but each one walked in the stubbornness of his evil heart. So I brought on them all the words of this covenant, which I commanded them to do, but they did not do them.

9The LORD said to me: A conspiracy has been found among the men of Judah and the inhabitants of Jerusalem.

10They have turned back to the iniquities of their forefathers, who refused to hear My words; they have gone after other gods to serve them. The house of Israel and the house of Judah have broken My covenant that I made with their fathers.

11Therefore this is what the LORD says: I am about to bring disaster on them that they will not be able to escape; they will cry to Me, but I will not listen to them.

12Then the cities of Judah and the inhabitants of Jerusalem will go and cry to the gods to whom they burn incense, but they will not save them at all in the time of their trouble.

13For as many as your cities are your gods, Judah; and as many as the streets of Jerusalem are the altars you have set up to the Shame, altars to burn incense to Baal.

14As for you, do not pray for this people, or lift up a cry or a prayer for them, for I will not listen when they call to Me in the time of their trouble.

15What right has My beloved in My house,
when she has done so many vile deeds?
Can holy flesh turn your disaster away from you,
so that you can exult?

16A green olive tree, fair with goodly fruit:
so the LORD named you.
With the roar of a great storm
He has set fire to it,
and its branches are broken.

17The LORD of hosts, who planted you, has pronounced disaster against you, because of the evil that the house of Israel and the house of Judah have done, provoking Me by burning incense to Baal.

18The LORD made it known to me, and I knew;
then You showed me their deeds.

19But I was like a gentle lamb
led to the slaughter;
I did not know it was against me
they devised schemes:
"Let us destroy the tree with its fruit;
let us cut him off from the land of the living,
so that his name will be remembered no more."

20But, LORD of hosts, who judges righteously,
who tests the mind and the heart,
let me see Your vengeance on them,
for to You I have committed my cause.

21Therefore this is what the LORD says concerning the men of Anathoth, who seek your life and say, "Do not prophesy in the name of the LORD, or you will die by our hand" —

22therefore this is what the LORD of hosts says: I am about to punish them; the young men will die by the sword; their sons and their daughters will die by famine;

23and no remnant will be left to them, for I will bring disaster on the men of Anathoth, the year of their punishment.

Notes

  • vv3–5 "Cursed is the man who does not obey the words of this covenant… Then I answered, 'Amen, LORD'" — the last of the curses read at Mount Ebal, Cursed is he who does not uphold the words of this instruction by doing them. All the people shall say, "Amen" (Deuteronomy 27:26). Jeremiah gives the people's answer himself. The Greek has So be it, Lord.

  • v4 "out of the iron furnace" — the words of Deuteronomy 4:20, the LORD has taken you and brought you out of the iron furnace, out of Egypt: Egypt as the furnace where iron is smelted.

  • vv7–8 "I solemnly warned your fathers… but they did not do them" — the Greek does not have these verses except their last words, but they did not do them.

  • v13 "the altars you have set up to the Shame" — la-boshet, the name for Baal given in 3:24; the first line is 2:28, for as many as your cities are your gods, Judah.

  • v15 "What right has My beloved in My house… Can holy flesh turn your disaster away from you?" — the Hebrew of this verse is hard to read: the vile deeds, the many and holy flesh will pass from upon you are rendered by their sense, which is uncertain. The Greek reads vows where the Hebrew has the many: Can vows and holy flesh take away your evils from you? Either way the question is whether sacrifice can buy off the judgment.

  • v16 "A green olive tree… its branches are broken" — the name the LORD gave His people, as the psalmist says, I am like a green olive tree in the house of God (Psalm 52:8). Paul builds on the picture: some of the branches were broken off, and you, a wild olive shoot, were grafted in among them (Romans 11:17).

  • v19 "like a gentle lamb led to the slaughter… let us cut him off from the land of the living" — the words of the servant in Isaiah, like a lamb that is led to the slaughter and cut off from the land of the living (Isaiah 53:7–8). Alluf, "gentle, tame," is the companion of 3:4. Let us destroy the tree with its fruit is lechem, "bread," used of fruit; the Greek reads it Come, let us put wood into his bread.

  • v20 "who tests the mind and the heart" — kelayot va-lev, "kidneys and heart," the inner self: You who test hearts and minds, righteous God (Psalm 7:9). In Revelation the Son of God says, I am He who searches minds and hearts (Revelation 2:23).

  • vv21–23 "the men of Anathoth, who seek your life" — Jeremiah's own town (1:1). No remnant will be left to them; yet when the exiles came home, the list counts the men of Anathoth, one hundred and twenty-eight (Ezra 2:23).

therefore this is what the LORD of hosts says: I am about to punish them; the young men will die by the sword; their sons and their daughters will die by famine;
and no remnant will be left to them, for I will bring disaster on the men of Anathoth, the year of their punishment.

chapters.title: Why Does the Way of the Wicked Prosper?
chapters.html:
Jeremiah 12

1You are righteous, LORD,
when I bring my case to You;
yet I would speak with You about Your judgments:
Why does the way of the wicked prosper?
Why are all who deal treacherously at ease?

2You plant them, and they take root;
they grow and bear fruit;
You are near in their mouth
but far from their hearts.

3But You, LORD, know me;
You see me and test my heart toward You.
Drag them off like sheep for the slaughter,
and set them apart for the day of slaughter.

4How long will the land mourn,
and the grass of every field wither?
Because of the wickedness of those who live in it,
the beasts and the birds are swept away;
for they said, "He will not see our end."

5If you have run with men on foot and they have wearied you,
how will you compete with horses?
If in a land of peace you are secure,
how will you do in the thickets of the Jordan?

6For even your brothers and the house of your father,
even they have dealt treacherously with you;
even they are in full cry after you.
Do not believe them,
though they speak fair words to you.

7I have forsaken My house;
I have abandoned My inheritance;
I have given the beloved of My soul
into the hands of her enemies.

8My inheritance has become to Me
like a lion in the forest;
she has raised her voice against Me;
therefore I hate her.

9Is My inheritance to Me a speckled bird of prey,
with birds of prey against her all around?
Go, gather all the beasts of the field;
bring them to devour.

10Many shepherds have destroyed My vineyard;
they have trampled down My portion;
they have made My pleasant portion
a desolate wilderness.

11They have made it a desolation;
desolate, it mourns to Me;
the whole land is made desolate,
because no man lays it to heart.

12On all the bare heights in the wilderness
destroyers have come,
for the sword of the LORD devours
from one end of the land to the other;
no flesh has peace.

13They have sown wheat and reaped thorns;
they have worn themselves out but profit nothing.
They will be ashamed of their harvests
because of the fierce anger of the LORD.

14This is what the LORD says concerning all My evil neighbors who touch the inheritance that I gave My people Israel to inherit: I am about to uproot them from their land, and I will uproot the house of Judah from among them.

15And it shall come to pass, after I have uprooted them, that I will again have compassion on them, and I will bring them back, each to his inheritance and each to his land.

16If they will diligently learn the ways of My people, to swear by My name, "As the LORD lives," as they taught My people to swear by Baal, then they will be built up among My people.

17But if any nation will not listen, I will utterly uproot that nation and destroy it, declares the LORD.

Notes

  • v1 "You are righteous, LORD, when I bring my case to You… Why does the way of the wicked prosper?" — ariv, the verb of a case at law. The LORD brought His case against the people (2:9); now the prophet brings his against the LORD, and asks the psalmist's question, I saw the prosperity of the wicked (Psalm 73:3).

  • v2 "You are near in their mouth but far from their hearts" — kilyoteihem, "their kidneys," the inner self of 11:20. Isaiah: this people draw near with their mouth and honor Me with their lips, while their heart is far from Me (Isaiah 29:13).

  • v3 "Drag them off like sheep for the slaughter" — the prophet who was like a gentle lamb led to the slaughter (11:19) asks for the same end for his enemies. Set them apart is haqdishem, "make them holy": set aside, like an offering, for the day of slaughter.

  • v5 "If you have run with men on foot… how will you compete with horses?… the thickets of the Jordan" — the LORD does not answer the why; He tells the prophet that worse is coming. Ge'on ha-Yarden, "the pride of the Jordan," is the place from which a lion comes up (49:19; 50:44).

  • v6 "even your brothers and the house of your father" — the men of Anathoth who sought his life (11:21) include his own family.

  • vv7–9 "the beloved of My soul… a speckled bird of prey" — yedidut nafshi, the beloved of 11:15, now handed to her enemies. Ayit, "bird of prey," is the word of Genesis 15:11, The birds of prey came down upon the carcasses. The Greek reads tsavua, "speckled," as "hyena": Is not My inheritance to Me a hyena's cave?

  • vv10–11 "Many shepherds have destroyed My vineyard… desolate, it mourns to Me" — the shepherds are rulers, as at 6:3, and the vineyard is Isaiah's (Isaiah 5:1–7). Shamem, "desolate," comes three times in v11, after desolate wilderness in v10.

  • vv14–17 "I am about to uproot them… they will be built up among My people" — the verbs of Jeremiah's call, to uproot… to build (1:10), turned on the nations. Judah's neighbors are uprooted with Judah, given compassion with Judah, and may be built up among My people if they learn to swear As the LORD lives (4:2).

chapters.title: The Linen Loincloth
chapters.html:
Jeremiah 13

1This is what the LORD said to me: "Go and buy yourself a linen loincloth, and put it around your waist, but do not put it in water."

2So I bought the loincloth as the LORD had said, and put it around my waist.

3The word of the LORD came to me a second time, saying,

4"Take the loincloth that you bought, which is around your waist, and arise, go to the Euphrates, and hide it there in a cleft of the rock."

5So I went and hid it by the Euphrates, as the LORD had commanded me.

6And it came to pass after many days that the LORD said to me, "Arise, go to the Euphrates, and take from there the loincloth that I commanded you to hide there."

7So I went to the Euphrates and dug, and I took the loincloth from the place where I had hidden it; it was ruined, good for nothing.

8Then the word of the LORD came to me, saying,

9"This is what the LORD says: Just so will I ruin the pride of Judah and the great pride of Jerusalem.

10This evil people, who refuse to hear My words, who walk in the stubbornness of their heart and have gone after other gods to serve them and to bow down to them, will be like this loincloth, which is good for nothing.

11For as the loincloth clings to a man's waist, so I made the whole house of Israel and the whole house of Judah cling to Me, declares the LORD, to be for Me a people, a name, a praise and a glory; but they did not listen.

12You shall speak this word to them: This is what the LORD, the God of Israel, says: Every jar is to be filled with wine. They will say to you, 'Do we not know very well that every jar is to be filled with wine?'

13Then you shall say to them, This is what the LORD says: I am about to fill all the inhabitants of this land — the kings who sit on David's throne, the priests, the prophets and all the inhabitants of Jerusalem — with drunkenness.

14I will dash them one against another, fathers and sons together, declares the LORD. I will not pity or spare or have compassion; nothing will keep Me from destroying them."

15Hear and give ear; do not be proud,
for the LORD has spoken.

16Give glory to the LORD your God
before He brings darkness,
before your feet stumble
on the mountains at twilight;
and while you look for light,
He turns it into the shadow of death
and makes it deep darkness.

17But if you will not listen,
my soul will weep in secret for your pride;
my eyes will weep bitterly and run down with tears,
because the LORD's flock has been taken captive.

18Say to the king and to the queen mother:
"Take a lowly seat,
for your beautiful crown
has come down from your heads."

19The cities of the Negev are shut up,
and there is no one to open them;
all Judah is taken into exile,
wholly taken into exile.

20Lift up your eyes and see
those who come from the north.
Where is the flock that was given to you,
your beautiful flock?

21What will you say when He sets over you as head
those you yourself taught to be your friends?
Will not pangs take hold of you,
like a woman in labor?

22If you say in your heart,
"Why have these things come upon me?" —
for the greatness of your iniquity
your skirts are lifted
and you are violated.

23Can the Cushite change his skin,
or the leopard his spots?
Then you also can do good,
who are accustomed to doing evil.

24I will scatter them like chaff
driven by the wind of the desert.

25This is your lot,
the portion I have measured out to you,
declares the LORD,
because you have forgotten Me
and trusted in falsehood.

26I Myself will lift up your skirts over your face,
and your shame will be seen.

27Your adulteries and your neighings,
your lewd prostitution,
on the hills in the field —
I have seen your loathsome things.
Woe to you, Jerusalem!
You will not be made clean —
how long yet?

Notes

  • vv1–7 "a linen loincloth… go to the Euphrates, and hide it" — ezor pishtim, a waistcloth of linen, the cloth of the priests' holy garments (linen undergarments… a linen sash, Leviticus 16:4), worn by a priest's son (1:1). Perat is the Euphrates, the river of Eden (Genesis 2:14), and the river into which the scroll against Babylon is thrown at the end of the book (51:63); the Greek has the Euphrates. Buried there, unwashed, the cloth rots.

  • v11 "as the loincloth clings to a man's waist, so I made the whole house of Israel… cling to Me… to be for Me a people, a name, a praise and a glory" — davaq, the word of Genesis 2:24, a man… clings to his woman, and of the command to Him you shall hold fast (Deuteronomy 10:20). A name, a praise and a glory is the promise of Deuteronomy 26:19, for praise and for a name and for glory.

  • vv12–14 "Every jar is to be filled with wine… I will dash them one against another" — a saying so plain the people mock it, and the LORD gives it its meaning: the jars are the people, the wine is drunkenness, and full jars knocked together break.

  • v18 "Say to the king and to the queen mother" — ha-gevirah, the king's mother. Jehoiachin went out to the king of Babylon he and his mother (2 Kings 24:12, 15), and Jeremiah's letter to the exiles names Jeconiah the king and the queen mother (29:2).

  • v23 "Can the Cushite change his skin, or the leopard his spots?" — kushi, a man of Cush. Moses married a Cushite woman (Numbers 12:1), and in this book it is Ebed-melech the Cushite who hears that Jeremiah has been thrown into the cistern and pulls him out (38:7–13).

  • vv22, 26 "your skirts are lifted… I Myself will lift up your skirts over your face" — the shaming of a woman taken in adultery; Nahum says the same words to Nineveh, I will lift up your skirts over your face (Nahum 3:5). In v22 the Hebrew says your heels suffer violence.

chapters.title: The Drought
chapters.html:
Jeremiah 14

1The word of the LORD that came to Jeremiah concerning the drought:

2Judah mourns,
and her gates languish;
they sit in black on the ground,
and the cry of Jerusalem goes up.

3Their nobles send their servants for water;
they come to the cisterns;
they find no water;
they return with their jars empty;
they are ashamed and dismayed,
and cover their heads.

4Because of the ground, which is cracked,
for there has been no rain in the land,
the farmers are ashamed;
they cover their heads.

5Even the doe in the field
gives birth and abandons her fawn,
because there is no grass.

6The wild donkeys stand on the bare heights;
they pant for air like jackals;
their eyes fail
because there is no vegetation.

7Though our iniquities testify against us,
act, LORD, for Your name's sake;
for our faithlessness is great;
we have sinned against You.

8Hope of Israel,
its Savior in time of trouble,
why should You be like a guest in the land,
like a traveler who turns aside to lodge for a night?

9Why should You be like a man dismayed,
like a mighty man who cannot save?
Yet You, LORD, are in our midst,
and we are called by Your name;
do not leave us.

10This is what the LORD says to this people:
They have loved to wander like this;
they have not restrained their feet;
so the LORD does not accept them;
now He will remember their iniquity
and punish their sins.

11The LORD said to me: "Do not pray for the good of this people.

12Though they fast, I will not hear their cry; and though they offer burnt offering and grain offering, I will not accept them; but I will consume them by the sword, by famine and by pestilence."

13Then I said, "Ah, Lord GOD! The prophets are telling them, 'You will not see the sword, and you will not have famine; but I will give you true peace in this place.'"

14The LORD said to me: "The prophets are prophesying lies in My name. I did not send them, or command them, or speak to them. They are prophesying to you a lying vision, divination, a worthless thing and the deceit of their own hearts.

15Therefore this is what the LORD says concerning the prophets who prophesy in My name although I did not send them, and who say, 'Sword and famine will not come on this land': By sword and famine those prophets will be consumed.

16The people to whom they prophesy will be thrown out into the streets of Jerusalem because of famine and sword, with no one to bury them — them, their wives, their sons and their daughters; for I will pour out their evil on them.

17You shall say this word to them:
'Let my eyes run down with tears
night and day, and let them not cease,
for the virgin daughter of my people
is broken with a great breaking,
with a very grievous wound.

18If I go out into the field,
there are those slain by the sword!
If I enter the city,
there are the diseases of famine!
For both prophet and priest
go about in a land they do not know.'"

19Have You utterly rejected Judah?
Does Your soul loathe Zion?
Why have You struck us down
so that there is no healing for us?
We hoped for peace, but no good came;
for a time of healing, but there is terror.

20We acknowledge our wickedness, LORD,
the iniquity of our fathers,
for we have sinned against You.

21Do not spurn us, for Your name's sake;
do not dishonor Your glorious throne;
remember, do not break Your covenant with us.

22Are there any among the emptinesses of the nations who bring rain?
Or can the heavens give showers?
Are You not He, LORD our God?
We hope in You,
for You have made all these things.

Notes

  • vv3–4 "they cover their heads" — the sign of grief and shame: David went up the Mount of Olives with his head covered, and all the people who were with him covered their heads (2 Samuel 15:30).

  • v8 "why should You be like a guest in the land" — ger, the word the law uses for the foreigner who lives among Israel, The guest living with you shall be to you as a native among you (Leviticus 19:34). The people ask why the LORD acts like a stranger passing through His own land. The Greek has a sojourner.

  • v10 "now He will remember their iniquity and punish their sins" — the words of Hosea 8:13, said there of the northern kingdom's sacrifices: the LORD does not accept them; now He will remember their iniquity and punish their sins.

  • vv11–12 "Do not pray for the good of this people… by the sword, by famine and by pestilence" — the third time the prophet is told not to pray (7:16; 11:14). The sword, famine and pestilence is a triad that runs through the book (21:9; 27:8; 29:18; 38:2; 44:13), first here.

  • vv13–15 "The prophets are prophesying lies in My name. I did not send them" — the law of the false prophet, the prophet who presumes to speak a word in My name that I have not commanded him to speak… that prophet shall die (Deuteronomy 18:20). They promised that sword and famine would not come; by sword and famine they will die.

  • v19 "We hoped for peace, but no good came; for a time of healing, but there is terror" — the words of 8:15, said again.

  • v21 "do not dishonor Your glorious throne" — kisse khevodekha. Jerusalem is the throne of the LORD (3:17), and the sanctuary a glorious throne, on high from the beginning (17:12).

  • v22 "Are there any among the emptinesses of the nations who bring rain?" — havlei ha-goyim, the emptiness (hevel) of 2:5 and 10:15, the idols. The LORD is the One who gives the rain in its season (5:24) and makes lightning for the rain (10:13).

chapters.title: Your Words Were Found, and I Ate Them
chapters.html:
Jeremiah 15

1Then the LORD said to me: "Even if Moses and Samuel stood before Me, My heart would not turn toward this people. Send them away from My presence, and let them go!

2And it shall come to pass, when they say to you, 'Where shall we go?' that you shall say to them, 'This is what the LORD says:
Those who are for death, to death;
those who are for the sword, to the sword;
those who are for famine, to famine;
and those who are for captivity, to captivity.'

3I will appoint over them four kinds of destroyers, declares the LORD: the sword to kill, the dogs to drag away, and the birds of the heavens and the beasts of the earth to devour and destroy.

4I will make them a horror to all the kingdoms of the earth because of Manasseh son of Hezekiah, king of Judah, for what he did in Jerusalem.

5Who will have pity on you, Jerusalem?
Who will mourn for you?
Who will turn aside
to ask about your welfare?

6You have rejected Me, declares the LORD;
you keep going backward;
so I have stretched out My hand against you and destroyed you;
I am weary of relenting.

7I have winnowed them with a winnowing fork
in the gates of the land;
I have bereaved them; I have destroyed My people;
they did not turn from their ways.

8Their widows have become more numerous before Me
than the sand of the seas;
I have brought against the mothers of young men
a destroyer at noonday;
I have made anguish and terror
fall on them suddenly.

9She who bore seven languishes;
she has breathed out her soul;
her sun has gone down while it was still day;
she is shamed and disgraced.
The rest of them I will give to the sword
before their enemies,
declares the LORD."

10Woe is me, my mother, that you bore me,
a man of strife and contention to the whole land!
I have not lent, nor have they lent to me,
yet every one of them curses me.

11The LORD said: Surely I will set you free for good;
surely I will make the enemy plead with you
in the time of disaster and the time of distress.

12Can one break iron,
iron from the north, and bronze?

13Your wealth and your treasures
I will give as plunder, without price,
for all your sins,
throughout all your territory.

14I will make you serve your enemies
in a land you do not know;
for a fire is kindled in My anger;
it will burn against you.

15You know, LORD;
remember me and visit me,
and avenge me on my persecutors.
In Your slowness to anger do not take me away;
know that for Your sake I bear reproach.

16Your words were found, and I ate them,
and Your word became to me a joy
and the delight of my heart;
for I am called by Your name,
LORD God of hosts.

17I did not sit in the company of revelers,
nor did I rejoice;
because of Your hand I sat alone,
for You had filled me with indignation.

18Why is my pain unending,
my wound incurable,
refusing to be healed?
Will You be to me like a deceitful brook,
like waters that fail?

19Therefore this is what the LORD says:
If you return, I will restore you,
and you shall stand before Me;
if you bring out what is precious from what is worthless,
you shall be as My mouth.
They shall turn to you,
but you shall not turn to them.

20I will make you to this people
a fortified wall of bronze;
they will fight against you,
but they will not overcome you,
for I am with you to save you and deliver you,
declares the LORD.

21I will deliver you out of the hand of the wicked,
and redeem you from the grasp of the ruthless.

Notes

  • v1 "Even if Moses and Samuel stood before Me" — the two great intercessors. Moses pleaded with the LORD his God after the golden calf (Exodus 32:11), and Samuel said, far be it from me that I should sin against the LORD by ceasing to pray for you (1 Samuel 12:23); the psalm names them together, Moses and Aaron were among His priests, Samuel among those who called on His name (Psalm 99:6).

  • v2 "Those who are for death, to death… for captivity, to captivity" — Revelation takes up the words: If anyone is for captivity, into captivity he goes; if anyone is to be killed with the sword, with the sword he must be killed (Revelation 13:10).

  • v4 "a horror to all the kingdoms of the earth because of Manasseh" — the curse of Deuteronomy 28:25, you will be a horror to all the kingdoms of the earth, and the reason the book of Kings gives for the fall, for the sins of Manasseh, according to all that he had done (2 Kings 24:3).

  • vv8–9 "more numerous… than the sand of the seas… She who bore seven languishes" — the measure of the promise to Abraham, as the sand that is on the lip of the sea (Genesis 22:17), now counts widows. Hannah sang, The barren has borne seven, and she who has many children languishes (1 Samuel 2:5); here the mother of seven languishes, the same verb, and her sun goes down at noon.

  • vv11–12 "Surely I will set you free for good… Can one break iron, iron from the north, and bronze?" — both verses are hard in the Hebrew. Sheritikha, "I will set you free," is the read form; the written form sherotikha is uncertain, and the Greek has So be it, Master. Iron from the north is the enemy of 1:14, or the prophet made an iron pillar and bronze walls (1:18); the verse does not say which.

  • vv13–14 "Your wealth and your treasures I will give as plunder… I will make you serve your enemies" — these lines come again in 17:3–4, where the Hebrew has I will make you serve your enemies in a land you do not know. Here the Hebrew has ha'avarti, "I will make pass," one letter from ha'avadti, "I will make serve"; the text follows 17:4 and the Greek, which has serve here as well. It is the curse of the covenant, you will serve your enemies (Deuteronomy 28:48).

  • v15 "In Your slowness to anger do not take me away" — le-erekh appekha, the LORD's name proclaimed to Moses, slow to anger, and abundant in loyal love (Exodus 34:6). The prophet asks that the patience shown to his enemies not cost him his life.

  • v16 "Your words were found, and I ate them" — Ezekiel is given a scroll to eat, and it was in my mouth as sweet as honey (Ezekiel 3:3), and so is John (Revelation 10:10). In Josiah's reign the high priest Hilkiah said, I have found the book of the instruction in the house of the LORD (2 Kings 22:8); Jeremiah's father bore the name Hilkiah (1:1), and nothing in the text says whether they were the same man.

  • v18 "like a deceitful brook, like waters that fail" — akhzav, a stream that runs dry when it is needed. The LORD called Himself the fountain of living waters (2:13); the prophet asks whether He has become the opposite.

  • v19 "If you return… you shall stand before Me… you shall be as My mouth" — shuv four times: If you return, I will restore you… They shall turn to you, but you shall not turn to them. Stand before Me is the prophet's service, as Elijah said, the LORD, the God of Israel… before whom I stand (1 Kings 17:1); as My mouth is what Aaron was to Moses, he will be a mouth for you (Exodus 4:16).

speech.text: Jeremiah 15
Then the LORD said to me: "Even if Moses and Samuel stood before Me, My heart would not turn toward this people. Send them away from My presence, and let them go!

And it shall come to pass, when they say to you, 'Where shall we go?' that you shall say to them, 'This is what the LORD says: Those who are for death, to death; those who are for the sword, to the sword; those who are for famine, to famine; and those who are for captivity, to captivity.'
I will appoint over them four kinds of destroyers, declares the LORD: the sword to kill, the dogs to drag away, and the birds of the heavens and the beasts of the earth to devour and destroy.
I will make them a horror to all the kingdoms of the earth because of Manasseh son of Hezekiah, king of Judah, for what he did in Jerusalem.
Who will have pity on you, Jerusalem? Who will mourn for you? Who will turn aside to ask about your welfare?
You have rejected Me, declares the LORD; you keep going backward; so I have stretched out My hand against you and destroyed you; I am weary of relenting.
I have winnowed them with a winnowing fork in the gates of the land; I have bereaved them; I have destroyed My people; they did not turn from their ways.

Their widows have become more numerous before Me than the sand of the seas; I have brought against the mothers of young men a destroyer at noonday; I have made anguish and terror fall on them suddenly.

She who bore seven languishes; she has breathed out her soul; her sun has gone down while it was still day; she is shamed and disgraced. The rest of them I will give to the sword before their enemies, declares the LORD."
Woe is me, my mother, that you bore me, a man of strife and contention to the whole land! I have not lent, nor have they lent to me, yet every one of them curses me.
The LORD said: Surely I will set you free for good; surely I will make the enemy plead with you in the time of disaster and the time of distress.
Can one break iron, iron from the north, and bronze?
Your wealth and your treasures I will give as plunder, without price, for all your sins, throughout all your territory.
I will make you serve your enemies in a land you do not know; for a fire is kindled in My anger; it will burn against you.
You know, LORD; remember me and visit me, and avenge me on my persecutors. In Your slowness to anger do not take me away; know that for Your sake I bear reproach.
Your words were found, and I ate them, and Your word became to me a joy and the delight of my heart; for I am called by Your name, LORD God of hosts.
I did not sit in the company of revelers, nor did I rejoice; because of Your hand I sat alone, for You had filled me with indignation.
Why is my pain unending, my wound incurable, refusing to be healed? Will You be to me like a deceitful brook, like waters that fail?

Therefore this is what the LORD says: If you return, I will restore you, and you shall stand before Me; if you bring out what is precious from what is worthless, you shall be as My mouth. They shall turn to you, but you shall not turn to them.
I will make you to this people a fortified wall of bronze; they will fight against you, but they will not overcome you, for I am with you to save you and deliver you, declares the LORD.
I will deliver you out of the hand of the wicked, and redeem you from the grasp of the ruthless.

chapters.title: No Wife, No Mourning, No Feasting
chapters.html:
Jeremiah 16

1The word of the LORD came to me, saying,

2"You shall not take a wife, and you shall not have sons or daughters in this place.

3For this is what the LORD says concerning the sons and daughters who are born in this place, and concerning the mothers who bear them and the fathers who father them in this land:

4They will die of deadly diseases. They will not be mourned or buried; they will be dung on the face of the ground. They will be consumed by the sword and by famine, and their corpses will be food for the birds of the heavens and for the beasts of the earth.

5For this is what the LORD says: Do not enter the house of mourning, or go to lament, or grieve for them; for I have taken away My peace from this people, declares the LORD, My loyal love and My compassion.

6Great and small will die in this land; they will not be buried, and no one will lament for them, or gash himself, or shave his head for them.

7No one will break bread for the mourner to comfort him for the dead, or give him the cup of consolation to drink for his father or his mother.

8You shall not go into the house of feasting to sit with them, to eat and drink.

9For this is what the LORD of hosts, the God of Israel, says: I am about to silence from this place, before your eyes and in your days, the voice of mirth and the voice of gladness, the voice of the bridegroom and the voice of the bride.

10And it shall come to pass, when you tell this people all these words, and they say to you, 'Why has the LORD pronounced all this great disaster against us? What is our iniquity? What is the sin that we have committed against the LORD our God?'

11that you shall say to them: 'Because your fathers have forsaken Me, declares the LORD, and have gone after other gods and served them and bowed down to them, and have forsaken Me and not kept My law;

12and you have done worse than your fathers, for each of you walks after the stubbornness of his evil heart, refusing to listen to Me.

13So I will hurl you out of this land into a land that neither you nor your fathers have known, and there you will serve other gods day and night, for I will show you no favor.'

14Therefore, days are coming, declares the LORD, when it will no longer be said, 'As the LORD lives, who brought up the sons of Israel out of the land of Egypt,'

15but, 'As the LORD lives, who brought up the sons of Israel out of the land of the north and out of all the lands where He had driven them.' For I will bring them back to their land that I gave to their fathers.

16I am about to send for many fishers, declares the LORD, and they will fish for them; and afterward I will send for many hunters, and they will hunt them from every mountain and every hill and out of the clefts of the rocks.

17For My eyes are on all their ways; they are not hidden from Me, nor is their iniquity concealed from My eyes.

18I will first repay double for their iniquity and their sin, because they have polluted My land with the carcasses of their loathsome things and have filled My inheritance with their detestable things."

19LORD, my strength and my stronghold,
my refuge in the day of trouble,
to You the nations will come
from the ends of the earth and say:
"Our fathers have inherited nothing but lies,
emptiness in which there is no profit.

20Can a man make gods for himself?
Such are not gods!"

21"Therefore I am about to make them know;
this time I will make them know
My hand and My might,
and they will know that My name is the LORD."

Notes

  • v2 "You shall not take a wife" — Hosea was told, Go, take for yourself a wife (Hosea 1:2), and Ezekiel was forbidden to mourn the wife who died (Ezekiel 24:16). Jeremiah is told to have no wife and no children at all: the prophet's own house is the message.

  • v5 "the house of mourning… My loyal love and My compassion" — beit marzeach, here a house of mourning; the word is found elsewhere only in Amos 6:7, of a feast, the revelry of those who sprawl. What the LORD takes away is named: My peace… My loyal love (chesed) and My compassion.

  • v6 "or gash himself, or shave his head for them" — the rites of grief the law forbade, You shall not gash yourselves or make a bald patch between your eyes for the dead (Deuteronomy 14:1). Even these will not be done.

  • v9 "the voice of the bridegroom and the voice of the bride" — the silence of 7:34, now before your eyes and in your days.

  • v13 "there you will serve other gods day and night" — the curse of Deuteronomy 28:64, there you will serve other gods that neither you nor your fathers have known, wood and stone.

  • vv14–15 "no longer… out of the land of Egypt, but… out of the land of the north" — the oath by the LORD who brought Israel out of Egypt will give way to an oath by the LORD who brought them back from exile, a second exodus greater than the first. The two verses come again in 23:7–8.

  • v16 "I am about to send for many fishers… and afterward… many hunters" — dayyagim, "fishers," is the read form; the written form is dugim, "fish." Here the fishers and hunters gather people for judgment, and none can hide (v17). Jesus uses the same picture for His call: Come, follow Me, and I will make you fishers of people (Matthew 4:19).

  • v18 "I will first repay double… the carcasses of their loathsome things" — mishneh, "double," the word Isaiah uses when the debt is paid, she has received from the LORD's hand double for all her sins (Isaiah 40:2). The idols are called carcasses, as the covenant curse called them corpses: I will… throw your corpses on the corpses of your idols (Leviticus 26:30).

  • v21 "they will know that My name is the LORD" — ki shemi YHWH, as in Isaiah 42:8, I am the LORD; that is My name.

chapters.title: Written on the Tablet of Their Heart
chapters.html:
Jeremiah 17

1The sin of Judah is written with a pen of iron;
with a point of diamond it is engraved
on the tablet of their heart
and on the horns of your altars,

2while their children remember their altars
and their Asherim beside the green trees,
on the high hills,

3My mountain in the open country.
Your wealth and all your treasures
I will give as plunder,
your high places, for sin,
throughout all your territory.

4You will let go, through your own fault,
of your inheritance that I gave you,
and I will make you serve your enemies
in a land you do not know;
for you have kindled a fire in My anger
that will burn forever.

5This is what the LORD says:
Cursed is the man who trusts in man
and makes flesh his arm,
whose heart turns away from the LORD.

6He will be like a shrub in the desert,
and will not see when good comes;
he will live in parched places in the wilderness,
in a salt land where no one lives.

7Blessed is the man who trusts in the LORD,
whose trust is the LORD.

8He will be like a tree planted by water,
that sends out its roots by the stream,
and does not see when heat comes;
its leaves stay green,
and in the year of drought it is not anxious,
and it does not cease to bear fruit.

9The heart is more deceitful than all else,
and desperately sick;
who can understand it?

10I the LORD search the heart
and test the mind,
to give to each man according to his ways,
according to the fruit of his deeds.

11Like a partridge that hatches eggs it did not lay
is he who gets riches, but not by justice;
in the middle of his days they will leave him,
and at his end he will be a fool.

12A glorious throne, on high from the beginning,
is the place of our sanctuary.

13Hope of Israel, LORD,
all who forsake You will be put to shame;
those who turn away from Me will be written in the earth,
for they have forsaken the LORD,
the fountain of living waters.

14Heal me, LORD, and I shall be healed;
save me, and I shall be saved;
for You are my praise.

15They keep saying to me,
"Where is the word of the LORD?
Let it come!"

16But I have not run away from being a shepherd after You,
nor have I longed for the day of disaster;
You know;
what came out of my lips
was before Your face.

17Do not be a terror to me;
You are my refuge in the day of disaster.

18Let my persecutors be put to shame,
but let me not be put to shame;
let them be dismayed,
but let me not be dismayed;
bring on them the day of disaster;
destroy them with double destruction.

The Sabbath

19This is what the LORD said to me: Go and stand in the gate of the sons of the people, by which the kings of Judah enter and by which they go out, and in all the gates of Jerusalem,

20and say to them: Hear the word of the LORD, kings of Judah, and all Judah, and all the inhabitants of Jerusalem who enter by these gates.

21This is what the LORD says: Take care, for your lives' sake, and do not carry a load on the sabbath day or bring it in by the gates of Jerusalem.

22Do not carry a load out of your houses on the sabbath day or do any work, but keep the sabbath day holy, as I commanded your fathers.

23Yet they did not listen or incline their ear, but stiffened their neck so as not to hear or take correction.

24If you diligently listen to Me, declares the LORD, and bring no load in through the gates of this city on the sabbath day, but keep the sabbath day holy and do no work on it,

25then there will enter by the gates of this city kings and princes who sit on the throne of David, riding in chariots and on horses, they and their princes, the men of Judah and the inhabitants of Jerusalem; and this city will be inhabited forever.

26People will come from the cities of Judah and from around Jerusalem, from the land of Benjamin, from the lowland, from the hill country and from the Negev, bringing burnt offerings and sacrifices, grain offerings and frankincense, and bringing thank offerings to the house of the LORD.

27But if you do not listen to Me, to keep the sabbath day holy and not to carry a load as you enter the gates of Jerusalem on the sabbath day, I will kindle a fire in its gates, and it will devour the palaces of Jerusalem and will not be quenched.

Notes

  • vv1–4 "written with a pen of iron… on the tablet of their heart" — the covenant was given on tablets of stone, written by the finger of God (Exodus 31:18); Judah's sin is cut into the tablet of the heart. The new covenant answers it in the same words: I will put My law within them, and on their heart I will write it (31:33). The Greek does not have vv1–4.

  • v4 "You will let go… of your inheritance… I will make you serve your enemies" — shamat, the verb of the seventh year, The seventh you shall let go and leave it (Exodus 23:11), and of the LORD's release (Deuteronomy 15:2). What Israel did not let go, it will lose: the Chronicler says the exile lasted until the land had been paid its sabbaths (2 Chronicles 36:21). The last lines repeat 15:13–14.

  • vv5–8 "Cursed is the man who trusts in man… Blessed is the man who trusts in the LORD… like a tree planted by water" — the two ways of Psalm 1, where the righteous man will be like a tree planted by streams of water… its leaf does not wither (Psalm 1:3). Does not see when heat comes is the read form, yir'eh, matching will not see when good comes in v6; the written form is yira, "does not fear."

  • v9 "The heart is more deceitful than all else" — aqov, the root of Jacob's name, as at 9:4, every brother is a supplanter. The Greek reads the line otherwise: The heart is deep above all things, and it is man; who can know him?

  • v11 "Like a partridge that hatches eggs it did not lay" — qore, the bird David named when Saul hunted him, as one hunts a partridge in the mountains (1 Samuel 26:20). Wealth gathered unjustly is a brood not one's own: it leaves.

  • v13 "those who turn away from Me will be written in the earth… the fountain of living waters" — the charge of 2:13, they have forsaken Me, the fountain of living waters, now in the prophet's own prayer.

  • v16 "I have not run away from being a shepherd after You" — me-ro'eh acharekha; the sense of the line is uncertain. The Greek has I have not grown weary following after You.

  • vv19–27 "keep the sabbath day holy, as I commanded your fathers" — the words of the commandment, Keep the sabbath day, to keep it holy, as the LORD your God commanded you (Deuteronomy 5:12). After the exile Nehemiah shut the gates against the sabbath trade and said, Did not your fathers act in this way, and did not our God bring all this evil on us and on this city? (Nehemiah 13:18). I will kindle a fire in its gates, and it will devour the palaces of Jerusalem is Amos's word against Judah (Amos 2:5).

chapters.title: The Potter's House
chapters.html:
Jeremiah 18

1The word that came to Jeremiah from the LORD:

2"Arise, and go down to the potter's house, and there I will let you hear My words."

3So I went down to the potter's house, and he was working at the wheel.

4Whenever the pot he was making of clay was spoiled in the potter's hand, he would make it again into another pot, as it seemed good to the potter to make.

5Then the word of the LORD came to me, saying,

6"Can I not do with you as this potter has done, house of Israel? declares the LORD. Like the clay in the potter's hand, so are you in My hand, house of Israel.

7At one moment I may speak concerning a nation or a kingdom, to uproot it, to pull it down and to destroy it;

8but if that nation, against which I have spoken, turns from its evil, I will relent of the disaster that I intended to do to it.

9At another moment I may speak concerning a nation or a kingdom, to build and to plant it;

10but if it does what is evil in My eyes, not listening to My voice, I will relent of the good that I had said I would do for it.

11So now, say to the men of Judah and to the inhabitants of Jerusalem: This is what the LORD says: I am about to shape disaster against you and devise a plan against you. Return, each of you, from his evil way, and amend your ways and your deeds."

12But they say, "It is hopeless! We will follow our own plans, and each of us will act according to the stubbornness of his evil heart."

13Therefore this is what the LORD says:
Ask among the nations:
Who has heard such things?
The virgin Israel
has done a very horrible thing.

14Does the snow of Lebanon
leave the rock of the field?
Do the cold flowing waters from afar
run dry?

15But My people have forgotten Me;
they burn incense to emptiness;
they have been made to stumble in their ways,
in the ancient paths,
to walk in side tracks,
on a road not built up,

16making their land a horror,
a thing to be hissed at forever;
everyone who passes by it is horrified
and shakes his head.

17Like the east wind
I will scatter them before the enemy;
I will show them My back and not My face
in the day of their disaster.

18Then they said, "Come, let us devise plans against Jeremiah, for the law will not perish from the priest, nor counsel from the wise, nor the word from the prophet. Come, let us strike him with the tongue, and let us pay no attention to any of his words."

19Pay attention to me, LORD,
and listen to the voice of those who contend with me.

20Should evil be repaid for good?
Yet they have dug a pit for my life.
Remember how I stood before You
to speak good for them,
to turn Your wrath away from them.

21Therefore give their children over to famine;
hand them over to the power of the sword;
let their wives be bereaved of children and widowed;
let their men be slain by death,
their young men struck down by the sword in battle.

22Let a cry be heard from their houses,
when You suddenly bring raiders upon them;
for they have dug a pit to take me,
and hidden snares for my feet.

23Yet You, LORD, know
all their plotting against me to kill me.
Do not atone for their iniquity,
and do not blot out their sin from before You;
let them be overthrown before You;
deal with them in the time of Your anger.

Notes

  • v3 "he was working at the wheel" — al ha-ovnayim, "on the two stones." The same word names the birthstool in Exodus 1:16, look at the two stones: the place where a pot is shaped and the place where a child is born.

  • vv4, 6 "he would make it again into another pot… Like the clay in the potter's hand, so are you in My hand" — the picture of Isaiah, we are the clay, and You are our potter (Isaiah 64:8; also 29:16; 45:9). Paul asks, Has the potter no right over the clay, to make from the same lump one vessel for honor and another for dishonor? (Romans 9:21). Here the potter remakes a spoiled pot, and vv7–10 say the clay's turning changes what he makes.

  • vv7–10 "to uproot it, to pull it down… to build and to plant… I will relent" — the verbs of Jeremiah's call (1:10). When Nineveh turned, God relented of the disaster that He had said He would do to them (Jonah 3:10).

  • v11 "I am about to shape disaster against you" — yotser, the word for the potter in vv2–6: the LORD speaks as the potter, and what He is shaping is disaster. Return is shuvu, the call of chapter 3.

  • v15 "in the ancient paths" — shevilei olam, the ancient paths the people were told to ask for (6:16, netivot olam); they stumble in them and leave them for side tracks.

  • v17 "I will show them My back and not My face" — oref ve-lo fanim ar'em, the letters read with the vowels of "I will show them," as the Greek reads them (I will show them, though the Greek goes on the day of their destruction). The Hebrew vowels give er'em, "I will see them": I will look on their backs and not their faces. The people turned their backs to Me, and not their faces (2:27), and the LORD gives them the same. Moses was shown only the LORD's back: you will see My back. But My face will not be seen (Exodus 33:23).

  • v18 "the law will not perish from the priest, nor counsel from the wise, nor the word from the prophet" — three offices, three gifts. Ezekiel turns the saying around: they will seek a vision from a prophet, but the law will perish from the priest, and counsel from the elders (Ezekiel 7:26).

  • vv20, 22 "Remember how I stood before You… to turn Your wrath away from them… they have dug a pit" — what Moses did, who stood in the breach before Him to turn away His wrath (Psalm 106:23), and what the LORD would no longer accept even from him (15:1). Shuchah, "a pit," in both verses; in v22 it is the read form, and the written form is sichah.

  • v23 "Do not atone for their iniquity, and do not blot out their sin from before You" — al tekhapper, the verb of atonement. Nehemiah prayed the same against his enemies: Do not cover their iniquity, and do not let their sin be blotted out from before You (Nehemiah 4:5).

speech.text: Jeremiah 18
The word that came to Jeremiah from the LORD:
"Arise, and go down to the potter's house, and there I will let you hear My words."
So I went down to the potter's house, and he was working at the wheel.
Whenever the pot he was making of clay was spoiled in the potter's hand, he would make it again into another pot, as it seemed good to the potter to make.
Then the word of the LORD came to me, saying,
"Can I not do with you as this potter has done, house of Israel? declares the LORD. Like the clay in the potter's hand, so are you in My hand, house of Israel.
At one moment I may speak concerning a nation or a kingdom, to uproot it, to pull it down and to destroy it;
but if that nation, against which I have spoken, turns from its evil, I will relent of the disaster that I intended to do to it.
At another moment I may speak concerning a nation or a kingdom, to build and to plant it;
but if it does what is evil in My eyes, not listening to My voice, I will relent of the good that I had said I would do for it.

So now, say to the men of Judah and to the inhabitants of Jerusalem: This is what the LORD says: I am about to shape disaster against you and devise a plan against you. Return, each of you, from his evil way, and amend your ways and your deeds."
But they say, "It is hopeless! We will follow our own plans, and each of us will act according to the stubbornness of his evil heart."
Therefore this is what the LORD says: Ask among the nations: Who has heard such things? The virgin Israel has done a very horrible thing.
Does the snow of Lebanon leave the rock of the field? Do the cold flowing waters from afar run dry?
But My people have forgotten Me; they burn incense to emptiness; they have been made to stumble in their ways, in the ancient paths, to walk in side tracks, on a road not built up,
making their land a horror, a thing to be hissed at forever; everyone who passes by it is horrified and shakes his head.
Like the east wind I will scatter them before the enemy; I will show them My back and not My face in the day of their disaster.

Then they said, "Come, let us devise plans against Jeremiah, for the law will not perish from the priest, nor counsel from the wise, nor the word from the prophet. Come, let us strike him with the tongue, and let us pay no attention to any of his words."
Pay attention to me, LORD, and listen to the voice of those who contend with me.
Should evil be repaid for good? Yet they have dug a pit for my life. Remember how I stood before You to speak good for them, to turn Your wrath away from them.

Therefore give their children over to famine; hand them over to the power of the sword; let their wives be bereaved of children and widowed; let their men be slain by death, their young men struck down by the sword in battle.
Let a cry be heard from their houses, when You suddenly bring raiders upon them; for they have dug a pit to take me, and hidden snares for my feet.

Yet You, LORD, know all their plotting against me to kill me. Do not atone for their iniquity, and do not blot out their sin from before You; let them be overthrown before You; deal with them in the time of Your anger.

chapters.title: The Broken Flask
chapters.html:
Jeremiah 19

1This is what the LORD says: Go and buy a potter's earthenware flask, and take some of the elders of the people and some of the elders of the priests,

2and go out to the Valley of the Son of Hinnom, at the entrance of the Potsherd Gate, and proclaim there the words that I will speak to you.

3Say: Hear the word of the LORD, kings of Judah and inhabitants of Jerusalem. This is what the LORD of hosts, the God of Israel, says: I am about to bring disaster on this place, so that the ears of everyone who hears of it will tingle,

4because they have forsaken Me and made this place foreign, and have burned incense in it to other gods whom neither they nor their fathers nor the kings of Judah have known; and they have filled this place with the blood of the innocent,

5and have built the high places of Baal to burn their sons in the fire as burnt offerings to Baal, which I did not command or speak, nor did it come into My mind.

6Therefore, days are coming, declares the LORD, when this place will no longer be called Topheth or the Valley of the Son of Hinnom, but the Valley of Slaughter.

7In this place I will make void the plans of Judah and Jerusalem; I will make them fall by the sword before their enemies and by the hand of those who seek their life; and I will give their corpses as food to the birds of the heavens and to the beasts of the earth.

8I will make this city a horror and a thing to be hissed at; everyone who passes by it will be horrified and will hiss because of all its wounds.

9I will make them eat the flesh of their sons and the flesh of their daughters, and each will eat the flesh of his neighbor, in the siege and in the distress with which their enemies and those who seek their life will distress them.

10Then you shall break the flask before the eyes of the men who go with you,

11and say to them: This is what the LORD of hosts says: So will I break this people and this city, as one breaks a potter's jar so that it can never be mended. They will bury in Topheth because there is no other place to bury.

12This is what I will do to this place, declares the LORD, and to its inhabitants, making this city like Topheth.

13The houses of Jerusalem and the houses of the kings of Judah will be unclean like the place of Topheth — all the houses on whose roofs they burned incense to all the host of heaven and poured out drink offerings to other gods.

14Then Jeremiah came from Topheth, where the LORD had sent him to prophesy, and he stood in the court of the LORD's house and said to all the people,

15"This is what the LORD of hosts, the God of Israel, says: I am about to bring on this city and on all its towns all the disaster that I have pronounced against it, because they have stiffened their neck, refusing to hear My words."

Notes

  • vv1, 7, 10 "a potter's earthenware flask… I will make void the plans… break the flask" — baqbuq, "flask," and u-vaqqoti, "I will make void," from baqaq, the verb of The LORD is about to empty the earth (Isaiah 24:1): the same letters. Where the flask is broken, the LORD empties out Judah's plans.

  • v2 "the Potsherd Gate" — sha'ar ha-charsit, the read form; the written form is ha-charsot. Cheres, "earthenware," is the flask of v1: the gate of broken pots.

  • v3 "the ears of everyone who hears of it will tingle" — the words spoken to Samuel against the house of Eli at Shiloh, both ears of everyone who hears it will tingle (1 Samuel 3:11), and against Jerusalem in Manasseh's day (2 Kings 21:12). Shiloh is the example the temple sermon held up (7:12).

  • vv5–6 "to burn their sons in the fire as burnt offerings to Baal… the Valley of Slaughter" — the charge of 7:31–32, with burnt offerings to Baal added: the offering the LORD asked of Abraham, his son as a burnt offering (Genesis 22:2), and then stopped (22:12), given to Baal.

  • v9 "I will make them eat the flesh of their sons… in the siege and in the distress" — the curse of Deuteronomy 28:53, the flesh of your sons and your daughters… in the siege and in the distress with which your enemy will distress you, in the same words.

  • v11 "as one breaks a potter's jar so that it can never be mended" — lehera-feh, "be healed," the word of 8:22, Why then has the daughter of my people not been healed? At the potter's house a spoiled pot could be remade (18:4); an earthenware flask, once broken, cannot.

  • v13 "all the houses on whose roofs they burned incense to all the host of heaven" — the altars Josiah broke down on the roof of the upper chamber of Ahaz (2 Kings 23:12); Zephaniah names those who bow down on the roofs to the host of heaven (Zephaniah 1:5).

chapters.title: You Enticed Me, LORD
chapters.html:
Jeremiah 20

1Pashhur son of Immer, the priest, who was chief officer in the house of the LORD, heard Jeremiah prophesying these things.

2Then Pashhur struck Jeremiah the prophet and put him in the stocks that were in the Upper Benjamin Gate in the house of the LORD.

3And it came to pass the next day that Pashhur released Jeremiah from the stocks, and Jeremiah said to him, "The LORD does not call your name Pashhur, but Terror on Every Side.

4For this is what the LORD says: I am about to make you a terror to yourself and to all your friends. They will fall by the sword of their enemies while your eyes look on. I will give all Judah into the hand of the king of Babylon; he will carry them into exile to Babylon and strike them down with the sword.

5I will give all the wealth of this city, all its gains, all its precious things and all the treasures of the kings of Judah into the hand of their enemies, who will plunder them, seize them and carry them to Babylon.

6As for you, Pashhur, you and all who live in your house will go into captivity; you will go to Babylon, and there you will die, and there you will be buried, you and all your friends to whom you have prophesied falsely."

7You enticed me, LORD, and I was enticed;
You were stronger than I, and You prevailed.
I have become a laughingstock all day long;
everyone mocks me.

8For whenever I speak, I cry out;
I shout, "Violence and destruction!"
For the word of the LORD has become for me
a reproach and derision all day long.

9If I say, "I will not mention Him,
or speak any more in His name,"
then in my heart it becomes like a burning fire
shut up in my bones;
I am weary of holding it in,
and I cannot.

10For I hear the whispering of many:
"Terror on every side!
Denounce him! Let us denounce him!"
All my friends watch for my fall:
"Perhaps he will be enticed,
and we can prevail against him
and take our revenge on him."

11But the LORD is with me as a dread warrior;
therefore my persecutors will stumble;
they will not prevail.
They will be greatly put to shame,
for they will not succeed;
their everlasting disgrace will never be forgotten.

12LORD of hosts, who tests the righteous,
who sees the mind and the heart,
let me see Your vengeance on them,
for to You I have committed my cause.

13Sing to the LORD;
praise the LORD!
For He has delivered the life of the needy
from the hand of evildoers.

14Cursed be the day
on which I was born!
The day my mother bore me,
let it not be blessed!

15Cursed be the man
who brought the news to my father,
"A son is born to you, a male child,"
making him very glad.

16Let that man be like the cities
that the LORD overturned without relenting;
let him hear a cry in the morning
and an alarm at noon,

17because he did not kill me in the womb;
so my mother would have been my grave,
and her womb pregnant forever.

18Why did I come out of the womb
to see toil and sorrow,
and spend my days in shame?

Notes

  • v1 "Pashhur son of Immer, the priest" — of the priestly course of Immer, the sixteenth to Immer in David's order of the priests (1 Chronicles 24:14). The temple's officers had charge over every madman who prophesies, to put him in the stocks (29:26), and Jeremiah had just preached in its court (19:14).

  • vv3, 10 "Terror on Every Side" — Magor-missabib, the phrase of 6:25, terror is on every side, given to Pashhur as a name; in v10 Jeremiah hears it whispered against himself, in the words of the psalm, I hear the whispering of many, terror on every side (Psalm 31:13). The Greek has Exile for the name.

  • vv4–6 "the king of Babylon… to Babylon" — the first time the book names Babylon. Until now the enemy has been from the north (1:14; 4:6; 6:22).

  • vv7, 10 "You enticed me, LORD, and I was enticed; You were stronger than I, and You prevailed… Perhaps he will be enticed, and we can prevail against him" — pittitani, from patah, "to entice, to persuade," the word of the heavenly council, Who will entice Ahab? (1 Kings 22:20); the Greek has You deceived me. In v10 his enemies hope to do to him what he says the LORD did: the same two verbs, entice and prevail.

  • v9 "like a burning fire shut up in my bones; I am weary of holding it in" — nil'eiti, the words of 6:11, I am full of the wrath of the LORD; I am weary of holding it in. The LORD had said, I am about to make My words in your mouth a fire (5:14).

  • v12 "who tests the righteous, who sees the mind and the heart" — 11:20 again, nearly word for word: who tests the mind and the heart, let me see Your vengeance on them, for to You I have committed my cause.

  • vv14–18 "Cursed be the day on which I was born!… Why did I come out of the womb" — Job curses his birth in the same way, Let the day perish on which I was born (Job 3:3). The cities that the LORD overturned are Sodom and Gomorrah, He overturned those cities (Genesis 19:25). The last verse turns his call around: before you came out of the womb I consecrated you (1:5); now, Why did I come out of the womb?

chapters.title: The Way of Life and the Way of Death
chapters.html:
Jeremiah 21

1The word that came to Jeremiah from the LORD when King Zedekiah sent to him Pashhur son of Malchiah and Zephaniah son of Maaseiah, the priest, saying,

2"Please inquire of the LORD for us, for Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon is making war against us. Perhaps the LORD will deal with us according to all His wonderful works, and make him withdraw from us."

3Jeremiah said to them, "This is what you shall say to Zedekiah:

4This is what the LORD, the God of Israel, says: I am about to turn back the weapons of war that are in your hands, with which you are fighting the king of Babylon and the Chaldeans who are besieging you outside the wall, and I will gather them into the middle of this city.

5I Myself will fight against you with an outstretched hand and a strong arm, in anger and in fury and in great wrath.

6I will strike the inhabitants of this city, both man and beast; they will die of a great pestilence.

7After that, declares the LORD, I will give Zedekiah king of Judah, his servants and the people, those in this city who survive the pestilence, the sword and the famine, into the hand of Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon, into the hand of their enemies and into the hand of those who seek their life. He will strike them down with the sword; he will not pity them or spare them or have compassion."

8To this people you shall say: This is what the LORD says: I am setting before you the way of life and the way of death.

9Whoever stays in this city will die by the sword, by famine and by pestilence; but whoever goes out and surrenders to the Chaldeans who are besieging you will live, and his life will be his as plunder.

10For I have set My face against this city for harm and not for good, declares the LORD. It will be given into the hand of the king of Babylon, and he will burn it with fire.

The House of David

11To the house of the king of Judah: Hear the word of the LORD,

12house of David! This is what the LORD says:
Execute justice in the morning,
and rescue the one who has been robbed
from the hand of the oppressor;
or My wrath will go out like fire
and burn with no one to quench it,
because of the evil of your deeds.

13I am against you, inhabitant of the valley,
rock of the plain, declares the LORD,
you who say, "Who will come down against us?
Who will enter our dwellings?"

14I will punish you according to the fruit of your deeds,
declares the LORD;
I will kindle a fire in her forest,
and it will devour all that is around her.

Notes

  • v1 "Pashhur son of Malchiah and Zephaniah son of Maaseiah, the priest" — not the Pashhur son of Immer who put Jeremiah in the stocks (20:1). This Pashhur is among the officials who later want him dead (38:1, 4). Zephaniah is sent to him again (37:3) and is taken by the Babylonians as the second priest (52:24).

  • v2 "Perhaps the LORD will deal with us according to all His wonderful works" — nifle'otav, the word of the exodus, I will strike Egypt with all My wonders (Exodus 3:20). Once before, with an Assyrian army at the wall, a king of Judah sent the elders of the priests to a prophet (2 Kings 19:2), and the LORD's messenger struck the camp that night (19:35). Zedekiah asks for the same.

  • vv4–5 "I Myself will fight against you with an outstretched hand and a strong arm, in anger and in fury and in great wrath" — the exodus is with a strong hand and an outstretched arm (Deuteronomy 26:8); here the two words change places, and the hand is raised against Jerusalem. At the sea Moses said, The LORD will fight for you (Exodus 14:14); now the LORD fights against them. In anger and in fury and in great wrath is how Deuteronomy says the LORD would uproot the people from their land (Deuteronomy 29:28).

  • v7 "he will not pity them or spare them or have compassion" — the three verbs of 13:14, where the LORD said them of Himself. Here the king of Babylon carries them out.

  • vv8–9 "I am setting before you the way of life and the way of death… his life will be his as plunder" — Moses set before Israel life and death, the blessing and the curse. Choose life (Deuteronomy 30:19). There life was to keep the covenant; here it is to walk out of the city and give up to the enemy. Shalal is a soldier's share of the spoil: when the city falls, the one who went out takes away nothing but his life. The book gives the same promise to all who go out (38:2), to Ebed-melech (39:18) and to Baruch (45:5).

  • v10 "I have set My face against this city for harm and not for good" — samti fanai, the words of the law against the man who gives his child to Molech, I Myself will set My face against that man (Leviticus 20:5), now spoken against a city. Amos has the full sentence: I will set My eyes on them for harm and not for good (Amos 9:4). Jeremiah 24:6 turns it around for the exiles: I will set My eyes on them for good.

  • v12 "Execute justice in the morning… or My wrath will go out like fire and burn with no one to quench it, because of the evil of your deeds" — the last three lines are 4:4, said there to the men of Judah, here to the house of David. A king's justice was done in the morning: Morning by morning I will destroy all the wicked of the land (Psalm 101:8).

  • v14 "I will kindle a fire in her forest" — the forest is cedar. In the next chapter the king's house is Gilead… the summit of Lebanon, and its choicest cedars go on the fire (22:6–7); the king is the one nested among the cedars (22:23). Solomon's great hall was the House of the Forest of Lebanon, built on rows of cedar pillars (1 Kings 7:2).

chapters.title: Is Not This to Know Me?
chapters.html:
Jeremiah 22

1This is what the LORD says: Go down to the house of the king of Judah, and speak this word there.

2Say: Hear the word of the LORD, king of Judah, you who sit on the throne of David — you, your servants and your people who enter by these gates.

3This is what the LORD says: Do justice and righteousness, and rescue the one who has been robbed from the hand of the oppressor. Do not wrong the guest, the fatherless and the widow, do no violence, and do not shed innocent blood in this place.

4For if you diligently do this, then there will enter by the gates of this house kings who sit on the throne of David, riding in chariots and on horses, the king and his servants and his people.

5But if you do not listen to these words, by Myself I have sworn, declares the LORD, that this house shall become a desolation.

6For this is what the LORD says concerning the house of the king of Judah:
You are Gilead to Me,
the summit of Lebanon;
yet I will surely make you a wilderness,
cities that are not inhabited.

7I will consecrate destroyers against you,
each with his weapons;
they will cut down your choicest cedars
and throw them on the fire.

8Many nations will pass by this city, and each will say to his neighbor, "Why has the LORD done this to this great city?"

9They will answer, "Because they forsook the covenant of the LORD their God, and bowed down to other gods and served them."

Shallum

10Do not weep for the dead,
or grieve for him;
weep bitterly for the one who goes away,
for he shall return no more
nor see the land of his birth.

11For this is what the LORD says concerning Shallum son of Josiah, king of Judah, who reigned in place of Josiah his father, and who went out from this place: He shall not return here again;

12he shall die in the place where they have carried him into exile, and he shall not see this land again.

Jehoiakim

13Woe to him who builds his house without righteousness,
and his upper rooms without justice;
who makes his neighbor work for nothing
and does not give him his wages;

14who says, "I will build myself a spacious house
with airy upper rooms,"
and cuts out windows for it,
paneling it with cedar
and painting it with vermilion.

15Are you a king
because you compete in cedar?
Did not your father eat and drink,
and do justice and righteousness?
Then it was well with him.

16He judged the cause of the poor and needy;
then it was well.
Is not this to know Me?
declares the LORD.

17But your eyes and your heart
are only on your own gain,
on shedding innocent blood,
and on practicing oppression and extortion.

18Therefore this is what the LORD says concerning Jehoiakim son of Josiah, king of Judah:
They shall not mourn for him,
"Alas, my brother!" or "Alas, sister!"
They shall not mourn for him,
"Alas, lord!" or "Alas, his majesty!"

19He will be buried with the burial of a donkey,
dragged off and thrown out
beyond the gates of Jerusalem.

20Go up to Lebanon and cry out,
and lift up your voice in Bashan;
cry out from Abarim,
for all your lovers are crushed.

21I spoke to you in your ease,
but you said, "I will not listen."
This has been your way from your youth:
you have not obeyed My voice.

22The wind will shepherd all your shepherds,
and your lovers will go into captivity;
then you will be ashamed and disgraced
because of all your evil.

23You who dwell in Lebanon,
nested among the cedars,
how you will be pitied when pangs come upon you,
pain like a woman in labor!

Coniah

24As I live, declares the LORD, though Coniah son of Jehoiakim, king of Judah, were the signet ring on My right hand, yet I would tear you off from there,

25and give you into the hand of those who seek your life, into the hand of those you dread, into the hand of Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon and into the hand of the Chaldeans.

26I will hurl you and the mother who bore you into another land, where you were not born, and there you will die.

27But to the land they long to return to, there they shall not return.

28Is this man Coniah a despised, broken pot,
a jar no one wants?
Why are he and his seed hurled out
and cast into a land they do not know?

29Land, land, land,
hear the word of the LORD!

30This is what the LORD says:
Write this man down as childless,
a man who will not prosper in his days;
for no man of his seed will prosper,
sitting on the throne of David
and ruling again in Judah.

Notes

  • v5 "by Myself I have sworn… this house shall become a desolation" — the oath the LORD swore to Abraham, By Myself I have sworn (Genesis 22:16), here sworn against the house of David's sons. Le-chorbah, "a desolation": Jesus said to Jerusalem, Your house is left to you desolate (Matthew 23:38).

  • vv6–7 "I will consecrate destroyers against you… they will cut down your choicest cedars" — qiddashti, the word that made war a holy act, Consecrate war against her! (6:4). The palace is a mountain forest, Gilead and Lebanon, and its cedars are timber for the fire. In v14 the king is still paneling with cedar.

  • vv10–12 "Do not weep for the dead… weep bitterly for the one who goes away" — the dead is Josiah, killed by Pharaoh Neco at Megiddo (2 Kings 23:29). The one who goes away is his son Shallum, the fourth Shallum (1 Chronicles 3:15), crowned as Jehoahaz and taken by Neco to Egypt, and he came to Egypt and died there (2 Kings 23:34). The verse grieves more for the son who lives on in exile than for the father who died.

  • vv13–16 "Woe to him who builds his house without righteousness… Is not this to know Me?" — the king is Jehoiakim (v18). The law said, The wages of a hired man shall not stay with you overnight (Leviticus 19:13); he pays none. His father Josiah ate and drank like any man and did justice; that, not cedar, made him a king. To know the LORD is defined as judging the cause of the poor, as at 9:24, that he understands and knows Me, that I am the LORD who practices loyal love, justice and righteousness.

  • vv18–19 "Alas, my brother!… He will be buried with the burial of a donkey" — the cry raised over the man of God at Bethel, Alas, my brother! (1 Kings 13:30). No one will raise it for Jehoiakim. A donkey is not buried: it is dragged off and thrown away. Kings says of his death only that he lay down with his fathers (2 Kings 24:6), and records no burial.

  • v22 "The wind will shepherd all your shepherds" — kol ro'ayikh tir'eh ruach: the noun and the verb are from the same root. The shepherds are the rulers (2:8); the next chapter opens with a woe on them (23:1).

  • v23 "how you will be pitied when pangs come upon you" — mah nechant, from chanan, "to show favor," in a form found only here: the one who nested among the cedars will be pitied, as a woman in labor is. The Greek has you will groan.

  • v24 "Coniah… the signet ring on My right hand" — Coniah is Jehoiachin (2 Kings 24:8), called Jeconiah in 24:1. Even the ring on the LORD's own hand would be torn off. Haggai turns the word around for Zerubbabel son of Shealtiel: I will make you like a signet ring, for I have chosen you (Haggai 2:23).

  • v28 "a despised, broken pot, a jar no one wants" — keli, the word of the potter's house, where a spoiled pot was made again (18:4), of the jar broken so that it can never be mended (19:11), and of the rulers who fall like a precious jar (25:34). The Greek has only Jeconiah was dishonored like a vessel that is not needed.

  • vv29–30 "Land, land, land… Write this man down as childless" — the land is called three times to hear the verdict (the Greek has it twice). Ariri, the word of Abram, I am going stripped (Genesis 15:2), and of the law's sentence, they shall die childless (Leviticus 20:20). Coniah had sons, The sons of Jeconiah the captive: Shealtiel his son (1 Chronicles 3:17), and Matthew's line runs through him (Matthew 1:12). The verse says what childless means here: none of his seed will sit on David's throne.
