chapters.title: The LORD Is Our Righteousness
chapters.html:
Jeremiah 23

1Woe to the shepherds who destroy and scatter the sheep of My pasture! declares the LORD.

2Therefore this is what the LORD, the God of Israel, says concerning the shepherds who tend My people: You have scattered My flock and driven them away, and you have not cared for them. I am about to punish you for the evil of your deeds, declares the LORD.

3I Myself will gather the remnant of My flock out of all the lands where I have driven them, and bring them back to their fold, and they will be fruitful and multiply.

4I will raise up shepherds over them who will tend them; they will fear no more, nor be dismayed, nor will any be missing, declares the LORD.

The Righteous Branch

5Days are coming, declares the LORD,
when I will raise up for David a righteous Branch;
he will reign as king and act wisely,
and do justice and righteousness in the land.

6In his days Judah will be saved,
and Israel will dwell in safety;
and this is the name by which he will be called:
The LORD Is Our Righteousness.

7Therefore, days are coming, declares the LORD, when they will no longer say, "As the LORD lives, who brought up the sons of Israel out of the land of Egypt,"

8but, "As the LORD lives, who brought up and led the seed of the house of Israel out of the land of the north and out of all the lands where He had driven them." Then they will dwell on their own soil.

Concerning the Prophets

9Concerning the prophets:
My heart is broken within me;
all my bones shake;
I am like a drunken man,
like a man overcome by wine,
because of the LORD
and because of His holy words.

10For the land is full of adulterers;
because of the curse the land mourns;
the pastures of the wilderness are dried up.
Their course is evil,
and their might is not right.

11For both prophet and priest are godless;
even in My house I have found their evil,
declares the LORD.

12Therefore their way will be to them
like slippery paths in the darkness;
they will be driven on and fall in it;
for I will bring disaster on them,
the year of their punishment,
declares the LORD.

13In the prophets of Samaria
I saw an unseemly thing:
they prophesied by Baal
and led My people Israel astray.

14But in the prophets of Jerusalem
I have seen a horrible thing:
they commit adultery and walk in falsehood;
they strengthen the hands of evildoers,
so that no one turns from his evil.
All of them have become like Sodom to Me,
and its inhabitants like Gomorrah.

15Therefore this is what the LORD of hosts says concerning the prophets:
I am about to feed them with wormwood
and give them poisoned water to drink;
for from the prophets of Jerusalem
godlessness has gone out into all the land.

16This is what the LORD of hosts says:
Do not listen to the words of the prophets
who prophesy to you;
they are filling you with emptiness;
they speak a vision of their own heart,
not from the mouth of the LORD.

17They keep saying to those who despise Me,
"The LORD has said, 'You will have peace'";
and to everyone who walks in the stubbornness of his heart they say,
"No disaster will come on you."

18For who has stood in the council of the LORD,
to see and to hear His word?
Who has paid attention to His word and listened?

19The storm of the LORD has gone out in wrath,
a whirling tempest;
it will whirl down on the head of the wicked.

20The anger of the LORD will not turn back
until He has done and carried out
the purposes of His heart.
In the end of days
you will understand it clearly.

21I did not send the prophets,
yet they ran;
I did not speak to them,
yet they prophesied.

22But if they had stood in My council,
they would have made My people hear My words,
and turned them back from their evil way
and from the evil of their deeds.

23Am I a God who is near, declares the LORD,
and not a God far off?

24Can a man hide himself in secret places
so that I cannot see him? declares the LORD.
Do I not fill heaven and earth?
declares the LORD.

25I have heard what the prophets have said who prophesy lies in My name, saying, "I have dreamed, I have dreamed!"

26How long will this be in the heart of the prophets who prophesy lies, who prophesy the deceit of their own hearts?

27They plan to make My people forget My name by their dreams that they tell one another, just as their fathers forgot My name for Baal.

28Let the prophet who has a dream tell his dream, but let him who has My word speak My word faithfully. What has straw to do with wheat? declares the LORD.

29Is not My word like fire, declares the LORD, and like a hammer that shatters rock?

30Therefore I am against the prophets, declares the LORD, who steal My words from one another.

31I am against the prophets, declares the LORD, who use their own tongues and say, "He declares."

32I am against those who prophesy lying dreams, declares the LORD, who tell them and lead My people astray by their lies and their recklessness, when I did not send them or command them. They do not profit this people at all, declares the LORD.

The Burden of the LORD

33When this people, or a prophet or a priest, asks you, "What is the burden of the LORD?" you shall say to them, "You are the burden, and I will cast you off, declares the LORD."

34As for the prophet, the priest or the people who say, "The burden of the LORD," I will punish that man and his household.

35This is what you shall say, each to his neighbor and each to his brother: "What has the LORD answered?" and "What has the LORD spoken?"

36But you shall no longer mention "the burden of the LORD," for each man's own word will be his burden, and you have perverted the words of the living God, the LORD of hosts, our God.

37This is what you shall say to the prophet: "What has the LORD answered you?" and "What has the LORD spoken?"

38But if you say, "The burden of the LORD," then this is what the LORD says: Because you have said this word, "The burden of the LORD," when I sent to you, saying, "You shall not say, 'The burden of the LORD,'"

39therefore I am about to lift you up and cast you off, you and the city that I gave to you and to your fathers, away from My presence.

40I will bring on you an everlasting reproach and an everlasting disgrace that will not be forgotten.

Notes

  • vv2, 4 "you have not cared for them. I am about to punish you… nor will any be missing" — the verb paqad, "to attend to," three times: the shepherds lo feqadtem, did not attend to the flock, so the LORD is poqed, attending to them for their evil; and under the new shepherds none yippaqedu, the word of the count, not one man of us is missing (Numbers 31:49). The gathered flock will be fruitful and multiply, the first blessing (Genesis 1:28).

  • v5 "a righteous Branch… and do justice and righteousness in the land" — tsemach, what sprouts from the ground: Isaiah's branch of the LORD (Isaiah 4:2). Zechariah makes it a name, My servant the Branch (Zechariah 3:8), a man whose name is Branch (6:12). The king will do what was asked of the house of David, Do justice and righteousness (22:3), and what Josiah did (22:15).

  • v6 "The LORD Is Our Righteousness" — YHWH tsidqenu. This run of oracles began with King Zedekiah, Tsidqiyahu (21:1), whose name is made of the same two words: tsedeq and the LORD's name. The coming king will be what that name says. The Hebrew accents join the LORD's name to Our Righteousness, as in The LORD Is My Banner (Exodus 17:15) and The LORD Is Peace (Judges 6:24). The Greek reads the words otherwise: this is his name, which the Lord will call him: Iosedek. At 33:16 the same name is given to Jerusalem.

  • vv7–8 "As the LORD lives, who brought up… out of the land of the north" — 16:14–15 again, with small changes. Where He had driven them follows the Greek and the same oath in 16:15; the Hebrew here has where I had driven them, the LORD's own voice breaking into the people's oath.

  • v9 "all my bones shake" — rachafu, a verb found elsewhere only in the breath of God was hovering over the face of the waters (Genesis 1:2) and the eagle that hovers over its young (Deuteronomy 32:11). In the prophet's body the same movement is a trembling.

  • vv13–14 "In the prophets of Samaria I saw an unseemly thing… in the prophets of Jerusalem I have seen a horrible thing" — tiflah, the word of Job 1:22, nor did he charge God with wrong; sha'arurah, the word of 5:30, an appalling and horrible thing. Samaria's prophets prophesied by Baal (as 2:8), and Samaria fell; Jerusalem's are worse, as 3:11 said of the two kingdoms. Isaiah also called Jerusalem's rulers rulers of Sodom (Isaiah 1:10).

  • vv18, 22 "who has stood in the council of the LORD… if they had stood in My council" — sod, the council where the LORD's word is heard. Micaiah, the prophet who stood against four hundred prophets, saw the LORD sitting on His throne, and all the host of heaven standing beside Him (1 Kings 22:19). Amos says the Lord GOD does nothing without revealing His sod to His servants the prophets (Amos 3:7). Eliphaz asks Job, Have you listened in the council of God? (Job 15:8).

  • v23 "Am I a God who is near… and not a God far off?" — a question, and v24 gives its point: no one hides from Him, near or far. The Greek has no question, and denies the far: I am a God who draws near, and not a God from far off.

  • v31 "who use their own tongues and say, 'He declares'" — va-yin'amu ne'um, "and declare a declaration," using ne'um, the word of every declares the LORD in this chapter. The formula comes off their tongues with no word from the LORD behind it.

  • vv33–40 "the burden of the LORD… You are the burden" — massa, from nasa, "to lift, to carry": a load, and also a prophet's oracle, as in The oracle concerning Babylon (Isaiah 13:1). The people ask mockingly for the LORD's burden, and the answer turns the word on them. You are the burden is the Greek, attem ha-massa: the same Hebrew letters divided otherwise. The Hebrew vowels give et mah massa, "What burden?" In v39 nasho has the letters of nasa: I will lift you up (the Greek has I take). The Hebrew vowels give nashiti, from nashah, "to forget": I will forget you completely.

Woe to the shepherds who destroy and scatter the sheep of My pasture! declares the LORD.

Therefore this is what the LORD, the God of Israel, says concerning the shepherds who tend My people: You have scattered My flock and driven them away, and you have not cared for them. I am about to punish you for the evil of your deeds, declares the LORD.
I Myself will gather the remnant of My flock out of all the lands where I have driven them, and bring them back to their fold, and they will be fruitful and multiply.
I will raise up shepherds over them who will tend them; they will fear no more, nor be dismayed, nor will any be missing, declares the LORD.

but, "As the LORD lives, who brought up and led the seed of the house of Israel out of the land of the north and out of all the lands where He had driven them." Then they will dwell on their own soil.

But in the prophets of Jerusalem I have seen a horrible thing: they commit adultery and walk in falsehood; they strengthen the hands of evildoers, so that no one turns from his evil. All of them have become like Sodom to Me, and its inhabitants like Gomorrah.

Therefore this is what the LORD of hosts says concerning the prophets: I am about to feed them with wormwood and give them poisoned water to drink; for from the prophets of Jerusalem godlessness has gone out into all the land.

I did not send the prophets, yet they ran; I did not speak to them, yet they prophesied.
But if they had stood in My council, they would have made My people hear My words, and turned them back from their evil way and from the evil of their deeds.
Am I a God who is near, declares the LORD, and not a God far off?
Can a man hide himself in secret places so that I cannot see him? declares the LORD. Do I not fill heaven and earth? declares the LORD.
I have heard what the prophets have said who prophesy lies in My name, saying, "I have dreamed, I have dreamed!"
How long will this be in the heart of the prophets who prophesy lies, who prophesy the deceit of their own hearts?

Let the prophet who has a dream tell his dream, but let him who has My word speak My word faithfully. What has straw to do with wheat? declares the LORD.
Is not My word like fire, declares the LORD, and like a hammer that shatters rock?
Therefore I am against the prophets, declares the LORD, who steal My words from one another.
I am against the prophets, declares the LORD, who use their own tongues and say, "He declares."

I am against those who prophesy lying dreams, declares the LORD, who tell them and lead My people astray by their lies and their recklessness, when I did not send them or command them. They do not profit this people at all, declares the LORD.
The Burden of the LORD
When this people, or a prophet or a priest, asks you, "What is the burden of the LORD?" you shall say to them, "You are the burden, and I will cast you off, declares the LORD."
As for the prophet, the priest or the people who say, "The burden of the LORD," I will punish that man and his household.
This is what you shall say, each to his neighbor and each to his brother: "What has the LORD answered?" and "What has the LORD spoken?"
But you shall no longer mention "the burden of the LORD," for each man's own word will be his burden, and you have perverted the words of the living God, the LORD of hosts, our God.
This is what you shall say to the prophet: "What has the LORD answered you?" and "What has the LORD spoken?"

But if you say, "The burden of the LORD," then this is what the LORD says: Because you have said this word, "The burden of the LORD," when I sent to you, saying, "You shall not say, 'The burden of the LORD,'"
therefore I am about to lift you up and cast you off, you and the city that I gave to you and to your fathers, away from My presence.
I will bring on you an everlasting reproach and an everlasting disgrace that will not be forgotten.

chapters.title: Two Baskets of Figs
chapters.html:
Jeremiah 24

1The LORD showed me two baskets of figs set in front of the temple of the LORD. This was after Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon had carried into exile from Jerusalem Jeconiah son of Jehoiakim, king of Judah, with the princes of Judah, the craftsmen and the smiths, and had brought them to Babylon.

2One basket had very good figs, like first-ripe figs; the other basket had very bad figs, so bad that they could not be eaten.

3The LORD said to me, "What do you see, Jeremiah?" I said, "Figs: the good figs very good, and the bad figs very bad, so bad that they cannot be eaten."

4Then the word of the LORD came to me, saying,

5"This is what the LORD, the God of Israel, says: Like these good figs, so I will regard as good the exiles of Judah, whom I have sent away from this place to the land of the Chaldeans.

6I will set My eyes on them for good, and I will bring them back to this land. I will build them up and not overthrow them; I will plant them and not uproot them.

7I will give them a heart to know Me, that I am the LORD; they will be My people, and I will be their God, for they will return to Me with their whole heart.

8But like the bad figs, so bad that they cannot be eaten — for this is what the LORD says — so I will give up Zedekiah king of Judah, his princes, the remnant of Jerusalem who remain in this land, and those who live in the land of Egypt.

9I will make them a horror and a disaster to all the kingdoms of the earth, a reproach, a proverb, a byword and a curse in all the places where I will drive them.

10I will send the sword, famine and pestilence among them, until they are consumed from the land that I gave to them and to their fathers."

Notes

  • v1 "Jeconiah son of Jehoiakim… the craftsmen and the smiths" — the Coniah of 22:24–30, now in Babylon. Kings tells the same exile: all the craftsmen and the smiths. None remained except the poorest people of the land (2 Kings 24:14). Zedekiah, his uncle, now reigns in Jerusalem (2 Kings 24:17), and the vision is about the two halves of the people: those taken and those left.

  • v2 "like first-ripe figs" — bikkurot, the first figs of the year, the best. Hosea: Like the first-ripe fruit on the fig tree I saw your fathers (Hosea 9:10); Isaiah: like a first-ripe fig before the summer: whoever sees it swallows it as soon as it is in his hand (Isaiah 28:4).

  • v3 "What do you see, Jeremiah?" — the question of the almond branch and the boiling pot (1:11, 13). The book's first visions told of judgment coming; this one sorts the people after it has begun.

  • vv5–6 "I will set My eyes on them for good… I will build them up and not overthrow them; I will plant them and not uproot them" — the reverse of 21:10, I have set My face against this city for harm and not for good, and of Amos 9:4, I will set My eyes on them for harm and not for good. The four verbs are Jeremiah's call, to uproot and to pull down, to destroy and to overthrow, to build and to plant (1:10): the building and planting fall to the exiles.

  • v7 "I will give them a heart to know Me" — Moses said at the end of the wilderness years, Yet the LORD has not given you a heart to know, or eyes to see, or ears to hear, to this day (Deuteronomy 29:4). What that generation was not given, the exiles will be. They will be My people, and I will be their God is the covenant's own sentence (11:4).

  • vv8–10 "the bad figs… a horror… a reproach, a proverb, a byword and a curse" — the curses of Deuteronomy: you will be a horror to all the kingdoms of the earth (28:25); a horror, a proverb and a byword among all the peoples where the LORD drives you (28:37). Those left in Jerusalem said of the exiles, Keep far from the LORD; to us this land is given as a possession (Ezekiel 11:15). The vision says the opposite: the ones taken away are the good figs.

speech.text: Jeremiah 24

The LORD showed me two baskets of figs set in front of the temple of the LORD. This was after Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon had carried into exile from Jerusalem Jeconiah son of Jehoiakim, king of Judah, with the princes of Judah, the craftsmen and the smiths, and had brought them to Babylon.
One basket had very good figs, like first-ripe figs; the other basket had very bad figs, so bad that they could not be eaten.
The LORD said to me, "What do you see, Jeremiah?" I said, "Figs: the good figs very good, and the bad figs very bad, so bad that they cannot be eaten."
Then the word of the LORD came to me, saying,
"This is what the LORD, the God of Israel, says: Like these good figs, so I will regard as good the exiles of Judah, whom I have sent away from this place to the land of the Chaldeans.
I will set My eyes on them for good, and I will bring them back to this land. I will build them up and not overthrow them; I will plant them and not uproot them.
I will give them a heart to know Me, that I am the LORD; they will be My people, and I will be their God, for they will return to Me with their whole heart.

But like the bad figs, so bad that they cannot be eaten — for this is what the LORD says — so I will give up Zedekiah king of Judah, his princes, the remnant of Jerusalem who remain in this land, and those who live in the land of Egypt.
I will make them a horror and a disaster to all the kingdoms of the earth, a reproach, a proverb, a byword and a curse in all the places where I will drive them.
I will send the sword, famine and pestilence among them, until they are consumed from the land that I gave to them and to their fathers."

chapters.title: The Cup of the Wine of Wrath
chapters.html:
Jeremiah 25

1The word that came to Jeremiah concerning all the people of Judah, in the fourth year of Jehoiakim son of Josiah, king of Judah, which was the first year of Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon,

2which Jeremiah the prophet spoke to all the people of Judah and to all the inhabitants of Jerusalem:

3"From the thirteenth year of Josiah son of Amon, king of Judah, to this day, these twenty-three years, the word of the LORD has come to me, and I have spoken to you again and again, but you have not listened.

4The LORD has sent to you all His servants the prophets again and again, but you have not listened or inclined your ear to hear,

5saying, 'Turn now, each of you, from his evil way and from the evil of your deeds, and live on the land that the LORD has given to you and to your fathers from of old and forever.

6Do not go after other gods to serve them and to worship them, and do not provoke Me to anger with the work of your hands; then I will do you no harm.'

7Yet you have not listened to Me, declares the LORD, and so you have provoked Me to anger with the work of your hands, to your own harm.

8Therefore this is what the LORD of hosts says: Because you have not listened to My words,

9I am about to send for all the clans of the north, declares the LORD, and for Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon, My servant, and I will bring them against this land and its inhabitants, and against all these nations around it. I will destroy them completely, and make them a horror and a thing to be hissed at, and everlasting ruins.

10I will banish from them the voice of mirth and the voice of gladness, the voice of the bridegroom and the voice of the bride, the sound of the millstones and the light of the lamp.

11This whole land will become a ruin and a horror, and these nations will serve the king of Babylon seventy years.

12And it shall come to pass, when seventy years are completed, that I will punish the king of Babylon and that nation for their iniquity, declares the LORD, and the land of the Chaldeans; and I will make it an everlasting desolation.

13I will bring on that land all My words that I have spoken against it, all that is written in this book, which Jeremiah prophesied against all the nations.

14For many nations and great kings will make slaves of them too, and I will repay them according to their deeds and the work of their hands."

The Cup

15For this is what the LORD, the God of Israel, said to me: Take from My hand this cup of the wine of wrath, and make all the nations to whom I send you drink it.

16They will drink and stagger and go mad because of the sword that I am sending among them.

17So I took the cup from the LORD's hand and made all the nations to whom the LORD sent me drink it:

18Jerusalem and the cities of Judah, its kings and its princes, to make them a ruin, a horror, a thing to be hissed at and a curse, as it is this day;

19Pharaoh king of Egypt, his servants, his princes and all his people;

20all the mixed peoples; all the kings of the land of Uz; all the kings of the land of the Philistines: Ashkelon, Gaza, Ekron and the remnant of Ashdod;

21Edom, Moab and the sons of Ammon;

22all the kings of Tyre, all the kings of Sidon, and the kings of the coastlands across the sea;

23Dedan, Tema, Buz, and all who clip the hair at the sides of their head;

24all the kings of Arabia, and all the kings of the mixed peoples who live in the wilderness;

25all the kings of Zimri, all the kings of Elam and all the kings of Media;

26all the kings of the north, near and far, one after another; and all the kingdoms of the world on the face of the earth. After them the king of Sheshach will drink.

27Then you shall say to them: This is what the LORD of hosts, the God of Israel, says: Drink, get drunk and vomit, fall and rise no more, because of the sword that I am sending among you.

28And it shall come to pass, when they refuse to take the cup from your hand to drink, that you shall say to them: This is what the LORD of hosts says: You must drink!

29For I am beginning to bring disaster on the city that is called by My name, and will you go unpunished? You will not go unpunished, for I am calling for a sword against all the inhabitants of the earth, declares the LORD of hosts.

30As for you, prophesy against them all these words, and say to them:
The LORD will roar from on high,
and utter His voice from His holy dwelling;
He will roar mightily against His fold;
He will raise a shout like those who tread grapes
against all the inhabitants of the earth.

31The tumult has reached the end of the earth,
for the LORD has a dispute with the nations;
He is entering into judgment with all flesh;
the wicked He has given to the sword,
declares the LORD.

32This is what the LORD of hosts says:
Disaster is going out
from nation to nation,
and a great storm is stirring
from the farthest parts of the earth.

33Those slain by the LORD on that day will lie from one end of the earth to the other. They will not be mourned or gathered or buried; they will be dung on the face of the ground.

34Wail, you shepherds, and cry out;
roll in the dust, you leaders of the flock,
for the days of your slaughter have come,
and of your scatterings;
you will fall like a precious jar.

35Flight will fail the shepherds,
and escape the leaders of the flock.

36The sound of the shepherds' cry,
and the wailing of the leaders of the flock!
For the LORD is laying waste their pasture,

37and the peaceful folds are silenced
because of the fierce anger of the LORD.

38Like a young lion He has left His lair;
for their land has become a horror
because of the oppressing sword
and because of His fierce anger.

Notes

  • vv1, 3 "the fourth year of Jehoiakim… the first year of Nebuchadnezzar… these twenty-three years" — the year Nebuchadnezzar defeated Pharaoh Neco at Carchemish (46:2), and the year Jeremiah was told to write all his words in a scroll (36:1–2). Twenty-three years earlier, in the thirteenth year of Josiah, the word first came to him (1:2). The Greek does not have the first year of Nebuchadnezzar.

  • v9 "Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon, My servant… I will destroy them completely" — avdi, "My servant," the title of Moses and of David, given to the king of Babylon (also 27:6; 43:10). Hacharamtim is the verb of Jericho, They devoted to destruction all that was in the city (Joshua 6:21): the ban Israel once carried out in Canaan is now carried out on Judah. The Greek names neither Nebuchadnezzar nor My servant here, only a clan from the north.

  • v10 "the voice of the bridegroom and the voice of the bride, the sound of the millstones and the light of the lamp" — 7:34 and 16:9 silence the wedding voices; here the grinding of the day's grain and the lamp in the house at night are added. The same voices are promised back in 33:11. The lament over Babylon in Revelation takes up three of them: the sound of the millstone… the light of a lamp… the voice of bridegroom and bride (Revelation 18:22–23).

  • vv11–12 "seventy years… when seventy years are completed" — the count is given again at 29:10. The Chronicler ends his book with it, to fulfill seventy years (2 Chronicles 36:21), and Daniel reads it in the books… the word of the LORD to Jeremiah the prophet (Daniel 9:2). When it is done, the same punishment falls on Babylon.

  • vv13–15 "all that is written in this book, which Jeremiah prophesied against all the nations" — here the Greek takes another order. Its sentence ends at written in this book; What Jeremiah prophesied against the nations becomes a heading, and the oracles against the nations follow at once, Elam first. The cup of vv15–38 comes after them. The Hebrew keeps those oracles for chapters 46–51 (Elam at 49:34–39). The Greek has no v14.

  • v15 "this cup of the wine of wrath" — the cup of Isaiah 51:17, you who have drunk from the hand of the LORD the cup of His wrath. Jerusalem drinks first (v18), then the nations. The Greek has the cup of this unmixed wine.

  • v26 "the king of Sheshach" — Babylon's name written in a letter-swap. Each letter of Bavel (b, b, l), counted from the start of the alphabet, is replaced by the letter that stands as far from the end (sh, sh, k). Jeremiah 51:41 sets the two names side by side: How Sheshach is taken… How Babylon has become a horror among the nations! Babylon, the LORD's servant against the nations (v9), drinks last, as v12 said it would be punished. The Greek does not have the line.

  • v29 "I am beginning to bring disaster on the city that is called by My name" — the LORD's own city is first, so no other will be spared. Peter: it is time for the judgment to begin from the house of God; and if it begins first from us, what will be the end of those who do not obey the gospel of God? (1 Peter 4:17).

  • v30 "The LORD will roar from on high… He will raise a shout like those who tread grapes" — Amos opens with The LORD roars from Zion and utters His voice from Jerusalem (Amos 1:2; also Joel 3:16). Here the roar comes from heaven, against the whole earth. Heidad is the harvest shout of the men treading the winepress (Isaiah 16:10), and the LORD treads the nations as grapes: I have trodden the winepress alone (Isaiah 63:3).

  • vv34, 38 "and of your scatterings… because of the oppressing sword" — in v34, u-tefotsotikhem is found only here; its sense is uncertain, and the Greek does not have it. For like a precious jar the Greek has like the choice rams, the flock picture of vv34–36. In v38 the Greek reads sword (the great sword), and mippenei cherev ha-yonah, "because of the oppressing sword," is the book's own phrase at 46:16 and 50:16; the sword is what the LORD sends through this whole chapter (vv16, 27, 29, 31). The Hebrew here has charon ha-yonah, "the fierceness of the oppressor," with charon again in the next line, His fierce anger.

chapters.title: Jeremiah on Trial
chapters.html:
Jeremiah 26

1In the beginning of the reign of Jehoiakim son of Josiah, king of Judah, this word came from the LORD:

2This is what the LORD says: Stand in the court of the LORD's house, and speak to all who come from the cities of Judah to worship in the LORD's house all the words that I command you to speak to them; do not take away a word.

3Perhaps they will listen and turn, each from his evil way, and I will relent of the disaster that I intend to do to them because of the evil of their deeds.

4Say to them: This is what the LORD says: If you will not listen to Me, to walk in My law that I have set before you,

5and to listen to the words of My servants the prophets whom I send to you again and again, though you have not listened,

6then I will make this house like Shiloh, and I will make this city a curse to all the nations of the earth.

7The priests and the prophets and all the people heard Jeremiah speaking these words in the house of the LORD.

8When Jeremiah had finished speaking all that the LORD had commanded him to speak to all the people, the priests and the prophets and all the people seized him, saying, "You must die!

9Why have you prophesied in the name of the LORD, saying, 'This house will be like Shiloh, and this city will be laid waste, without an inhabitant'?" All the people crowded around Jeremiah in the house of the LORD.

10When the officials of Judah heard these things, they came up from the king's house to the house of the LORD and sat at the entrance of the New Gate of the LORD's house.

11Then the priests and the prophets said to the officials and to all the people, "This man deserves to die, because he has prophesied against this city, as you have heard with your own ears."

12Jeremiah said to all the officials and to all the people, "The LORD sent me to prophesy against this house and against this city all the words that you have heard.

13So now, amend your ways and your deeds, and obey the voice of the LORD your God, and the LORD will relent of the disaster that He has pronounced against you.

14As for me, I am in your hands; do with me as seems good and right to you.

15Only know for certain that if you put me to death, you will bring innocent blood on yourselves and on this city and its inhabitants; for in truth the LORD has sent me to you to speak all these words in your hearing."

16Then the officials and all the people said to the priests and the prophets, "This man does not deserve to die, for he has spoken to us in the name of the LORD our God."

17Some of the elders of the land rose and said to all the assembled people,

18"Micah of Moresheth prophesied in the days of Hezekiah king of Judah, and said to all the people of Judah: This is what the LORD of hosts says:
Zion shall be plowed as a field;
Jerusalem shall become a heap of ruins,
and the mountain of the house a wooded height.

19Did Hezekiah king of Judah and all Judah put him to death? Did he not fear the LORD and plead with the LORD, so that the LORD relented of the disaster that He had pronounced against them? But we are about to bring great disaster on ourselves."

20There was also a man who prophesied in the name of the LORD, Uriah son of Shemaiah from Kiriath-jearim. He prophesied against this city and against this land in words just like Jeremiah's.

21When King Jehoiakim, with all his warriors and all the officials, heard his words, the king sought to put him to death. But Uriah heard of it and was afraid, and fled and went to Egypt.

22King Jehoiakim sent men to Egypt, Elnathan son of Achbor and others with him.

23They brought Uriah out of Egypt and took him to King Jehoiakim, who struck him down with the sword and threw his body into the graves of the common people.

24But the hand of Ahikam son of Shaphan was with Jeremiah, so that he was not given into the hand of the people to be put to death.

Notes

  • vv1–6 "Stand in the court of the LORD's house… I will make this house like Shiloh" — the temple sermon of chapter 7 (7:2, 12–14), told here as an event, with what followed. Do not take away a word is the law's command about itself, you shall not take away from it (Deuteronomy 4:2): the prophet may not soften the message.

  • vv7–16 "the priests and the prophets" — in vv7, 8, 11 and 16 the Greek calls them the false prophets; the Hebrew says only the prophets. It is the prophets who demand Jeremiah's death, and the officials and the people who refuse it.

  • vv8, 11, 16 "You must die!… This man deserves to die… This man does not deserve to die" — the law's sentence on the prophet who speaks a word the LORD has not commanded, that prophet shall die (Deuteronomy 18:20). Mishpat mavet, "a judgment of death," is the legal phrase of Deuteronomy 19:6, he did not deserve to die, and 21:22, a sin deserving death. The officials sit as judges at the gate, and the verdict turns on the law's own test: he has spoken in the name of the LORD our God (v16).

  • vv18–19 "Zion shall be plowed as a field… Did he not fear the LORD and plead with the LORD" — the elders quote Micah 3:12 word for word; Micah prophesied in the days of Hezekiah (Micah 1:1). Va-yechal et penei YHWH, "he pleaded with the LORD," is what Moses did after the golden calf, Moses pleaded with the LORD his God (Exodus 32:11), and there too the LORD relented (32:14). The elders argue from Hezekiah's day: a prophet of doom was heard, not killed, and the city was spared.

  • v22 "Elnathan son of Achbor" — the king's agent who brings Uriah back. He is among the officials who later hear Jeremiah's scroll read, and he pleads with Jehoiakim not to burn it (36:12, 25).

  • v23 "threw his body into the graves of the common people" — qivrei benei ha-am, a phrase found only here and where Josiah threw the dust of the burned Asherah on the graves of the common people (2 Kings 23:6). Josiah's son throws a prophet's body where his father threw the idol's ashes.

  • v24 "Ahikam son of Shaphan" — one of the men Josiah sent to inquire of the LORD when the book of the law was found (2 Kings 22:12–13). His son Gedaliah will take Jeremiah into his care after Jerusalem falls (39:14; 40:5–6).

chapters.title: The Yoke of the King of Babylon
chapters.html:
Jeremiah 27

1In the beginning of the reign of Jehoiakim son of Josiah, king of Judah, this word came to Jeremiah from the LORD:

2This is what the LORD said to me: Make yourself straps and yoke bars, and put them on your neck.

3Then send them to the king of Edom, the king of Moab, the king of the sons of Ammon, the king of Tyre and the king of Sidon, by the envoys who have come to Jerusalem to Zedekiah king of Judah.

4Give them this charge for their masters: This is what the LORD of hosts, the God of Israel, says: This is what you shall say to your masters:

5It is I who made the earth, and the man and the beast that are on the face of the earth, by My great power and My outstretched arm, and I give it to whomever seems right in My eyes.

6So now I Myself have given all these lands into the hand of Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon, My servant; I have given him even the beasts of the field to serve him.

7All the nations will serve him, and his son and his son's son, until the time of his own land comes; then many nations and great kings will make him their slave.

8But the nation or kingdom that will not serve him, Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon, and will not put its neck under the yoke of the king of Babylon, I will punish that nation by the sword, by famine and by pestilence, declares the LORD, until I have consumed them by his hand.

9As for you, do not listen to your prophets, your soothsayers, your dreams, those who read omens for you or your sorcerers, who keep saying to you, "You will not serve the king of Babylon."

10For they are prophesying a lie to you, so that you will be removed far from your land; I will drive you out, and you will perish.

11But the nation that brings its neck under the yoke of the king of Babylon and serves him, I will leave on its own land, declares the LORD, and it will till it and live in it.

To Zedekiah and the Priests

12To Zedekiah king of Judah I spoke in the same way: Bring your necks under the yoke of the king of Babylon, and serve him and his people, and live.

13Why will you die, you and your people, by the sword, by famine and by pestilence, as the LORD has spoken concerning the nation that will not serve the king of Babylon?

14Do not listen to the words of the prophets who keep saying to you, "You will not serve the king of Babylon," for they are prophesying a lie to you.

15I have not sent them, declares the LORD, but they are prophesying falsely in My name, so that I will drive you out and you will perish, you and the prophets who are prophesying to you.

16Then I spoke to the priests and to all this people, saying: This is what the LORD says: Do not listen to the words of your prophets who are prophesying to you, "The vessels of the LORD's house will now shortly be brought back from Babylon," for they are prophesying a lie to you.

17Do not listen to them. Serve the king of Babylon, and live. Why should this city become a ruin?

18If they are prophets, and if the word of the LORD is with them, let them intercede with the LORD of hosts, so that the vessels that are left in the house of the LORD, in the house of the king of Judah and in Jerusalem do not go to Babylon.

19For this is what the LORD of hosts says concerning the pillars, the Sea, the stands and the rest of the vessels that are left in this city,

20which Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon did not take when he carried Jeconiah son of Jehoiakim, king of Judah, into exile from Jerusalem to Babylon, with all the nobles of Judah and Jerusalem —

21this is what the LORD of hosts, the God of Israel, says concerning the vessels that are left in the house of the LORD, in the house of the king of Judah and in Jerusalem:

22They will be carried to Babylon, and there they will stay until the day I attend to them, declares the LORD. Then I will bring them up and restore them to this place.

Notes

  • v1 "In the beginning of the reign of Jehoiakim" — the same words as 26:1, but the chapter is set under Zedekiah: the envoys come to Zedekiah king of Judah (v3), Jeremiah speaks to Zedekiah (v12), and the next chapter begins in that same year, at the beginning of the reign of Zedekiah (28:1). The Greek has no v1. The Hebrew stands as it is.

  • vv2, 8, 11–12 "straps and yoke bars… put its neck under the yoke" — motot, the bars of a yoke. At the exodus the LORD broke them: I broke the bars of your yoke and made you walk upright (Leviticus 26:13). Now the prophet wears them, and tells five kings and his own king to bend their necks. Hananiah will break them off him (28:10).

  • vv5–6 "It is I who made the earth… I have given him even the beasts of the field" — the Creator gives the earth to whomever seems right in My eyes, and for now that is Nebuchadnezzar… My servant, as at 25:9. Daniel tells the same king, the beasts of the field and the birds of the heavens He has given into your hand (Daniel 2:38).

  • v7 "his son and his son's son, until the time of his own land comes" — Babylon's rule has an end, as 25:12, 14 said. The Greek does not have the verse.

  • v9 "your prophets, your soothsayers, your dreams, those who read omens for you or your sorcerers" — the law's list of what Israel must not have, a soothsayer, one who reads omens… or a sorcerer (Deuteronomy 18:10), with Judah's own prophets at its head. For your dreams the Greek has those who dream for you.

  • v18 "let them intercede with the LORD of hosts" — yifge'u, the verb forbidden to Jeremiah himself: do not pray for this people… or intercede with Me (7:16). The test he sets them is the work of a prophet, as the LORD said of Abraham: he is a prophet, and he will pray for you (Genesis 20:7).

  • vv19–22 "the pillars, the Sea, the stands… until the day I attend to them. Then I will bring them up" — Nebuchadnezzar had already cut in pieces all the vessels of gold that Solomon king of Israel had made (2 Kings 24:13). What was left the Chaldeans broke in pieces and carried the bronze to Babylon (2 Kings 25:13). The rest came back: King Cyrus also brought out the vessels of the house of the LORD that Nebuchadnezzar had carried away (Ezra 1:7). The Greek of vv16–22 is much shorter and has no promise of return.

chapters.title: Hananiah Breaks the Yoke
chapters.html:
Jeremiah 28

1And it came to pass in that same year, at the beginning of the reign of Zedekiah king of Judah, in the fourth year, in the fifth month, that Hananiah son of Azzur, the prophet from Gibeon, spoke to me in the house of the LORD in the sight of the priests and all the people, saying,

2"This is what the LORD of hosts, the God of Israel, says: I have broken the yoke of the king of Babylon.

3Within two years I will bring back to this place all the vessels of the LORD's house that Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon took from this place and carried to Babylon.

4I will also bring back to this place Jeconiah son of Jehoiakim, king of Judah, and all the exiles of Judah who went to Babylon, declares the LORD, for I will break the yoke of the king of Babylon."

5Then Jeremiah the prophet spoke to Hananiah the prophet in the sight of the priests and of all the people who were standing in the house of the LORD.

6Jeremiah the prophet said, "Amen! May the LORD do so! May the LORD fulfill the words that you have prophesied, and bring back from Babylon to this place the vessels of the LORD's house and all the exiles.

7But listen now to this word that I speak in your hearing and in the hearing of all the people:

8The prophets who were before me and before you from of old prophesied against many lands and great kingdoms, of war, of disaster and of pestilence.

9As for the prophet who prophesies peace, when the word of that prophet comes to pass, then it will be known that the LORD has truly sent the prophet."

10Then Hananiah the prophet took the yoke bar from the neck of Jeremiah the prophet and broke it.

11Hananiah spoke in the sight of all the people, saying, "This is what the LORD says: Even so will I break the yoke of Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon from the neck of all the nations within two years." Then Jeremiah the prophet went his way.

12After Hananiah the prophet had broken the yoke bar from the neck of Jeremiah the prophet, the word of the LORD came to Jeremiah, saying,

13"Go and tell Hananiah: This is what the LORD says: You have broken wooden bars, but you have made in their place bars of iron.

14For this is what the LORD of hosts, the God of Israel, says: I have put an iron yoke on the neck of all these nations, to serve Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon, and they will serve him; I have given him even the beasts of the field."

15Then Jeremiah the prophet said to Hananiah the prophet, "Listen, Hananiah! The LORD has not sent you, and you have made this people trust in a lie.

16Therefore this is what the LORD says: I am about to send you off the face of the earth. This year you will die, because you have spoken rebellion against the LORD."

17Hananiah the prophet died that same year, in the seventh month.

Notes

  • v1 "Hananiah son of Azzur, the prophet from Gibeon" — the Hebrew calls him the prophet, as it calls Jeremiah, six times in this chapter; the Greek calls him the false prophet. The Hebrew sets the two prophets side by side in the temple, with the same title, and lets the event decide (v9, v17).

  • vv2–4, 10–11 "I have broken the yoke of the king of Babylon… within two years" — the words of the exodus, I broke the bars of your yoke (Leviticus 26:13), and a sign to match Jeremiah's: Jeremiah wore the bars (27:2), and Hananiah breaks them in public, as Jeremiah once broke a flask (19:10). He promises two years; Jeremiah has said seventy (25:11).

  • vv6–9 "Amen! May the LORD do so!… when the word of that prophet comes to pass" — Jeremiah wishes Hananiah right, then gives the law's test: when a prophet speaks in the name of the LORD, and the word does not happen and does not come true, that is the word that the LORD has not spoken (Deuteronomy 18:22). Prophets of war and disaster stand in a long line (v8); a prophet of peace must wait to be proved.

  • vv13–14 "You have broken wooden bars, but you have made in their place bars of iron… an iron yoke" — the curse of the covenant, He will put an iron yoke on your neck until He has destroyed you (Deuteronomy 28:48). The Greek has I will make in their place bars of iron.

  • vv15–16 "The LORD has not sent you… I am about to send you off the face of the earth… you have spoken rebellion against the LORD" — lo shelachakha… meshallechakha: the LORD did not send him, so the LORD will send him, out of the world. Sarah dibbarta, "you have spoken rebellion," is the law's charge against the false prophet, because he has spoken rebellion against the LORD your God (Deuteronomy 13:5), and its sentence was death.

  • v17 "died that same year, in the seventh month" — two months after his prophecy in the fifth month (v1). He had promised the yoke broken in two years; he did not live out the year.

chapters.title: The Letter to the Exiles
chapters.html:
Jeremiah 29

1These are the words of the letter that Jeremiah the prophet sent from Jerusalem to the elders who were left among the exiles, to the priests, to the prophets and to all the people whom Nebuchadnezzar had carried into exile from Jerusalem to Babylon.

2This was after King Jeconiah, the queen mother, the eunuchs, the princes of Judah and Jerusalem, the craftsmen and the smiths had gone out from Jerusalem.

3It was sent by the hand of Elasah son of Shaphan and Gemariah son of Hilkiah, whom Zedekiah king of Judah sent to Babylon, to Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon. It said:

4"This is what the LORD of hosts, the God of Israel, says to all the exiles whom I have carried into exile from Jerusalem to Babylon:

5Build houses and live in them; plant gardens and eat their fruit.

6Take wives and father sons and daughters; take wives for your sons, and give your daughters to husbands, so that they may bear sons and daughters. Multiply there, and do not decrease.

7Seek the peace of the city where I have carried you into exile, and pray to the LORD on its behalf, for in its peace you will have peace.

8For this is what the LORD of hosts, the God of Israel, says: Do not let your prophets who are among you and your soothsayers deceive you, and do not listen to the dreams that you cause them to dream,

9for they are prophesying falsely to you in My name. I have not sent them, declares the LORD.

10For this is what the LORD says: When seventy years are completed for Babylon, I will attend to you, and I will fulfill for you My good word, to bring you back to this place.

11For I Myself know the plans I have for you, declares the LORD, plans for peace and not for harm, to give you a future and a hope.

12Then you will call on Me and come and pray to Me, and I will listen to you.

13You will seek Me and find Me, when you search for Me with all your heart.

14I will let Myself be found by you, declares the LORD, and I will restore your fortunes and gather you from all the nations and all the places where I have driven you, declares the LORD, and I will bring you back to the place from which I carried you into exile.

15Because you have said, 'The LORD has raised up prophets for us in Babylon' —

16for this is what the LORD says concerning the king who sits on the throne of David, and concerning all the people who live in this city, your brothers who did not go out with you into exile —

17this is what the LORD of hosts says: I am about to send among them the sword, famine and pestilence, and I will make them like rotten figs that cannot be eaten, they are so bad.

18I will pursue them with the sword, with famine and with pestilence, and I will make them a horror to all the kingdoms of the earth, a curse, an astonishment, a thing to be hissed at and a reproach among all the nations where I have driven them,

19because they have not listened to My words, declares the LORD, which I sent to them by My servants the prophets again and again; and you have not listened, declares the LORD.

20As for you, all you exiles whom I have sent away from Jerusalem to Babylon, hear the word of the LORD.

21This is what the LORD of hosts, the God of Israel, says concerning Ahab son of Kolaiah and Zedekiah son of Maaseiah, who are prophesying a lie to you in My name: I am about to give them into the hand of Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon, and he will strike them down before your eyes.

22Because of them, all the exiles of Judah who are in Babylon will use this curse: 'May the LORD make you like Zedekiah and like Ahab, whom the king of Babylon roasted in the fire,'

23because they have done an outrage in Israel: they have committed adultery with their neighbors' wives and have spoken lying words in My name, which I did not command them. I am He who knows, and I am witness, declares the LORD."

Shemaiah's Letter

24To Shemaiah the Nehelamite you shall say:

25"This is what the LORD of hosts, the God of Israel, says: Because you have sent letters in your own name to all the people who are in Jerusalem, and to Zephaniah son of Maaseiah the priest, and to all the priests, saying,

26'The LORD has made you priest in place of Jehoiada the priest, to be overseers in the house of the LORD over every madman who prophesies, to put him in the stocks and the collar.

27So now, why have you not rebuked Jeremiah of Anathoth, who is prophesying to you?

28For he has sent to us in Babylon, saying, "It will be long. Build houses and live in them; plant gardens and eat their fruit."'"

29Zephaniah the priest read this letter in the hearing of Jeremiah the prophet.

30Then the word of the LORD came to Jeremiah, saying,

31"Send to all the exiles, saying: This is what the LORD says concerning Shemaiah the Nehelamite: Because Shemaiah has prophesied to you, though I did not send him, and has made you trust in a lie,

32therefore this is what the LORD says: I am about to punish Shemaiah the Nehelamite and his seed. He will have no one living among this people, and he will not see the good that I am about to do for My people, declares the LORD, because he has spoken rebellion against the LORD."

Notes

  • vv5–7 "Build houses… plant gardens… Take wives… Seek the peace of the city" — the three things for which the law sent a man home before a battle: he has built a new house and has not dedicated it, has planted a vineyard and has not yet used its fruit, is engaged to a woman and has not taken her (Deuteronomy 20:5–7). In Babylon they are to do all three, as people who will stay. Shalom comes three times in v7: the peace of the city… in its peace you will have peace. The Greek has the peace of the land.

  • v8 "the dreams that you cause them to dream" — machlemim, a causative form of chalam, "to dream," found only here: the people prompt the dreams they want to hear, as 27:9 lists your dreams among the people's own diviners. The Greek reads the plain verb, the dreams that you dream.

  • vv10–11 "I will attend to you… plans for peace and not for harm, to give you a future and a hope" — the seventy years of 25:11–12. Efqod, "I will attend to," is the verb that came down on the shepherds (23:2), here turned to the exiles' good. Acharit ve-tiqvah, "a future and a hope," comes back in the word to Rachel: There is hope for your future (31:17). The Greek has only to give you these things.

  • vv13–14 "You will seek Me and find Me, when you search for Me with all your heart… I will restore your fortunes" — the promise Moses gave for the exile: you will seek the LORD your God, and you will find Him, if you search for Him with all your heart and with all your soul (Deuteronomy 4:29); the LORD your God will restore your fortunes… and He will gather you again from all the peoples (30:3). The Greek ends v14 at I will appear to you, and has none of vv16–20.

  • vv16–17 "your brothers who did not go out with you… like rotten figs" — the two baskets of chapter 24: the exiles are the good figs, and the king and people left in Jerusalem the bad ones that cannot be eaten.

  • v22 "this curse… whom the king of Babylon roasted in the fire" — qelalah, "curse," and qalam, "roasted": the curse is made from the sound of what was done to them.

  • v23 "they have done an outrage in Israel" — nevalah, the word of Dinah's brothers, he had done an outrage in Israel (Genesis 34:7), and of Tamar, Do not do this outrage (2 Samuel 13:12). The two prophets' adultery is named with it.

  • vv25–29 "overseers in the house of the LORD over every madman who prophesies… the stocks and the collar" — after Athaliah fell, the priest appointed overseers over the house of the LORD (2 Kings 11:18). Pashhur held the office, chief officer in the house of the LORD, when he put Jeremiah in the stocks (20:1–2). Madman is what Jehu's officers called the prophet sent to anoint him (2 Kings 9:11). Shemaiah asks Zephaniah to do it again; Zephaniah reads the letter to Jeremiah instead (v29).

  • vv31–32 "though I did not send him, and has made you trust in a lie… because he has spoken rebellion against the LORD" — the words of the sentence on Hananiah (28:15–16), now passed on a prophet in Babylon.

chapters.title: A Time of Distress for Jacob
chapters.html:
Jeremiah 30

1The word that came to Jeremiah from the LORD:

2This is what the LORD, the God of Israel, says: Write in a book all the words that I have spoken to you.

3For days are coming, declares the LORD, when I will restore the fortunes of My people Israel and Judah, says the LORD, and I will bring them back to the land that I gave to their fathers, and they will possess it.

4These are the words that the LORD spoke concerning Israel and Judah:

5This is what the LORD says:
We have heard a cry of trembling,
of terror, and no peace.

6Ask now and see:
can a male give birth?
Why then do I see every man
with his hands on his loins like a woman in labor,
and every face turned pale?

7Alas! For that day is great;
there is none like it.
It is a time of distress for Jacob,
yet out of it he will be saved.

8And it shall come to pass in that day, declares the LORD of hosts, that I will break his yoke from off your neck and tear off your bonds, and strangers will no longer make him their slave.

9They will serve the LORD their God and David their king, whom I will raise up for them.

10But you, do not fear, Jacob My servant, declares the LORD,
and do not be dismayed, Israel;
for I am about to save you from far away,
and your seed from the land of their captivity.
Jacob will return and have quiet and ease,
with no one to make him afraid.

11For I am with you, declares the LORD, to save you.
I will make a full end of all the nations
among which I have scattered you,
but of you I will not make a full end.
I will correct you with justice,
and I will not leave you unpunished.

12For this is what the LORD says:
Your hurt is incurable,
your wound is grievous.

13There is no one to plead your cause;
for your sore there is no healing,
no new flesh for you.

14All your lovers have forgotten you;
they do not seek you;
for I have struck you as an enemy strikes,
with the correction of a cruel one,
because your guilt is great,
because your sins are many.

15Why do you cry out over your hurt?
Your pain is incurable.
Because your guilt is great,
because your sins are many,
I have done these things to you.

16Therefore all who devour you will be devoured,
and all your adversaries, every one of them, will go into captivity;
those who plunder you will be plundered,
and all who prey on you I will give up as prey.

17For I will make new flesh grow for you,
and heal you of your wounds, declares the LORD,
because they have called you an outcast:
"It is Zion; no one seeks her."

18This is what the LORD says:
I am about to restore the fortunes of the tents of Jacob,
and have compassion on his dwellings;
the city will be rebuilt on its mound,
and the palace will stand in its rightful place.

19Out of them will come thanksgiving
and the voice of revelers.
I will multiply them, and they will not decrease;
I will honor them, and they will not be made small.

20Their sons will be as of old,
and their congregation will be established before Me,
and I will punish all who oppress them.

21Their prince will be one of their own,
and their ruler will come from their midst;
I will bring him near, and he will approach Me;
for who is he who would pledge his heart
to approach Me? declares the LORD.

22You will be My people,
and I will be your God.

23The storm of the LORD has gone out in wrath,
a sweeping tempest;
it will whirl down on the head of the wicked.

24The fierce anger of the LORD will not turn back
until He has done and carried out
the purposes of His heart.
In the end of days
you will understand it.

Notes

  • vv6–7 "can a male give birth?… It is a time of distress for Jacob, yet out of it he will be saved" — the men double over like women in labor. Et tsarah, "a time of distress," is Daniel's phrase for the last trouble, a time of distress such as has not been since there was a nation (Daniel 12:1). And the name is chosen: Jacob himself built an altar to the God who answered me in the day of my distress (Genesis 35:3).

  • vv8–9 "I will break his yoke from off your neck and tear off your bonds… David their king" — the yoke Jeremiah wore and Hananiah broke too soon (27:2; 28:10–11): what Hananiah promised within two years the LORD will do on His own day. Tear off your bonds is what the LORD had done once already, long ago I broke your yoke and tore off your bonds (2:20). Hosea: the sons of Israel will return and seek the LORD their God and David their king… in the end of days (Hosea 3:5).

  • vv10–11 "do not fear, Jacob My servant… I will correct you with justice, and I will not leave you unpunished" — the two verses stand again at 46:27–28; the Greek does not have them here. Do not fear, Jacob My servant is Isaiah's word (Isaiah 44:2). The prophet had prayed, Correct me, LORD, but with justice (10:24); not leaving it unpunished is part of the LORD's name proclaimed at Sinai (Exodus 34:7).

  • vv12–17 "Your hurt is incurable… For I will make new flesh grow for you" — anush, the word of the prophet's own complaint, my wound incurable (15:18). Arukhah, "new flesh," is what he asked about: Why then has the daughter of my people not been healed? (8:22). The same verb runs from v13, no new flesh for you (te'alah), to v17, I will make new flesh grow (a'aleh). V16 begins Therefore where judgment is expected, and v17 gives the reason: because they have called you an outcast.

  • v18 "the city will be rebuilt on its mound" — tel, the heap a ruined city leaves. The law made a town that turned to other gods a heap forever; it shall not be built again (Deuteronomy 13:16). This heap will be built again.

  • v21 "who is he who would pledge his heart to approach Me?" — arav, to stand as a pledge, the word of Judah for Benjamin, I myself will stand as the pledge for him (Genesis 43:9). To come near was the priests' right: the outsider who comes near shall be put to death (Numbers 18:7). The ruler is one the LORD Himself brings near.

  • vv23–24 "The storm of the LORD has gone out in wrath" — 23:19–20 again, with three small changes: a sweeping tempest (mitgorer) for a whirling tempest, fierce added to anger, and clearly gone from you will understand it.

chapters.title: A New Covenant
chapters.html:
Jeremiah 31

1At that time, declares the LORD, I will be the God of all the clans of Israel, and they will be My people.

2This is what the LORD says:
The people who survived the sword
found favor in the wilderness,
when Israel went to find its rest.

3From far away the LORD appeared to me:
I have loved you with an everlasting love;
therefore I have drawn you with loyal love.

4Again I will build you, and you will be built,
virgin Israel;
again you will adorn yourself with your tambourines
and go out in the dance of the revelers.

5Again you will plant vineyards
on the mountains of Samaria;
the planters will plant
and use their fruit.

6For there will be a day when watchmen will call
on Mount Ephraim:
"Arise, and let us go up to Zion,
to the LORD our God."

7For this is what the LORD says:
Sing with gladness for Jacob,
and shout at the head of the nations;
proclaim, give praise, and say,
"Save Your people, LORD,
the remnant of Israel."

8I am about to bring them from the land of the north,
and gather them from the farthest parts of the earth;
among them the blind and the lame,
the woman with child and the one in labor, together;
a great company, they will return here.

9With weeping they will come,
and with pleas for mercy I will lead them;
I will bring them to streams of water,
on a straight road where they will not stumble;
for I am a father to Israel,
and Ephraim is My firstborn.

10Hear the word of the LORD, you nations,
and declare it in the coastlands far away;
say: He who scattered Israel will gather him,
and keep him as a shepherd keeps his flock.

11For the LORD has ransomed Jacob,
and redeemed him from the hand of one stronger than he.

12They will come and sing on the height of Zion,
and stream to the goodness of the LORD,
to the grain, the new wine and the oil,
and to the young of the flock and the herd;
their soul will be like a watered garden,
and they will never languish again.

13Then the virgin will rejoice in the dance,
and the young men and the old together;
I will turn their mourning into joy;
I will comfort them, and give them gladness after their sorrow.

14I will saturate the soul of the priests with richness,
and My people will be satisfied with My goodness,
declares the LORD.

Rachel Weeping

15This is what the LORD says:
A voice is heard in Ramah,
lamentation and bitter weeping.
Rachel is weeping for her children;
she refuses to be comforted for her children,
because they are no more.

16This is what the LORD says:
Keep your voice from weeping,
and your eyes from tears;
for there is a reward for your work, declares the LORD,
and they will return from the land of the enemy.

17There is hope for your future, declares the LORD,
and your children will return to their own border.

18I have heard Ephraim grieving:
"You corrected me, and I was corrected,
like an untrained calf.
Bring me back, that I may return,
for You are the LORD my God.

19For after I turned, I repented;
and after I was made to understand, I struck my thigh;
I was ashamed, and humiliated too,
because I bore the disgrace of my youth."

20Is Ephraim My dear son?
Is he My darling child?
For as often as I speak against him,
I still remember him.
Therefore My heart yearns for him;
I will surely have compassion on him,
declares the LORD.

21Set up road markers for yourself;
make yourself guideposts;
set your heart on the highway,
the road by which you went.
Return, virgin Israel,
return to these your cities.

22How long will you waver,
faithless daughter?
For the LORD has created a new thing in the land:
a woman encompasses a man.

23This is what the LORD of hosts, the God of Israel, says: Once more they will say this word in the land of Judah and in its cities, when I restore their fortunes:
"The LORD bless you, abode of righteousness,
holy mountain!"

24Judah and all its cities will live there together, the farmers and those who go about with the flocks.

25For I have saturated the weary soul,
and every languishing soul I have filled.

26At this I awoke and looked, and my sleep was sweet to me.

27Days are coming, declares the LORD, when I will sow the house of Israel and the house of Judah with the seed of man and the seed of beast.

28And it shall come to pass that as I have watched over them to uproot and to pull down, to overthrow, to destroy and to bring disaster, so I will watch over them to build and to plant, declares the LORD.

29In those days they will no longer say,
"The fathers have eaten sour grapes,
and the children's teeth are set on edge."

30But each will die for his own iniquity: every man who eats sour grapes, his own teeth will be set on edge.

The New Covenant

31Days are coming, declares the LORD, when I will make a new covenant with the house of Israel and with the house of Judah,

32not like the covenant that I made with their fathers on the day I took them by the hand to bring them out of the land of Egypt, My covenant that they broke, though I was their husband, declares the LORD.

33For this is the covenant that I will make with the house of Israel after those days, declares the LORD: I will put My law within them, and on their heart I will write it; and I will be their God, and they will be My people.

34No longer will each man teach his neighbor and each his brother, saying, "Know the LORD," for they will all know Me, from the least of them to the greatest, declares the LORD; for I will forgive their iniquity, and their sin I will remember no more.

35This is what the LORD says,
the One who gives the sun for light by day,
and the fixed order of the moon and the stars for light by night,
who stirs up the sea so that its waves roar —
the LORD of hosts is His name:

36If this fixed order departs from before Me, declares the LORD,
then the seed of Israel also will cease
from being a nation before Me forever.

37This is what the LORD says:
If the heavens above can be measured,
and the foundations of the earth below be searched out,
then I too will reject all the seed of Israel
for all that they have done,
declares the LORD.

38Days are coming, declares the LORD, when the city will be rebuilt for the LORD from the Tower of Hananel to the Corner Gate.

39The measuring line will go out farther, straight ahead, to the hill Gareb, and then turn to Goah.

40The whole valley of the corpses and the ashes, and all the fields as far as the Brook Kidron, to the corner of the Horse Gate toward the east, will be holy to the LORD. It will never again be uprooted or overthrown.

Notes

  • v2 "found favor in the wilderness, when Israel went to find its rest" — the wilderness after the golden calf, where Moses was told you have also found favor in My eyes and I will give you rest (Exodus 33:12, 14). The Greek reads I found warmth in the wilderness.

  • v3 "I have loved you with an everlasting love; therefore I have drawn you with loyal love" — meshakhtikh, the verb of Hosea, I drew them with cords of a man, with bands of love (Hosea 11:4). Chesed, loyal love, is the love of a covenant kept.

  • vv8–9 "the blind and the lame… Ephraim is My firstborn" — pisseach, "the lame," has the same letters as pesach, Passover, and the Greek reads it so: I will gather them from the end of the earth at the feast of Passover. The return is told as a second exodus: Israel is My son, My firstborn was the word to Pharaoh (Exodus 4:22), and here the firstborn is Ephraim.

  • vv15–17, 21 "Rachel is weeping for her children… There is hope for your future… make yourself guideposts" — Rachel, mother of Joseph and Benjamin, grandmother of Ephraim, weeps at Ramah, a town of Benjamin (Joshua 18:25). It was at Ramah that the captives were gathered for Babylon, and Jeremiah was released there in chains (40:1). Matthew hears her weeping again at Bethlehem (Matthew 2:18). Tamrurim, "bitter" (v15), is spelled the same as tamrurim, "guideposts" (v21): the bitter weeping is answered by markers on the road home.

  • vv18–22 "Bring me back, that I may return… Return, virgin Israel… faithless daughter" — shuv, "turn," runs through the passage: hashiveni ve-ashuvah (v18), acharei shuvi (v19), shuvi… shuvi (v21), ha-shovevah, "the faithless" (v22), the wordplay of chapter 3. Lamentations ends with Ephraim's prayer in the people's mouth: Bring us back to You, LORD, and we will return (Lamentations 5:21).

  • v22 "the LORD has created a new thing in the land: a woman encompasses a man" — bara, the verb of Genesis 1, said only of God; and neqevah, "female," the word of male and female He created them (Genesis 1:27), here set beside gever, "a strong man." What encompasses means is uncertain: to surround, to protect, to go around. The Greek has the LORD has created salvation for a new planting; in salvation men will go about.

  • v28 "as I have watched over them to uproot and to pull down… so I will watch over them to build and to plant" — the verbs of Jeremiah's call (1:10) and the almond branch: I am watching over My word to do it (1:12), shoqed, the word in both places.

  • vv29–30 "The fathers have eaten sour grapes" — the proverb Ezekiel also hears and answers (Ezekiel 18:2–4). The law already said, each shall be put to death for his own sin (Deuteronomy 24:16).

  • vv31–34 "a new covenant… though I was their husband… on their heart I will write it" — ve-anokhi ba'alti vam, the words of 3:14, for I am your husband. The first covenant was given on tablets of stone (Exodus 31:18), and Judah's sin was cut on the tablet of their heart (17:1); the new one is written there. The letter to the Hebrews quotes vv31–34 from the Greek, which has and I disregarded them for though I was their husband (Hebrews 8:8–12). Jesus: This cup is the new covenant in My blood (Luke 22:20).

  • vv35–37 "who stirs up the sea so that its waves roar — the LORD of hosts is His name" — the last two lines are Isaiah's, letter for letter (Isaiah 51:15). The Greek gives the three verses in another order: v37, then vv35–36.
