chapters.title: The Field at Anathoth
chapters.html:
Jeremiah 32

1The word that came to Jeremiah from the LORD in the tenth year of Zedekiah king of Judah, which was the eighteenth year of Nebuchadnezzar.

2At that time the army of the king of Babylon was besieging Jerusalem, and Jeremiah the prophet was shut up in the court of the guard, which was in the house of the king of Judah,

3where Zedekiah king of Judah had shut him up, saying, "Why do you prophesy, saying, 'This is what the LORD says: I am about to give this city into the hand of the king of Babylon, and he will take it;

4Zedekiah king of Judah will not escape from the hand of the Chaldeans, but will surely be given into the hand of the king of Babylon, and will speak with him mouth to mouth and see him eye to eye;

5he will take Zedekiah to Babylon, and there he will stay until I attend to him, declares the LORD. Though you fight against the Chaldeans, you will not succeed'?"

6Jeremiah said: The word of the LORD came to me, saying,

7"Hanamel son of Shallum your uncle is about to come to you and say, 'Buy my field that is at Anathoth, for the right of redemption is yours to buy it.'"

8Then Hanamel my uncle's son came to me in the court of the guard, as the LORD had said, and said to me, "Buy my field that is at Anathoth in the land of Benjamin, for the right of possession is yours, and the redemption is yours; buy it for yourself." Then I knew that this was the word of the LORD.

9So I bought the field at Anathoth from Hanamel my uncle's son, and weighed out the silver for him, seventeen shekels of silver.

10I signed the deed, sealed it, called witnesses, and weighed the silver on scales.

11Then I took the deed of purchase, both the sealed copy, containing the terms and conditions, and the open copy,

12and I gave the deed of purchase to Baruch son of Neriah son of Mahseiah, in the sight of Hanamel my uncle's son and of the witnesses who had signed the deed of purchase, and in the sight of all the Jews who were sitting in the court of the guard.

13In their sight I charged Baruch, saying,

14"This is what the LORD of hosts, the God of Israel, says: Take these deeds, this deed of purchase, both the sealed copy and this open copy, and put them in an earthenware jar, so that they may last for many days.

15For this is what the LORD of hosts, the God of Israel, says: Houses and fields and vineyards will again be bought in this land."

Jeremiah's Prayer

16After I had given the deed of purchase to Baruch son of Neriah, I prayed to the LORD, saying:

17"Ah, Lord GOD! It is You who made the heavens and the earth by Your great power and Your outstretched arm. Nothing is too wondrous for You.

18You show loyal love to thousands, and repay the guilt of fathers into the lap of their children after them, the great and mighty God, whose name is the LORD of hosts,

19great in counsel and mighty in deed, whose eyes are open on all the ways of the sons of men, to give to each man according to his ways and according to the fruit of his deeds.

20You set signs and wonders in the land of Egypt, and to this day in Israel and among mankind, and have made a name for Yourself, as it is this day.

21You brought Your people Israel out of the land of Egypt with signs and wonders, with a strong hand and an outstretched arm, and with great terror,

22and You gave them this land, which You swore to their fathers to give them, a land flowing with milk and honey.

23They went in and took possession of it, but they did not obey Your voice or walk in Your law; they did nothing of all that You commanded them to do. So You have made all this disaster come upon them.

24The siege ramps have reached the city to take it, and the city is given into the hand of the Chaldeans who are fighting against it, because of the sword, famine and pestilence. What You spoke has come to pass, and You see it.

25Yet You have said to me, Lord GOD, 'Buy the field for money and call witnesses' — though the city is given into the hand of the Chaldeans."

The Answer

26Then the word of the LORD came to Jeremiah, saying,

27"I am the LORD, the God of all flesh. Is anything too wondrous for Me?

28Therefore this is what the LORD says: I am about to give this city into the hand of the Chaldeans and into the hand of Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon, and he will take it.

29The Chaldeans who are fighting against this city will come and set this city on fire and burn it, with the houses on whose roofs they burned incense to Baal and poured out drink offerings to other gods, to provoke Me to anger.

30For the sons of Israel and the sons of Judah have done nothing but evil in My eyes from their youth; the sons of Israel have done nothing but provoke Me to anger with the work of their hands, declares the LORD.

31For this city has roused My anger and My wrath from the day they built it to this day, so that I must remove it from before My face,

32because of all the evil that the sons of Israel and the sons of Judah have done to provoke Me to anger, they, their kings, their princes, their priests and their prophets, the men of Judah and the inhabitants of Jerusalem.

33They have turned their backs to Me, and not their faces; though I taught them again and again, they would not listen and take correction.

34They set their loathsome things in the house that is called by My name, to defile it.

35They built the high places of Baal in the Valley of the Son of Hinnom, to make their sons and their daughters pass over to Molech, which I did not command them, nor did it come into My mind, that they should do this detestable thing, to make Judah sin.

36But now this is what the LORD, the God of Israel, says concerning this city of which you say, 'It is given into the hand of the king of Babylon by the sword, by famine and by pestilence':

37I am about to gather them from all the lands to which I have driven them in My anger and in My fury and in great wrath, and I will bring them back to this place and make them dwell in safety.

38They will be My people, and I will be their God.

39I will give them one heart and one way, to fear Me always, for their own good and the good of their children after them.

40I will make with them an everlasting covenant, that I will not turn back from them, from doing them good; and I will put the fear of Me in their hearts, so that they will not turn away from Me.

41I will rejoice over them to do them good, and I will plant them in this land in faithfulness, with all My heart and with all My soul.

42For this is what the LORD says: Just as I have brought all this great disaster on this people, so I will bring on them all the good that I am promising them.

43Fields will be bought in this land of which you say, 'It is a desolation, without man or beast; it is given into the hand of the Chaldeans.'

44Men will buy fields for money, sign deeds, seal them and call witnesses, in the land of Benjamin, around Jerusalem, in the cities of Judah, in the cities of the hill country, in the cities of the lowland and in the cities of the Negev; for I will restore their fortunes, declares the LORD."

Notes

  • vv1–5 "the tenth year of Zedekiah… shut up in the court of the guard… see him eye to eye" — the siege had begun in Zedekiah's ninth year (2 Kings 25:1); how Jeremiah came to the court of the guard is told in 37:21. Zedekiah did see the king of Babylon eye to eye, and then they slaughtered the sons of Zedekiah before his eyes, then put out the eyes of Zedekiah (2 Kings 25:7).

  • vv7–8 "the right of redemption is yours to buy it" — the law of the redeemer: If your brother becomes poor and sells some of his holding, his redeemer who is closest to him shall come and redeem what his brother has sold (Leviticus 25:25). Boaz took up the same right for Elimelech's field: If you will redeem it, redeem it (Ruth 4:4). Jeremiah is told to buy land the Babylonians already hold.

  • vv10–15 "the sealed copy… and the open copy… an earthenware jar, so that they may last for many days" — an earthenware flask was broken in the Valley of Hinnom as one breaks a potter's jar so that it can never be mended (19:11). This earthenware jar keeps the deed whole for the day of v15, Houses and fields and vineyards will again be bought in this land.

  • v12 "Hanamel my uncle's son" — so the Greek, as vv7–9 have it; the Hebrew here has Chanam'el dodi, "Hanamel my uncle."

  • vv17, 27 "Nothing is too wondrous for You… Is anything too wondrous for Me?" — pala, the word the LORD spoke over Sarah's laughter, Is any word too wondrous for the LORD? (Genesis 18:14). Jeremiah says it in his prayer, which ends on a field bought in a city already lost (v25); the LORD gives his own words back to him as a question. It is You who made the heavens and the earth by Your great power and Your outstretched arm is 27:5 in the prophet's mouth.

  • v18 "You show loyal love to thousands, and repay the guilt of fathers into the lap of their children" — the words of Sinai, doing loyal love to thousands (Exodus 20:6) and calling the guilt of fathers to account on sons (34:7); into their lap as in Isaiah 65:6.

  • vv33–35 "They have turned their backs to Me, and not their faces… their loathsome things in the house that is called by My name… nor did it come into My mind" — the charges of 2:27 and 7:30–31, nearly word for word, now given as the reason the city falls. To make their sons and their daughters pass over to Molech is the act the law forbade (Leviticus 18:21).

  • vv37, 39 "in My anger and in My fury and in great wrath… one heart and one way" — the words with which the LORD fought against the city (21:5) are the anger that scattered them, and the same LORD gathers them. For one heart and one way the Greek has another way and another heart: echad, "one," and acher, "another," differ by one letter (d and r).

  • vv40–41 "an everlasting covenant… with all My heart and with all My soul" — the new covenant of 31:31–34 under another name. With all My heart and with all My soul is the great command, You shall love the LORD your God with all your heart and with all your soul (Deuteronomy 6:5), said by the LORD of Himself, and nowhere else.

speech.text: Jeremiah 32
The word that came to Jeremiah from the LORD in the tenth year of Zedekiah king of Judah, which was the eighteenth year of Nebuchadnezzar.
At that time the army of the king of Babylon was besieging Jerusalem, and Jeremiah the prophet was shut up in the court of the guard, which was in the house of the king of Judah,

where Zedekiah king of Judah had shut him up, saying, "Why do you prophesy, saying, 'This is what the LORD says: I am about to give this city into the hand of the king of Babylon, and he will take it;
Zedekiah king of Judah will not escape from the hand of the Chaldeans, but will surely be given into the hand of the king of Babylon, and will speak with him mouth to mouth and see him eye to eye;
he will take Zedekiah to Babylon, and there he will stay until I attend to him, declares the LORD. Though you fight against the Chaldeans, you will not succeed'?"
Jeremiah said: The word of the LORD came to me, saying,
"Hanamel son of Shallum your uncle is about to come to you and say, 'Buy my field that is at Anathoth, for the right of redemption is yours to buy it.'"

Then Hanamel my uncle's son came to me in the court of the guard, as the LORD had said, and said to me, "Buy my field that is at Anathoth in the land of Benjamin, for the right of possession is yours, and the redemption is yours; buy it for yourself." Then I knew that this was the word of the LORD.
So I bought the field at Anathoth from Hanamel my uncle's son, and weighed out the silver for him, seventeen shekels of silver.
I signed the deed, sealed it, called witnesses, and weighed the silver on scales.
Then I took the deed of purchase, both the sealed copy, containing the terms and conditions, and the open copy,

and I gave the deed of purchase to Baruch son of Neriah son of Mahseiah, in the sight of Hanamel my uncle's son and of the witnesses who had signed the deed of purchase, and in the sight of all the Jews who were sitting in the court of the guard.
In their sight I charged Baruch, saying,

"This is what the LORD of hosts, the God of Israel, says: Take these deeds, this deed of purchase, both the sealed copy and this open copy, and put them in an earthenware jar, so that they may last for many days.
For this is what the LORD of hosts, the God of Israel, says: Houses and fields and vineyards will again be bought in this land."
Jeremiah's Prayer
After I had given the deed of purchase to Baruch son of Neriah, I prayed to the LORD, saying:
"Ah, Lord GOD! It is You who made the heavens and the earth by Your great power and Your outstretched arm. Nothing is too wondrous for You.
You show loyal love to thousands, and repay the guilt of fathers into the lap of their children after them, the great and mighty God, whose name is the LORD of hosts,
great in counsel and mighty in deed, whose eyes are open on all the ways of the sons of men, to give to each man according to his ways and according to the fruit of his deeds.
You set signs and wonders in the land of Egypt, and to this day in Israel and among mankind, and have made a name for Yourself, as it is this day.
You brought Your people Israel out of the land of Egypt with signs and wonders, with a strong hand and an outstretched arm, and with great terror,
and You gave them this land, which You swore to their fathers to give them, a land flowing with milk and honey.

Then the word of the LORD came to Jeremiah, saying,
"I am the LORD, the God of all flesh. Is anything too wondrous for Me?
Therefore this is what the LORD says: I am about to give this city into the hand of the Chaldeans and into the hand of Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon, and he will take it.

The Chaldeans who are fighting against this city will come and set this city on fire and burn it, with the houses on whose roofs they burned incense to Baal and poured out drink offerings to other gods, to provoke Me to anger.

because of all the evil that the sons of Israel and the sons of Judah have done to provoke Me to anger, they, their kings, their princes, their priests and their prophets, the men of Judah and the inhabitants of Jerusalem.

They built the high places of Baal in the Valley of the Son of Hinnom, to make their sons and their daughters pass over to Molech, which I did not command them, nor did it come into My mind, that they should do this detestable thing, to make Judah sin.
But now this is what the LORD, the God of Israel, says concerning this city of which you say, 'It is given into the hand of the king of Babylon by the sword, by famine and by pestilence':
I am about to gather them from all the lands to which I have driven them in My anger and in My fury and in great wrath, and I will bring them back to this place and make them dwell in safety.
They will be My people, and I will be their God.
I will give them one heart and one way, to fear Me always, for their own good and the good of their children after them.
I will make with them an everlasting covenant, that I will not turn back from them, from doing them good; and I will put the fear of Me in their hearts, so that they will not turn away from Me.
I will rejoice over them to do them good, and I will plant them in this land in faithfulness, with all My heart and with all My soul.

chapters.title: Great and Inaccessible Things
chapters.html:
Jeremiah 33

1The word of the LORD came to Jeremiah a second time, while he was still shut up in the court of the guard, saying,

2This is what the LORD says, the One who made it,
the LORD who formed it to establish it —
the LORD is His name:

3Call to Me, and I will answer you,
and I will tell you great and inaccessible things
that you have not known.

4For this is what the LORD, the God of Israel, says concerning the houses of this city and the houses of the kings of Judah that are torn down to hold off the siege ramps and the sword:

5Men come to fight against the Chaldeans, only to fill those houses with the corpses of the men whom I have struck down in My anger and My wrath; for I have hidden My face from this city because of all their evil.

6I am about to bring it new flesh and healing; I will heal them and reveal to them an abundance of peace and truth.

7I will restore the fortunes of Judah and the fortunes of Israel, and build them as they were at first.

8I will cleanse them from all their iniquity by which they have sinned against Me, and I will forgive all their iniquities by which they have sinned against Me and rebelled against Me.

9This city will be to Me a name of joy, a praise and a glory before all the nations of the earth, who will hear of all the good that I am doing for them; they will fear and tremble because of all the good and all the peace that I am doing for it.

10This is what the LORD says: Once more there will be heard in this place, of which you say, "It is a ruin, without man or beast," in the cities of Judah and in the streets of Jerusalem that are desolate, without man, without inhabitant and without beast,

11the voice of mirth and the voice of gladness, the voice of the bridegroom and the voice of the bride, the voice of those who say,
"Give thanks to the LORD of hosts,
for the LORD is good,
for His loyal love endures forever,"
as they bring thank offerings to the house of the LORD. For I will restore the fortunes of the land as at first, says the LORD.

12This is what the LORD of hosts says: Once more there will be in this place, which is a ruin without man or beast, and in all its cities, pastures where shepherds rest their flocks.

13In the cities of the hill country, in the cities of the lowland and in the cities of the Negev, in the land of Benjamin, around Jerusalem and in the cities of Judah, flocks will again pass under the hands of the one who counts them, says the LORD.

A Branch of Righteousness

14Days are coming, declares the LORD, when I will fulfill the good word that I have spoken concerning the house of Israel and the house of Judah.

15In those days and at that time
I will make a Branch of righteousness sprout for David,
and he will do justice and righteousness in the land.

16In those days Judah will be saved,
and Jerusalem will dwell in safety;
and this is the name by which she will be called:
The LORD Is Our Righteousness.

17For this is what the LORD says: David will never lack a man to sit on the throne of the house of Israel,

18and the Levitical priests will never lack a man before Me to offer burnt offerings, to burn grain offerings and to make sacrifices all the days.

19The word of the LORD came to Jeremiah, saying,

20This is what the LORD says: If you can break My covenant with the day and My covenant with the night, so that day and night do not come at their time,

21then My covenant with David My servant can also be broken, so that he would have no son to reign on his throne, and My covenant with the Levitical priests, My ministers.

22As the host of heaven cannot be counted and the sand of the sea cannot be measured, so I will multiply the seed of David My servant and the Levites who minister to Me.

23The word of the LORD came to Jeremiah, saying,

24Have you not seen what this people have said: "The two clans that the LORD chose, He has rejected"? So they despise My people, as though they were no longer a nation in their sight.

25This is what the LORD says: If I have not established My covenant with day and night, and the fixed order of heaven and earth,

26then I will also reject the seed of Jacob and of David My servant, and not take from his seed rulers over the seed of Abraham, Isaac and Jacob. For I will restore their fortunes and have compassion on them.

Notes

  • v2 "the One who made it, the LORD who formed it to establish it" — yotser, "who formed," is the potter at his wheel (18:4–6): the LORD shapes what He has made. The Hebrew does not say what it is; the Greek has who makes the earth.

  • v3 "great and inaccessible things that you have not known" — betsurot, the word for walled cities: the spies came back with the cities are great and fortified up to the heavens (Deuteronomy 1:28), gedolot u-vetsurot, the same pair. What was walled off the LORD will open. Isaiah has a near word, hidden things that you have not known (netsurot, Isaiah 48:6).

  • vv4–5 "the houses… torn down to hold off the siege ramps and the sword" — as Isaiah said of Jerusalem under threat, you tore down the houses to fortify the wall (Isaiah 22:10). The Hebrew of these two verses is broken in places, and the English follows the sense.

  • v6 "I am about to bring it new flesh and healing" — arukhah, the healing the prophet asked for, Why then has the daughter of my people not been healed? (8:22), and promised in 30:17, I will make new flesh grow for you.

  • v9 "a name of joy, a praise and a glory… they will fear and tremble because of all the good" — the words of the loincloth: the LORD made Israel cling to Him to be for Me a people, a name, a praise and a glory; but they did not listen (13:11). The nations will tremble at the LORD's goodness, as Hosea said Israel would come trembling to the LORD and to His goodness in the end of days (Hosea 3:5).

  • vv10–11 "the voice of mirth… the voice of the bridegroom and the voice of the bride… Give thanks to the LORD of hosts, for the LORD is good" — the voices silenced at 7:34, 16:9 and 25:10 come back, with the song of the temple added: Give thanks to the LORD, for He is good, for His loyal love endures forever (Psalm 136:1).

  • v13 "flocks will again pass under the hands of the one who counts them" — the shepherd's evening count. The law used the same picture for the tithe of the flock, every tenth one that passes under the rod (Leviticus 27:32).

  • vv14–16 "a Branch of righteousness… The LORD Is Our Righteousness" — 23:5–6 again, with changes: a Branch of righteousness (tsemach tsedaqah) for a righteous Branch, I will make… sprout (atsmiach, the verb of tsemach), and the name given now to Jerusalem, by which she will be called. The Greek has nothing of vv14–26.

  • vv17–22 "David will never lack a man to sit on the throne… as the sand of the sea cannot be measured" — the promise to David, you shall not lack a man on the throne of Israel (1 Kings 2:4), and to Abraham, I will multiply your seed as the stars of the heavens and as the sand that is on the lip of the sea (Genesis 22:17). The covenant with day and night is the one made after the flood, day and night shall not cease (Genesis 8:22).

  • vv24–26 "The two clans that the LORD chose, He has rejected" — Israel and Judah, the two kingdoms of v14; v26 answers with the seed of Jacob and of David My servant.

chapters.title: Liberty Proclaimed and Taken Back
chapters.html:
Jeremiah 34

1The word that came to Jeremiah from the LORD, when Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon and all his army, all the kingdoms of the earth under his rule and all the peoples were fighting against Jerusalem and all its cities:

2This is what the LORD, the God of Israel, says: Go and speak to Zedekiah king of Judah, and say to him: This is what the LORD says: I am about to give this city into the hand of the king of Babylon, and he will burn it with fire.

3You will not escape from his hand, but will surely be captured and given into his hand; your eyes will see the eyes of the king of Babylon, and he will speak with you mouth to mouth, and you will go to Babylon.

4Yet hear the word of the LORD, Zedekiah king of Judah: This is what the LORD says concerning you: You will not die by the sword.

5You will die in peace; and as they burned for your fathers, the former kings who were before you, so they will burn for you, and lament for you, "Alas, lord!" For I Myself have spoken the word, declares the LORD.

6Then Jeremiah the prophet spoke all these words to Zedekiah king of Judah in Jerusalem,

7while the army of the king of Babylon was fighting against Jerusalem and against all the cities of Judah that were left, against Lachish and Azekah; for these were the only fortified cities left among the cities of Judah.

The Slaves Set Free

8The word that came to Jeremiah from the LORD, after King Zedekiah had made a covenant with all the people in Jerusalem to proclaim liberty to them:

9that each should set free his male servant and his female servant, a Hebrew man or a Hebrew woman, so that no one should keep a fellow Jew in servitude.

10All the princes and all the people who had entered into the covenant obeyed: each would set free his male servant and his female servant, so as not to keep them in servitude any longer. They obeyed and let them go.

11But afterward they turned around and took back the male and female servants whom they had set free, and brought them into subjection as male and female servants.

12Then the word of the LORD came to Jeremiah from the LORD, saying,

13This is what the LORD, the God of Israel, says: I Myself made a covenant with your fathers on the day I brought them out of the land of Egypt, out of the house of slaves, saying,

14"At the end of seven years each of you shall set free his brother, the Hebrew who has been sold to you and has served you six years; you shall set him free from you." But your fathers did not listen to Me or incline their ear.

15You yourselves had turned today and done what is right in My eyes, proclaiming liberty each to his neighbor, and you had made a covenant before Me in the house that is called by My name;

16but then you turned back and profaned My name, and each of you took back his male servant and his female servant whom you had set free to go where they wished, and you brought them into subjection to be your male and female servants.

17Therefore this is what the LORD says: You have not obeyed Me by proclaiming liberty each to his brother and each to his neighbor. I am about to proclaim liberty for you, declares the LORD — to the sword, to pestilence and to famine; and I will make you a horror to all the kingdoms of the earth.

18I will make the men who transgressed My covenant, who did not keep the words of the covenant that they made before Me, like the calf that they cut in two and passed between its halves —

19the princes of Judah and the princes of Jerusalem, the eunuchs, the priests and all the people of the land who passed between the halves of the calf.

20I will give them into the hand of their enemies and into the hand of those who seek their life, and their corpses will be food for the birds of the heavens and for the beasts of the earth.

21Zedekiah king of Judah and his princes I will give into the hand of their enemies, into the hand of those who seek their life, and into the hand of the army of the king of Babylon, which has withdrawn from you.

22I am about to give the command, declares the LORD, and I will bring them back to this city; they will fight against it, take it and burn it with fire; and I will make the cities of Judah a desolation, without inhabitant.

Notes

  • vv3–5 "your eyes will see the eyes of the king of Babylon… You will die in peace… so they will burn for you, and lament for you, 'Alas, lord!'" — what 32:4 said, with a promise added: you will not die by the sword. The burning is the fire made at a king's burial, as for Asa, they made a very great fire in his honor (2 Chronicles 16:14); Alas, lord! is the lament denied to Jehoiakim (22:18). Zedekiah did see the king of Babylon, and then they put out the eyes of Zedekiah (2 Kings 25:7).

  • v7 "Lachish and Azekah" — two of the cities Rehoboam fortified (2 Chronicles 11:9), the last walls of Judah still standing besides Jerusalem.

  • vv8–10 "to proclaim liberty" — deror, the word of the jubilee, proclaim liberty in the land to all who live in it (Leviticus 25:10), and of Isaiah's anointed one, to proclaim liberty to the captives (Isaiah 61:1).

  • v14 "At the end of seven years… who has been sold to you and has served you six years" — two sentences of the law joined: At the end of every seven years you shall make a release (Deuteronomy 15:1), and he shall serve you six years, and in the seventh year you shall send him away from you free (15:12). The Greek has when six years are complete.

  • vv11, 15–16 "they turned around… You yourselves had turned today… but then you turned back" — shuv, "turn," three ways in six verses: they turned around and took the servants back (va-yashuvu… va-yashivu, v11), they had turned to do right (v15), and they turned back (v16).

  • v17 "I am about to proclaim liberty for you… to the sword" — deror again. The freedom they would not give their servants the LORD gives them: they are set free to the sword, pestilence and famine.

  • vv18–20 "the calf that they cut in two and passed between its halves" — the rite of the covenant with Abram, who cut them in two through the middle, and set each piece opposite its fellow (bitro, Genesis 15:10); the fire passed between those pieces (15:17). Beter, "half," is found only there and here. Ha-overim et beriti, "who transgressed My covenant," and va-ya'avru, "they passed," are the same verb: they crossed between the halves, and then crossed the covenant. Ve-natatti et ha-anashim… ha-egel, "I will make the men… the calf," has no word for like: the verb takes the men and the calf as its two objects, as in father of a roar of nations I have made you (Genesis 17:5, netattikha). Read so, what was done to the calf is done to them, and their corpses will be food for the birds (v20).

  • vv21–22 "the army of the king of Babylon, which has withdrawn from you… I will bring them back" — the siege was lifted for a time when Pharaoh's army came out of Egypt (37:5, 11). The servants were freed with the enemy at the gates (vv1, 7); now the army has withdrawn (v21), and the servants have been taken back (v11).

speech.text: Jeremiah 34

The word that came to Jeremiah from the LORD, when Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon and all his army, all the kingdoms of the earth under his rule and all the peoples were fighting against Jerusalem and all its cities:

This is what the LORD, the God of Israel, says: Go and speak to Zedekiah king of Judah, and say to him: This is what the LORD says: I am about to give this city into the hand of the king of Babylon, and he will burn it with fire.

You will not escape from his hand, but will surely be captured and given into his hand; your eyes will see the eyes of the king of Babylon, and he will speak with you mouth to mouth, and you will go to Babylon.
Yet hear the word of the LORD, Zedekiah king of Judah: This is what the LORD says concerning you: You will not die by the sword.

You will die in peace; and as they burned for your fathers, the former kings who were before you, so they will burn for you, and lament for you, "Alas, lord!" For I Myself have spoken the word, declares the LORD.
Then Jeremiah the prophet spoke all these words to Zedekiah king of Judah in Jerusalem,

while the army of the king of Babylon was fighting against Jerusalem and against all the cities of Judah that were left, against Lachish and Azekah; for these were the only fortified cities left among the cities of Judah.
The Slaves Set Free
The word that came to Jeremiah from the LORD, after King Zedekiah had made a covenant with all the people in Jerusalem to proclaim liberty to them:
that each should set free his male servant and his female servant, a Hebrew man or a Hebrew woman, so that no one should keep a fellow Jew in servitude.

All the princes and all the people who had entered into the covenant obeyed: each would set free his male servant and his female servant, so as not to keep them in servitude any longer. They obeyed and let them go.
But afterward they turned around and took back the male and female servants whom they had set free, and brought them into subjection as male and female servants.
Then the word of the LORD came to Jeremiah from the LORD, saying,
This is what the LORD, the God of Israel, says: I Myself made a covenant with your fathers on the day I brought them out of the land of Egypt, out of the house of slaves, saying,

"At the end of seven years each of you shall set free his brother, the Hebrew who has been sold to you and has served you six years; you shall set him free from you." But your fathers did not listen to Me or incline their ear.
You yourselves had turned today and done what is right in My eyes, proclaiming liberty each to his neighbor, and you had made a covenant before Me in the house that is called by My name;

but then you turned back and profaned My name, and each of you took back his male servant and his female servant whom you had set free to go where they wished, and you brought them into subjection to be your male and female servants.

Therefore this is what the LORD says: You have not obeyed Me by proclaiming liberty each to his brother and each to his neighbor. I am about to proclaim liberty for you, declares the LORD — to the sword, to pestilence and to famine; and I will make you a horror to all the kingdoms of the earth.
I will make the men who transgressed My covenant, who did not keep the words of the covenant that they made before Me, like the calf that they cut in two and passed between its halves —
the princes of Judah and the princes of Jerusalem, the eunuchs, the priests and all the people of the land who passed between the halves of the calf.
I will give them into the hand of their enemies and into the hand of those who seek their life, and their corpses will be food for the birds of the heavens and for the beasts of the earth.

Zedekiah king of Judah and his princes I will give into the hand of their enemies, into the hand of those who seek their life, and into the hand of the army of the king of Babylon, which has withdrawn from you.

I am about to give the command, declares the LORD, and I will bring them back to this city; they will fight against it, take it and burn it with fire; and I will make the cities of Judah a desolation, without inhabitant.

chapters.title: The Rechabites
chapters.html:
Jeremiah 35

1The word that came to Jeremiah from the LORD in the days of Jehoiakim son of Josiah, king of Judah:

2"Go to the house of the Rechabites and speak to them, and bring them to the house of the LORD, into one of the chambers, and give them wine to drink."

3So I took Jaazaniah son of Jeremiah, son of Habazziniah, and his brothers and all his sons, and the whole house of the Rechabites,

4and I brought them into the house of the LORD, to the chamber of the sons of Hanan son of Igdaliah, the man of God, which was next to the chamber of the princes, above the chamber of Maaseiah son of Shallum, the keeper of the threshold.

5Then I set before the men of the house of the Rechabites bowls full of wine, and cups, and I said to them, "Drink wine."

6But they said, "We will drink no wine, for Jonadab son of Rechab our father commanded us, 'You shall drink no wine, neither you nor your sons, forever.

7You shall not build a house or sow seed or plant a vineyard, or have any; but you shall live in tents all your days, so that you may live many days on the face of the ground where you live as guests.'

8We have obeyed the voice of Jehonadab son of Rechab our father in all that he commanded us: to drink no wine all our days, we, our wives, our sons and our daughters,

9and not to build houses to live in. We have no vineyard or field or seed.

10We have lived in tents, and have obeyed and done all that Jonadab our father commanded us.

11But when Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon came up against the land, we said, 'Come, let us go to Jerusalem, away from the army of the Chaldeans and the army of Aram.' So we are living in Jerusalem."

12Then the word of the LORD came to Jeremiah, saying,

13This is what the LORD of hosts, the God of Israel, says: Go and say to the men of Judah and the inhabitants of Jerusalem: Will you not take correction and listen to My words? declares the LORD.

14The words of Jehonadab son of Rechab, which he commanded his sons, to drink no wine, have been kept; they have drunk none to this day, for they have obeyed their father's command. But I Myself have spoken to you again and again, and you have not listened to Me.

15I have sent to you all My servants the prophets again and again, saying, "Turn now, each of you, from his evil way, and amend your deeds, and do not go after other gods to serve them; then you will live on the land that I gave to you and to your fathers." But you did not incline your ear or listen to Me.

16The sons of Jehonadab son of Rechab have kept the command of their father which he commanded them, but this people has not listened to Me.

17Therefore this is what the LORD, the God of hosts, the God of Israel, says: I am about to bring on Judah and on all the inhabitants of Jerusalem all the disaster that I have pronounced against them, because I spoke to them and they did not listen, and I called to them and they did not answer.

18To the house of the Rechabites Jeremiah said, "This is what the LORD of hosts, the God of Israel, says: Because you have obeyed the command of Jehonadab your father, and kept all his commands, and done all that he commanded you,

19therefore this is what the LORD of hosts, the God of Israel, says: Jonadab son of Rechab will never lack a man to stand before Me all the days."

Notes

  • v2 "the house of the Rechabites" — the line of Jehonadab son of Rechab, who rode in Jehu's chariot when Jehu wiped out the house of Ahab and the worshippers of Baal (2 Kings 10:15–23). Chronicles counts the house of Rechab among the Kenites (1 Chronicles 2:55), the people of the Kenite, Moses' father-in-law, who came up with Judah into the wilderness (Judges 1:16).

  • vv6–7 "You shall drink no wine… you shall live in tents all your days, so that you may live many days on the face of the ground where you live as guests" — a long life on the ground, the promise the law attaches to honoring father and mother, so that your days may be long on the ground (Exodus 20:12); these sons honor their father's word. They are guests (garim) in the land and live like it, with no house, field or vineyard of their own. To the exiles in Babylon Jeremiah said the opposite: Build houses… plant gardens (29:5).

  • v11 "the army of the Chaldeans and the army of Aram" — the raiders Kings names in Jehoiakim's day, bands of Chaldeans, bands of Arameans, bands of Moabites and bands of Ammonites (2 Kings 24:2). The Greek has the army of the Assyrians. The tent-dwellers have come inside the walls of Jerusalem and still keep their father's rule.

  • vv13–16 "Will you not take correction… The words of Jehonadab… have been kept… But I Myself have spoken to you again and again" — the argument runs from the lesser to the greater: a man's command to his sons is kept for generations, and the LORD's word, sent again and again (hashkem), is not kept at all. Turn now, each of you, from his evil way is 25:5 word for word.

  • v17 "I spoke to them and they did not listen, and I called to them and they did not answer" — the charge of the temple sermon, I spoke to you again and again, but you did not listen, and I called you, but you did not answer (7:13).

  • v19 "Jonadab son of Rechab will never lack a man to stand before Me" — the words of the promises to David and to the Levitical priests, will never lack a man (33:17–18). To stand before the LORD is the service of the Levites (Deuteronomy 10:8), and the prophet's place: you shall stand before Me (15:19), and Elijah's oath, As the LORD… lives, before whom I stand (1 Kings 17:1).

chapters.title: The Scroll Burned and Written Again
chapters.html:
Jeremiah 36

1And it came to pass in the fourth year of Jehoiakim son of Josiah, king of Judah, that this word came to Jeremiah from the LORD:

2"Take a scroll and write on it all the words that I have spoken to you concerning Israel and Judah and all the nations, from the day I first spoke to you, in the days of Josiah, until this day.

3Perhaps the house of Judah will hear all the disaster that I intend to do to them, so that each will turn from his evil way, and I will forgive their iniquity and their sin."

4Then Jeremiah called Baruch son of Neriah, and Baruch wrote on the scroll at Jeremiah's dictation all the words of the LORD that He had spoken to him.

5Jeremiah commanded Baruch, saying, "I am barred; I cannot go into the house of the LORD.

6So you go, and on a fast day read the words of the LORD from the scroll that you have written at my dictation, in the hearing of the people in the house of the LORD. Read them also in the hearing of all Judah who come in from their cities.

7Perhaps their plea will come before the LORD, and each will turn from his evil way; for great is the anger and the wrath that the LORD has pronounced against this people."

8Baruch son of Neriah did all that Jeremiah the prophet commanded him, reading from the book the words of the LORD in the house of the LORD.

9And it came to pass in the fifth year of Jehoiakim son of Josiah, king of Judah, in the ninth month, that all the people in Jerusalem and all the people who came from the cities of Judah to Jerusalem proclaimed a fast before the LORD.

10Then Baruch read from the book the words of Jeremiah in the house of the LORD, in the chamber of Gemariah son of Shaphan the scribe, in the upper court, at the entrance of the New Gate of the LORD's house, in the hearing of all the people.

11When Micaiah son of Gemariah, son of Shaphan, heard all the words of the LORD from the book,

12he went down to the king's house, to the scribe's chamber; and all the princes were sitting there: Elishama the scribe, Delaiah son of Shemaiah, Elnathan son of Achbor, Gemariah son of Shaphan, Zedekiah son of Hananiah and all the princes.

13Micaiah told them all the words that he had heard when Baruch read the book in the hearing of the people.

14Then all the princes sent Jehudi son of Nethaniah, son of Shelemiah, son of Cushi, to Baruch, saying, "Take in your hand the scroll that you read in the hearing of the people, and come." So Baruch son of Neriah took the scroll in his hand and came to them.

15They said to him, "Sit down, please, and read it in our hearing." So Baruch read it in their hearing.

16When they had heard all the words, they turned to one another in fear, and they said to Baruch, "We must surely tell the king all these words."

17They asked Baruch, "Tell us, please, how did you write all these words? Was it at his dictation?"

18Baruch said to them, "He dictated all these words to me, and I wrote them in the book with ink."

19Then the princes said to Baruch, "Go and hide, you and Jeremiah, and let no one know where you are."

20They went in to the king in the court, having left the scroll in the chamber of Elishama the scribe, and they told all the words in the hearing of the king.

21The king sent Jehudi to get the scroll, and he took it from the chamber of Elishama the scribe. Jehudi read it in the hearing of the king and of all the princes who stood beside the king.

22The king was sitting in the winter house in the ninth month, with a fire burning in the brazier before him.

23As Jehudi read three or four columns, the king would cut them off with the scribe's knife and throw them into the fire in the brazier, until the whole scroll was consumed in the fire that was in the brazier.

24Yet neither the king nor any of his servants who heard all these words was afraid, nor did they tear their garments.

25Even when Elnathan, Delaiah and Gemariah pleaded with the king not to burn the scroll, he would not listen to them.

26The king commanded Jerahmeel the king's son, Seraiah son of Azriel and Shelemiah son of Abdeel to seize Baruch the scribe and Jeremiah the prophet; but the LORD hid them.

The Second Scroll

27Then the word of the LORD came to Jeremiah, after the king had burned the scroll with the words that Baruch had written at Jeremiah's dictation, saying,

28"Take another scroll, and write on it all the former words that were on the first scroll, which Jehoiakim king of Judah burned.

29Concerning Jehoiakim king of Judah you shall say: This is what the LORD says: You burned this scroll, saying, 'Why have you written on it that the king of Babylon will surely come and destroy this land, and cut off from it man and beast?'

30Therefore this is what the LORD says concerning Jehoiakim king of Judah: He will have no one to sit on the throne of David, and his dead body will be thrown out to the heat by day and to the frost by night.

31I will punish him and his seed and his servants for their iniquity, and I will bring on them and on the inhabitants of Jerusalem and on the men of Judah all the disaster that I have pronounced against them, and they did not listen."

32Then Jeremiah took another scroll and gave it to Baruch son of Neriah, the scribe, and he wrote on it at Jeremiah's dictation all the words of the book that Jehoiakim king of Judah had burned in the fire; and many similar words were added to them.

Notes

  • vv1–3 "the fourth year of Jehoiakim… Take a scroll… Perhaps the house of Judah will hear… and I will forgive" — the year of 25:1, when Nebuchadnezzar defeated Pharaoh at Carchemish (46:2). Megillat sefer, "a scroll," the words of the psalm, in the scroll of the book it is written of me (Psalm 40:7). Perhaps is the hope of 26:3, given again.

  • vv4, 17–18, 32 "at Jeremiah's dictation… He dictated all these words to me, and I wrote them in the book with ink… many similar words were added" — mi-pi Yirmeyahu, "from Jeremiah's mouth," six times in the chapter: the book is made from the prophet's mouth by the scribe's hand. The scroll the king burned was written again, with more besides; the book of Jeremiah as it stands is that second scroll and what was added to it.

  • v9 "in the fifth year… in the ninth month… a fast" — a year after the scroll was written (v1). The Greek has the eighth year.

  • vv10–12 "the chamber of Gemariah son of Shaphan the scribe… Elishama the scribe" — Shaphan was the secretary who read the book of the law found in the temple to King Josiah (2 Kings 22:8–10). Now the scroll is read in his son's chamber, and his grandson Micaiah carries it to the princes.

  • vv23–24 "the king would cut them off with the scribe's knife… neither the king nor any of his servants… was afraid, nor did they tear their garments" — When the king heard the words of the book of the instruction, he tore his clothes (2 Kings 22:11): so Josiah. His son cuts the scroll column by column with the scribe's knife and feeds it to the fire. Pachadu, "afraid": the princes were afraid when they heard it (v16); the king was not.

  • v25 "pleaded with the king not to burn the scroll" — Elnathan, the king's agent against Uriah (26:22), here pleads for the scroll. The Greek reads it the other way: Elnathan and Gedaliah urged the king to burn the scroll.

  • v26 "but the LORD hid them" — the princes told them to hide (v19); the Hebrew credits the hiding to the LORD. The Greek has only and they were hidden.

  • v30 "He will have no one to sit on the throne of David, and his dead body will be thrown out to the heat by day and to the frost by night" — the sentence of 22:18–19, the burial of a donkey… thrown out beyond the gates of Jerusalem. His son Jehoiachin reigned three months (2 Kings 24:8) and was taken to Babylon, and of him 22:30 says, no man of his seed will prosper, sitting on the throne of David.

chapters.title: Is There a Word from the LORD?
chapters.html:
Jeremiah 37

1Zedekiah son of Josiah, whom Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon made king in the land of Judah, reigned as king in place of Coniah son of Jehoiakim.

2But neither he nor his servants nor the people of the land listened to the words of the LORD that He spoke through Jeremiah the prophet.

3King Zedekiah sent Jehucal son of Shelemiah and Zephaniah son of Maaseiah, the priest, to Jeremiah the prophet, saying, "Please pray for us to the LORD our God."

4Jeremiah was still coming and going among the people, for they had not yet put him in prison.

5Pharaoh's army had come out of Egypt; and when the Chaldeans who were besieging Jerusalem heard the news of them, they withdrew from Jerusalem.

6Then the word of the LORD came to Jeremiah the prophet, saying,

7This is what the LORD, the God of Israel, says: This is what you shall say to the king of Judah, who sent you to Me to inquire of Me: Pharaoh's army, which came out to help you, is about to return to its own land, Egypt.

8The Chaldeans will come back and fight against this city; they will take it and burn it with fire.

9This is what the LORD says: Do not deceive yourselves, saying, "The Chaldeans will surely go away from us," for they will not go.

10For even if you struck down the whole army of the Chaldeans who are fighting against you, and only men who had been run through were left among them, each in his tent, they would get up and burn this city with fire.

Arrested at the Benjamin Gate

11And it came to pass, when the army of the Chaldeans had withdrawn from Jerusalem because of Pharaoh's army,

12that Jeremiah went out of Jerusalem to go to the land of Benjamin, to take his share there among the people.

13When he was at the Benjamin Gate, an officer in charge there, whose name was Irijah son of Shelemiah, son of Hananiah, seized Jeremiah the prophet, saying, "You are going over to the Chaldeans!"

14Jeremiah said, "That is a lie! I am not going over to the Chaldeans." But he would not listen to him; Irijah seized Jeremiah and brought him to the princes.

15The princes were angry with Jeremiah; they beat him and put him in confinement in the house of Jonathan the scribe, for they had made it the prison.

16When Jeremiah had gone into the cistern house, into the vaults, he stayed there many days.

17Then King Zedekiah sent for him and had him brought, and the king asked him secretly in his house, "Is there a word from the LORD?" Jeremiah said, "There is." Then he said, "You will be given into the hand of the king of Babylon."

18Jeremiah also said to King Zedekiah, "What sin have I committed against you or your servants or this people, that you have put me in prison?

19Where are your prophets who prophesied to you, saying, 'The king of Babylon will not come against you or against this land'?

20So now, please listen, my lord the king: let my plea come before you, and do not send me back to the house of Jonathan the scribe, so that I do not die there."

21Then King Zedekiah gave orders, and they committed Jeremiah to the court of the guard, and he was given a loaf of bread daily from the bakers' street, until all the bread in the city was gone. So Jeremiah stayed in the court of the guard.

Notes

  • v1 "Zedekiah son of Josiah, whom Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon made king… in place of Coniah son of Jehoiakim" — The king of Babylon made Mattaniah, Jehoiachin's uncle, king in his place, and changed his name to Zedekiah (2 Kings 24:17). Coniah is Jehoiachin, the signet ring the LORD would tear off (22:24). The Greek has in place of Joakim, with no Coniah son of.

  • v3 "Please pray for us to the LORD our God" — the LORD had told Jeremiah do not pray for this people (7:16; 11:14), and Do not pray for the good of this people (14:11). Zedekiah had sent before, with the same Zephaniah, to ask Please inquire of the LORD for us (21:1–2).

  • vv5, 11 "they withdrew from Jerusalem" — what Zedekiah had hoped for, that the LORD would make him withdraw from us (21:2): alah me-al, the same verb. This is the withdrawal of 34:21, when the servants were taken back.

  • vv7–8 "Pharaoh's army, which came out to help you, is about to return to its own land, Egypt" — the warning of the book's first chapters: You will be put to shame by Egypt as you were put to shame by Assyria (2:36).

  • vv11–12 "And it came to pass… that Jeremiah went out of Jerusalem… to take his share there among the people" — ve-hayah, the form that usually looks ahead, here tells what happened, as again at 38:28. La-chaloq, "to share," is the verb of dividing an inheritance; the Hebrew does not say what share. His family was of Anathoth in the land of Benjamin (1:1), where he later bought his cousin's field while held in the court of the guard (32:2, 8). The Greek has to buy.

  • vv13–14 "You are going over to the Chaldeans!… That is a lie!" — nafal, the verb of his own counsel: whoever goes out and surrenders to the Chaldeans who are besieging you will live (21:9). The charge matched his words, and he denies it of himself.

  • vv15–16, 20 "the house of Jonathan the scribe… the cistern house" — bor, "cistern," the word of the cistern he is thrown into next (38:6). He begs not to be sent back to the scribe's house so that I do not die there, and the king tells him to say the same to the princes (38:26).

  • v17 "Is there a word from the LORD?… You will be given into the hand of the king of Babylon" — the word of 32:4 and 34:3, will surely be captured and given into his hand, now asked for in secret.

  • v19 "Where are your prophets…?" — the prophets who said No disaster will come on you (23:17), and Hananiah, who promised the yoke of Babylon broken within two years (28:11).

  • v21 "until all the bread in the city was gone" — as it was at the end: the famine was severe in the city, and there was no bread for the people of the land (2 Kings 25:3). Ebed-melech says it of the city at 38:9.

speech.text: Jeremiah 37
Zedekiah son of Josiah, whom Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon made king in the land of Judah, reigned as king in place of Coniah son of Jehoiakim.
But neither he nor his servants nor the people of the land listened to the words of the LORD that He spoke through Jeremiah the prophet.
King Zedekiah sent Jehucal son of Shelemiah and Zephaniah son of Maaseiah, the priest, to Jeremiah the prophet, saying, "Please pray for us to the LORD our God."
Jeremiah was still coming and going among the people, for they had not yet put him in prison.
Pharaoh's army had come out of Egypt; and when the Chaldeans who were besieging Jerusalem heard the news of them, they withdrew from Jerusalem.
Then the word of the LORD came to Jeremiah the prophet, saying,

This is what the LORD, the God of Israel, says: This is what you shall say to the king of Judah, who sent you to Me to inquire of Me: Pharaoh's army, which came out to help you, is about to return to its own land, Egypt.
The Chaldeans will come back and fight against this city; they will take it and burn it with fire.
This is what the LORD says: Do not deceive yourselves, saying, "The Chaldeans will surely go away from us," for they will not go.

For even if you struck down the whole army of the Chaldeans who are fighting against you, and only men who had been run through were left among them, each in his tent, they would get up and burn this city with fire.
Arrested at the Benjamin Gate
And it came to pass, when the army of the Chaldeans had withdrawn from Jerusalem because of Pharaoh's army,
that Jeremiah went out of Jerusalem to go to the land of Benjamin, to take his share there among the people.
When he was at the Benjamin Gate, an officer in charge there, whose name was Irijah son of Shelemiah, son of Hananiah, seized Jeremiah the prophet, saying, "You are going over to the Chaldeans!"
Jeremiah said, "That is a lie! I am not going over to the Chaldeans." But he would not listen to him; Irijah seized Jeremiah and brought him to the princes.
The princes were angry with Jeremiah; they beat him and put him in confinement in the house of Jonathan the scribe, for they had made it the prison.
When Jeremiah had gone into the cistern house, into the vaults, he stayed there many days.

Then King Zedekiah sent for him and had him brought, and the king asked him secretly in his house, "Is there a word from the LORD?" Jeremiah said, "There is." Then he said, "You will be given into the hand of the king of Babylon."
Jeremiah also said to King Zedekiah, "What sin have I committed against you or your servants or this people, that you have put me in prison?
Where are your prophets who prophesied to you, saying, 'The king of Babylon will not come against you or against this land'?
So now, please listen, my lord the king: let my plea come before you, and do not send me back to the house of Jonathan the scribe, so that I do not die there."

Then King Zedekiah gave orders, and they committed Jeremiah to the court of the guard, and he was given a loaf of bread daily from the bakers' street, until all the bread in the city was gone. So Jeremiah stayed in the court of the guard.

chapters.title: The Cistern of Malchiah
chapters.html:
Jeremiah 38

1Shephatiah son of Mattan, Gedaliah son of Pashhur, Jucal son of Shelemiah and Pashhur son of Malchiah heard the words that Jeremiah was speaking to all the people:

2This is what the LORD says: Whoever stays in this city will die by the sword, by famine and by pestilence; but whoever goes out to the Chaldeans will live, and his life will be his as plunder, and he will live.

3This is what the LORD says: This city will surely be given into the hand of the army of the king of Babylon, and he will take it.

4Then the princes said to the king, "Let this man be put to death, for he is weakening the hands of the men of war who are left in this city, and the hands of all the people, by speaking such words to them. This man is not seeking peace for this people, but harm."

5King Zedekiah said, "He is in your hands, for the king can do nothing against you."

6So they took Jeremiah and threw him into the cistern of Malchiah the king's son, which was in the court of the guard, letting Jeremiah down with ropes. There was no water in the cistern, only mud, and Jeremiah sank in the mud.

7Ebed-melech the Cushite, a eunuch who was in the king's house, heard that they had put Jeremiah into the cistern, while the king was sitting in the Benjamin Gate.

8Ebed-melech went out from the king's house and spoke to the king, saying,

9"My lord the king, these men have done evil in all that they have done to Jeremiah the prophet, whom they have thrown into the cistern; he will die where he is because of the famine, for there is no more bread in the city."

10Then the king commanded Ebed-melech the Cushite, "Take thirty men from here with you, and bring Jeremiah the prophet up out of the cistern before he dies."

11So Ebed-melech took the men with him and went into the king's house, to a place under the treasury, and took from there worn-out rags and worn-out clothes, and let them down to Jeremiah in the cistern with ropes.

12Ebed-melech the Cushite said to Jeremiah, "Put these worn-out rags and clothes under your armpits, under the ropes." Jeremiah did so.

13Then they pulled Jeremiah up with the ropes and brought him up out of the cistern; and Jeremiah stayed in the court of the guard.

At the Third Entrance

14King Zedekiah sent and had Jeremiah the prophet brought to him at the third entrance of the house of the LORD. The king said to Jeremiah, "I am going to ask you something; hide nothing from me."

15Jeremiah said to Zedekiah, "If I tell you, will you not surely put me to death? If I give you advice, you will not listen to me."

16King Zedekiah swore secretly to Jeremiah, "As the LORD lives, who made this life for us, I will not put you to death or give you into the hand of these men who are seeking your life."

17Then Jeremiah said to Zedekiah, "This is what the LORD, the God of hosts, the God of Israel, says: If you will indeed go out to the princes of the king of Babylon, then your life will be spared, and this city will not be burned with fire, and you will live, you and your house.

18But if you do not go out to the princes of the king of Babylon, this city will be given into the hand of the Chaldeans, and they will burn it with fire, and you will not escape from their hand."

19King Zedekiah said to Jeremiah, "I am anxious about the Jews who have gone over to the Chaldeans, in case they give me into their hand and they abuse me."

20Jeremiah said, "They will not give you over. Obey, please, the voice of the LORD in what I am telling you, and it will go well with you, and your life will be spared.

21But if you refuse to go out, this is the word that the LORD has shown me:

22All the women who are left in the house of the king of Judah are being brought out to the princes of the king of Babylon, and they are saying:
'Your friends have misled you
and prevailed over you;
your feet are sunk in the mire;
they have turned back.'

23All your wives and your sons they will bring out to the Chaldeans, and you will not escape from their hand, but will be captured by the hand of the king of Babylon; and you will burn this city with fire."

24Then Zedekiah said to Jeremiah, "Let no one know of these words, and you will not die.

25If the princes hear that I have spoken with you, and they come to you and say to you, 'Tell us, please, what you said to the king; hide nothing from us, and we will not put you to death; and what did the king say to you?'

26then you shall say to them, 'I was bringing my plea before the king, that he would not send me back to Jonathan's house to die there.'"

27All the princes came to Jeremiah and asked him, and he told them all these words, as the king had commanded. So they said no more to him, for the conversation had not been overheard.

28So Jeremiah stayed in the court of the guard until the day Jerusalem was taken. And it came to pass, when Jerusalem was taken —

Notes

  • v1 "Jucal son of Shelemiah and Pashhur son of Malchiah" — Jucal is written Yehukhal at 37:3, where Zedekiah sent him to ask for prayer; Pashhur son of Malchiah was sent to inquire of the LORD before (21:1). Both now want the prophet dead (v4). The Greek has three names, without Pashhur son of Malchiah.

  • v4 "he is weakening the hands of the men of war… This man is not seeking peace for this people, but harm" — what his letter to the exiles had said, turned around: Seek the peace of the city (29:7), and the LORD's plans for peace and not for harm (29:11).

  • v6 "There was no water in the cistern, only mud" — bor, as when Joseph's brothers threw him into the pit. The pit was empty; there was no water in it (Genesis 37:24).

  • vv7–13 "Ebed-melech the Cushite, a eunuch who was in the king's house" — Ebed-melech means "servant of the king." The Greek calls him the Ethiopian, its word for the Cushite of 13:23. The king was sitting in the Benjamin Gate, where Jeremiah had been seized (37:13). The princes put the prophet into the mud, and a Cushite of the king's house brings him out; his reward is told at 39:15–18.

  • v9 "he will die where he is" — va-yamat, "and he died": the Hebrew tells it as good as done. In the Greek, Ebed-melech says to the king, You have done evil in what you have done, to kill this man.

  • vv17, 20 "your life will be spared… you will live, you and your house" — chayah, "live," the word of the choice set before the people, the way of life and the way of death (21:8), now set before the king.

  • v19 "they abuse me" — hit'allelu bi, Saul's fear on his last day: these uncircumcised will come and run me through and abuse me (1 Samuel 31:4). Zedekiah fears his own people who have gone over more than the Chaldeans.

  • vv22–23 "Your friends have misled you and prevailed over you; your feet are sunk in the mire… and you will burn this city with fire" — anshei shelomekha, "the men of your peace," and yakhol, "prevail," are the words of the prophet's complaint: All my friends watch for my fall… and we can prevail against him (20:10). Tava, "sink," is the verb of v6: the king who let Jeremiah sink in the mud of the cistern will be left with his own feet in the mire. The Hebrew lays the burning of the city on the king: tisrof, "you will burn." The Greek has this city will be burned.

  • vv25–27 "I was bringing my plea before the king… for the conversation had not been overheard" — the plea he had in fact made (37:20). The Greek ends v27 with for the word of the Lord had not been heard.

  • v28 "And it came to pass, when Jerusalem was taken —" — the sentence is finished at 39:3, after the dates of 39:1–2: all the princes of the king of Babylon came and sat in the Middle Gate. Ve-hayah tells what happened, as at 37:11. The Greek has only until the time when Jerusalem was taken.

chapters.title: Jerusalem Taken
chapters.html:
Jeremiah 39

1In the ninth year of Zedekiah king of Judah, in the tenth month, Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon and all his army came against Jerusalem and besieged it.

2In the eleventh year of Zedekiah, in the fourth month, on the ninth day of the month, the city was breached.

3Then all the princes of the king of Babylon came and sat in the Middle Gate: Nergal-sharezer, Samgar-nebo, Sarsechim the Rab-saris, Nergal-sharezer the Rab-mag, and all the rest of the princes of the king of Babylon.

4When Zedekiah king of Judah and all the men of war saw them, they fled and went out of the city by night, by the way of the king's garden, through the gate between the two walls; and he went out by the way of the Arabah.

5But the army of the Chaldeans pursued them and overtook Zedekiah in the plains of Jericho. They took him and brought him up to Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon at Riblah in the land of Hamath, and he passed sentence on him.

6The king of Babylon slaughtered the sons of Zedekiah at Riblah before his eyes; the king of Babylon also slaughtered all the nobles of Judah.

7He put out Zedekiah's eyes and bound him in bronze fetters to bring him to Babylon.

8The Chaldeans burned the king's house and the houses of the people with fire, and broke down the walls of Jerusalem.

9The rest of the people who were left in the city, the deserters who had gone over to him, and the rest of the people who were left, Nebuzaradan the chief of the slaughterers carried into exile to Babylon.

10But Nebuzaradan the chief of the slaughterers left in the land of Judah some of the poor people who had nothing, and gave them vineyards and fields on that day.

Jeremiah Set Free

11Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon gave orders concerning Jeremiah through Nebuzaradan the chief of the slaughterers, saying,

12"Take him and set your eyes on him; do him no harm, but do with him as he tells you."

13So Nebuzaradan the chief of the slaughterers sent, with Nebushazban the Rab-saris, Nergal-sharezer the Rab-mag and all the chief officers of the king of Babylon;

14they sent and took Jeremiah from the court of the guard and gave him to Gedaliah son of Ahikam, son of Shaphan, to take him home. So he stayed among the people.

A Word for Ebed-melech

15The word of the LORD had come to Jeremiah while he was shut up in the court of the guard, saying,

16Go and say to Ebed-melech the Cushite: This is what the LORD of hosts, the God of Israel, says: I am about to bring My words on this city for harm and not for good, and they will come to pass before you on that day.

17But I will deliver you on that day, declares the LORD, and you will not be given into the hand of the men you dread.

18For I will surely let you escape, and you will not fall by the sword; your life will be yours as plunder, because you have trusted in Me, declares the LORD.

Notes

  • vv1–2 "In the ninth year of Zedekiah… in the tenth month… in the eleventh year… on the ninth day of the month, the city was breached" — as Kings tells it, in the ninth year of his reign, in the tenth month, on the tenth day of the month… Then the city was breached (2 Kings 25:1–4). The Greek has only in the ninth month of Zedekiah in v1.

  • v3 "all the princes of the king of Babylon came and sat in the Middle Gate" — what the LORD had said at the call: each will set his throne at the entrance of the gates of Jerusalem (1:15). The Hebrew runs the names and titles together, and the division here is uncertain. Rab-saris, "chief eunuch," is a title, as in 2 Kings 18:17, and v13 gives it to Nebushazban; Rab-mag is another title. The Greek has other names.

  • vv4–13 — the Greek has nothing of these verses. It goes from the princes in the gate (v3) to Jeremiah taken from the court of the guard (v14).

  • vv4–7 "they fled… by the way of the king's garden… slaughtered the sons of Zedekiah at Riblah before his eyes… He put out Zedekiah's eyes" — told also in 2 Kings 25:4–7, in many of the same words. The king had been told your eyes will see the eyes of the king of Babylon (34:3); the last thing they saw was his sons' death.

  • v8 "the king's house and the houses of the people" — beit ha-am, "the house of the people," one house in the Hebrew. Kings names the temple first: He burned the house of the LORD, the king's house and all the houses of Jerusalem (2 Kings 25:9). This chapter does not name the house of the LORD.

  • v9 "Nebuzaradan the chief of the slaughterers… the deserters who had gone over to him" — rav tabbachim, his title in Kings (2 Kings 25:8), close to Potiphar's, chief of the slaughterers (Genesis 37:36). Ha-noflim, "the deserters," are those who did as Jeremiah had counselled (21:9; 38:2), the step he was accused of taking (37:13).

  • v10 "some of the poor people who had nothing… vineyards and fields" — Kings, with the same Hebrew letters for both words, has to be vinedressers and plowmen (2 Kings 25:12). The land passes to those who owned nothing, as the field at Anathoth had promised: Houses and fields and vineyards will again be bought in this land (32:15).

  • vv11–12 "set your eyes on him" — the words of the LORD's promise to the exiles, I will set My eyes on them for good (24:6), here in the king of Babylon's order.

  • v14 "Gedaliah son of Ahikam, son of Shaphan" — the son of the Ahikam whose hand kept Jeremiah from death under Jehoiakim (26:24). 40:1–6 tells the prophet's release another way, from among the captives at Ramah.

  • vv15–18 "while he was shut up in the court of the guard… the men you dread… I will surely let you escape… because you have trusted in Me" — the word is told after the fall, though it came while Jeremiah was still shut up (33:1). Into the hand of those you dread was said to Coniah (22:25), who was given into it; Ebed-melech will not be. Malat, "escape," is the word of the king's fate, you will not escape from their hand (38:18, 23). Your life will be yours as plunder is the promise of 21:9 and 38:2, and trusted the word of Blessed is the man who trusts in the LORD (17:7).

chapters.title: The Remnant under Gedaliah
chapters.html:
Jeremiah 40

1The word that came to Jeremiah from the LORD after Nebuzaradan the chief of the slaughterers had let him go from Ramah, when he had taken him bound in chains among all the exiles of Jerusalem and Judah who were being carried into exile to Babylon.

2The chief of the slaughterers took Jeremiah and said to him, "The LORD your God pronounced this disaster against this place.

3The LORD has brought it about and has done as He said, because you sinned against the LORD and did not obey His voice; so this thing has come upon you.

4But now, I have freed you today from the chains on your hands. If it seems good to you to come with me to Babylon, come, and I will set my eyes on you; but if it seems bad to you to come with me to Babylon, then stay. See, all the land is before you; wherever it seems good and right to you to go, go there."

5While Jeremiah had not yet turned to go, he said, "Go back to Gedaliah son of Ahikam, son of Shaphan, whom the king of Babylon has appointed over the cities of Judah, and stay with him among the people; or go wherever it seems right to you to go." Then the chief of the slaughterers gave him an allowance and a gift, and let him go.

6So Jeremiah went to Gedaliah son of Ahikam at Mizpah and stayed with him among the people who were left in the land.

Gedaliah at Mizpah

7When all the commanders of the forces who were in the open country, they and their men, heard that the king of Babylon had appointed Gedaliah son of Ahikam over the land, and had committed to him men, women and children, some of the poorest of the land who had not been carried into exile to Babylon,

8they came to Gedaliah at Mizpah: Ishmael son of Nethaniah, Johanan and Jonathan the sons of Kareah, Seraiah son of Tanhumeth, the sons of Ephai the Netophathite, and Jezaniah son of the Maacathite, they and their men.

9Gedaliah son of Ahikam, son of Shaphan, swore to them and to their men, saying, "Do not be afraid to serve the Chaldeans. Live in the land and serve the king of Babylon, and it will go well with you.

10As for me, I will stay at Mizpah to stand before the Chaldeans who come to us; but you, gather wine and summer fruit and oil, and put them in your jars, and live in your cities that you have taken."

11Likewise all the Jews who were in Moab, among the Ammonites, in Edom and in all the lands heard that the king of Babylon had left a remnant for Judah, and that he had appointed over them Gedaliah son of Ahikam, son of Shaphan.

12Then all the Jews returned from all the places to which they had been driven, and came to the land of Judah, to Gedaliah at Mizpah; and they gathered wine and summer fruit in great abundance.

13Johanan son of Kareah and all the commanders of the forces who were in the open country came to Gedaliah at Mizpah

14and said to him, "Do you know that Baalis king of the Ammonites has sent Ishmael son of Nethaniah to take your life?" But Gedaliah son of Ahikam did not believe them.

15Then Johanan son of Kareah spoke secretly to Gedaliah at Mizpah, saying, "Let me go, please, and strike down Ishmael son of Nethaniah, and no one will know. Why should he take your life, so that all the Jews who are gathered to you are scattered, and the remnant of Judah perishes?"

16But Gedaliah son of Ahikam said to Johanan son of Kareah, "Do not do this thing, for you are telling a lie about Ishmael."

Notes

  • vv1–6 "The word that came to Jeremiah from the LORD after Nebuzaradan… had let him go from Ramah" — the heading of a word from the LORD, but none follows in these verses, and the next word of the LORD to Jeremiah comes at 42:7. The release is told another way at 39:14, from the court of the guard straight to Gedaliah; here he is found in chains among the captives at Ramah, where Rachel weeps for her children (31:15).

  • vv2–3 "The LORD your God pronounced this disaster against this place… because you sinned against the LORD and did not obey His voice" — a Babylonian officer speaks the prophet's own message, in the words of the confession of 3:25, for we have sinned against the LORD our God… and we have not obeyed the voice of the LORD our God. You in v3 is plural: the people, not Jeremiah.

  • v4 "I will set my eyes on you… See, all the land is before you; wherever it seems good and right to you to go, go there" — the order of 39:12 kept. The words are Abram's to Lot, Is not all the land before you? (Genesis 13:9), and the foreign king Abimelech's to Abraham, Here is my land before you. Settle where it is good in your eyes (Genesis 20:15).

  • v5 "While Jeremiah had not yet turned to go, he said, 'Go back to Gedaliah'" — the Hebrew, ve-odennu lo yashuv, "and he still not turning back," is obscure, and has no he said; the English follows its sense. Yashuv, "turn back," and shuvah, "go back," are the same verb. The Greek has But if not, run off; go back to Gedaliah. Aruchah, "allowance," is the word for Jehoiachin's daily portion from the king of Babylon, For his allowance, a continual allowance was given him (2 Kings 25:30).

  • vv7–9 "the commanders of the forces… Do not be afraid to serve the Chaldeans. Live in the land and serve the king of Babylon, and it will go well with you" — Kings tells it more briefly (2 Kings 25:22–24), with Johanan son of Kareah and no Jonathan, Seraiah son of Tanhumeth the Netophathite and Jaazaniah son of the Maacathite, and Do not be afraid of the servants of the Chaldeans. The Greek also has no Jonathan, and the servants of the Chaldeans. Gedaliah gives the counsel of 27:17, Serve the king of Babylon, and live.

  • vv11–12 "all the Jews returned from all the places to which they had been driven" — a small return, in the words of the promise, I Myself will gather the remnant of My flock out of all the lands where I have driven them (23:3).

  • vv14–16 "Baalis king of the Ammonites has sent Ishmael son of Nethaniah to take your life… you are telling a lie about Ishmael" — sheqer, "lie," Jeremiah's answer to the guard who called him a deserter (37:14). Johanan's warning was true: Ishmael came with ten men, and they struck down Gedaliah, and he died (2 Kings 25:25).

speech.text: Jeremiah 40

The word that came to Jeremiah from the LORD after Nebuzaradan the chief of the slaughterers had let him go from Ramah, when he had taken him bound in chains among all the exiles of Jerusalem and Judah who were being carried into exile to Babylon.
The chief of the slaughterers took Jeremiah and said to him, "The LORD your God pronounced this disaster against this place.
The LORD has brought it about and has done as He said, because you sinned against the LORD and did not obey His voice; so this thing has come upon you.

But now, I have freed you today from the chains on your hands. If it seems good to you to come with me to Babylon, come, and I will set my eyes on you; but if it seems bad to you to come with me to Babylon, then stay. See, all the land is before you; wherever it seems good and right to you to go, go there."

While Jeremiah had not yet turned to go, he said, "Go back to Gedaliah son of Ahikam, son of Shaphan, whom the king of Babylon has appointed over the cities of Judah, and stay with him among the people; or go wherever it seems right to you to go." Then the chief of the slaughterers gave him an allowance and a gift, and let him go.
So Jeremiah went to Gedaliah son of Ahikam at Mizpah and stayed with him among the people who were left in the land.
